"Separated from the clan?" Wang Furen put on a look of shock and stared at the Old Matriarch.

"Grand Matriarch, this is such a significant matter — why did you not say a word of it to me?"

Not giving the Old Matriarch any room to collect herself, she then turned in feigned astonishment to Li Shi.

She asked with concern: "First Mistress — how did this come about so suddenly? Why would a perfectly good family separate from the clan?"

She was hoping Li Shi would read her look and tell her the reason.

That way she would have grounds to vent at the Second Branch — and relieve herself of some pent-up anger.

Li Shi, naturally, was not about to say a word.

She only smiled and gave a few vague answers.

After all, her husband and she had agreed: the Qin clan's consent to the separation came with a condition — that the shameful business of the Old Matriarch privately seizing her own first mother-in-law's dowry was not to be spread outside.

The First Branch kept their word.

Wang Furen was visibly disappointed.

But she quickly recovered.

Deliberately, she said to Li Shi: "I know what kind of a woman you are — you would never be in the wrong. Your First Branch cannot have erred! When people multiply, families divide; when trees flourish, branches grow. These things cannot always be helped."

She paused, then shifted: "Only — I wonder what the Qin clan was thinking. How could they agree?"

"By rights, First Master Qin has just been promoted... in any other family's clan, they would be clutching him close with both hands!"

Every word Wang Furen said made the Old Matriarch's face darker by a shade.

Wang Furen was all but pointing at her nose and saying: it is your Second Branch's fault. You bullied people so relentlessly that the moment they had any power, they couldn't wait to separate — and you couldn't even stop them.

Seeing the Old Matriarch's dead face producing not one syllable in response, what more did Wang Furen need to understand?

This was the Second Branch's fault entirely — they had driven the First Branch so hard that the First Branch chose to separate right before their daughter's wedding.

In-laws like this — she no longer merely disliked them. She was afraid of them.

"Oh, my dear First Mistress — isn't it our Wang family's luck to keep running into these things..."

Wang Furen lifted her handkerchief and dabbed at her eyes. "I don't even know how to say this — when did the Second Master Qin get the idea? I had clearly set my heart on your Sixth Young Miss, and in the end it was changed to Fifth Young Miss..."

Li Shi was genuinely startled.

How had this Wang Furen come out and said even that?

She was famously proper and strict about etiquette — was she not?

Yet here she was, with the wedding already arranged and the day after tomorrow set to welcome the bride — still coming here to say this!

If she could say it, she might be able to — but Li Shi could not listen to it.

If the Wang family had truly valued her Ruyin, how could they have so readily agreed to the Second Branch's swap?

And after the swap, this Wang Furen had never shown the slightest guilt when she met with her.

They had traded pleasantries — nothing more. No real feeling.

Why bring this up now? There was nothing to be gained by it — except to damage Ruyin's reputation.

The Old Matriarch at this point had been goaded into coughing uncontrollably, her face going a frightening deep red from the strain.

"Wang Furen — the fates of children are all destined. We as parents all want the best for our children. What's past is past — let's not speak of it anymore!" Li Shi's expression had turned cool.

Wang Furen heard these words and felt the flush of having overstepped.

She also knew that Li Shi had already been generous to her in saving her face.

She had come originally wanting to make a scene and get some of her frustration out — and by now her thoughts had shifted toward breaking off the engagement.

Only she hadn't yet had time to discuss the matter with her husband, so she dared not say it outright.

But now the Old Matriarch, once she recovered her breath, was having none of it any longer. After being jabbed at so thoroughly, she wasn't made of a turtle's patience.

She had been a formidable figure in her own right once, in those powder-and-rouge days of her youth...

If not for the sake of her grandchildren, why would she have put up with Wang Furen — a woman a generation younger — like this?

"Wang Furen — it was your Second Son who was heard declaring publicly, in front of many scholars over wine, that he would take no one but our Fifth Young Miss. And now you come to my house to find fault with Fifth Young Miss. What sense does that make?"

"They all say the Wang family's learning has been passed down for generations, that propriety and etiquette are paramount. I wonder — whose propriety, whose etiquette is Wang Furen observing?"

Wang Furen gave a cold laugh. "Since Madam Qin has said it — this junior will say only this: a fly cannot alight on an uncracked egg."

"Madam Qin would do better to ask your own Fifth Young Miss whether she has done anything improper behind closed doors!"

Li Shi's eyes went wide for a moment — even she failed to manage her expression in time.

This Wang Furen was truly willing to go all the way.

To counter the Old Matriarch, she had thrown even her own son under the cart.

Her son was the fly — which made Fifth Young Miss the cracked egg...

Absolutely priceless drama.

And she had not quite forgiven the Wang family for agreeing to that swap so readily either!

Might as well throw a little more kindling on the fire.

Li Shi pressed her lips together, looked at Wang Furen and said: "Wang Furen — Fifth Young Miss has long been praised for her exceptional talent. She is, after all, known as the family's most accomplished daughter."

"Your Second Son quietly admiring her from afar is no surprise. Only he should not have said it out loud in public!"

These words seemed to defend Fifth Young Miss — but Wang Furen heard them and fired back immediately:

"Since ancient times, women's greatest virtue has been found not in talent but in virtue! If Fifth Young Miss were truly a good woman, she should never have flaunted her learning and let others spread the news of it!"

Then she said: "I've seen First Mistress's three young ladies — all beautiful and brilliant on the inside. And have we ever heard anyone spreading word of them outside? Your family's newly adopted Fourth and Fifth Young Miss are clever and quick too — who is better than whom? Is the Fifth Young Miss of this house so exceptional?"

The Old Matriarch's heart and liver were nearly crumpling into a ball from fury, and she couldn't help but burst out: "This old woman never knew Wang Furen thought so little of my Fifth Young Miss! If that is the case, why did your Wang family ever come to propose the match in the first place?"

Her words, once said, were better left unsaid — because Wang Furen seized on them like a snake snatching a stick.

"What a thing to say, Madam Qin! I wasn't proposing to the Fifth Young Miss in the first place!"

"And if you mean what you're implying — that you are thoroughly dissatisfied with this engagement — then isn't that perfectly convenient? While the bride hasn't yet been welcomed, let us both be clear about it. Let's call the whole engagement off!"

chapters.title: Dogs Fighting Dogs, Fur Flying Everywhere
chapters.content:
Her words were both sharp and urgent — anyone who heard them could tell she was chomping at the bit to dissolve the engagement.

Old Madam Qin was so consumed by fury that her eyes rolled back and she nearly fainted dead away.

It was Lady Li who moved first. In a single stride she rushed forward, one hand bracing Old Madam Qin's back, the other pressing with all her might against the philtrum point beneath her nose.

She turned to Wang Furen, whose face had gone pale, and called out: "Wang Furen, you've gone too far with those words. If Qin Taifu Ren should really come to harm because of this, it won't reflect well on you when word gets around!"

Wang Furen knew perfectly well that Lady Li was right. The moment she saw Old Madam Qin's eyes roll back and her body begin to crumple, regret seized her instantly.

If word spread that she had driven her in-laws' Grand Dame into a faint, the consequences were too dreadful to imagine... At present, the two families were still connected — regardless of whether the engagement was truly dissolved.

"I..." Wang Furen didn't know what to say.

Lady Li paid her no mind and bore down with both hands on Old Madam Qin's philtrum point.

Inwardly she gave a cold snort. She was not being kind.

The Wang family was no better than the Qin Second Branch — let them get tangled up together. That would at least spare some poor girl from being harmed by them!

Wu Momo, who had been standing guard over Old Madam Qin, froze in place when she saw her mistress faint, too rattled to think straight.

When she finally came to her senses and moved to call for help, Lady Li snapped at her: "You old fool! Is this something to be making a fuss about? Get over here and help press the Taifu Ren's philtrum point!"

Wu Momo jolted as though struck. She knew the First Madam was right.

She thought: Even if the First Branch has split from the clan, there's still only one surname Qin written with one stroke — the First Madam is still thinking of the whole Qin family's dignity...

So when Lady Li said she had run out of strength and needed Wu Momo to take over pressing the philtrum point, Wu Momo hurried forward to help.

Lady Li frowned and said, "This is a matter of saving a life! Are you going to watch the Old Madam die by not putting in any effort?"

Wu Momo was so frightened she gave a start and pressed down harder.

She had spent years doing physical work — naturally her strength far exceeded Lady Li's...

Old Madam Qin was shocked awake by sheer pain.

When she came groggily to her senses, her philtrum was already mottled red and purple.

Seeing that it was Wu Momo who had stopped pressing, she said nothing.

Lady Li called out: "The Taifu Ren has finally come around!"

Wang Furen felt her face grow hot — after all, the old woman had fainted because of her words.

She had no choice but to step forward and offer a few words of concern.

Old Madam Qin recalled that just before she had blacked out, this woman had spoken of dissolving the engagement. Her aged eyes brimmed with fury.

But then she thought of what her Fifth Granddaughter had told her about the dreams regarding the Wang family, and she forced it all down.

"Many thanks for Wang Furen's concern. It's my own body that is no longer up to the task — I'm fine now."

Lady Li glanced sidelong at the old woman, surprised. She can hold that back too?

Is Qin Fifth Miss so unmarriageable that Wang the Second is her only option?

Wang Furen felt the great stone on her heart finally drop away.

At this moment she was even somewhat regretting that her mouth had been too quick.

Something as serious as dissolving an engagement could not be blurted out carelessly — once the words were spoken... even if the families remained in-laws afterward, there would always be a crack.

Yet her pride would not let her be the first to back down.

Old Madam Qin, for her part, feared the woman might truly be set on withdrawing the engagement before the wedding, and was already regretting that she had not held her own tongue...

"Wang Furen, I was addled with illness earlier — I don't remember a word I said... Treat it as though you never heard it, and don't hold it against a doddering old woman like me." Old Madam Qin forced a smile and looked at Wang Furen.

Seeing her concede first, Wang Furen relaxed again.

This time she had learned her lesson, and her reply was considerably more gracious.

Lady Li, seeing the two of them moving toward a truce, realized there was nothing more entertaining to watch and took her leave.

Old Madam Qin was only too happy to see her go, and at once said: "Since your First Branch is in a hurry to move, I won't keep you — off you go then."

Lady Li gave a cold inward snort.

"We can hardly afford not to move — the West Courtyard of the Qin compound is simply too cramped! My Yin Niang's trousseau can't even be laid out properly — we can't have people laughing at us."

Wang Furen pressed her lips together, nearly bursting into laughter.

Lady Li was truly a marvel.

In a battle of wits and words, she was no match for Lady Li at all.

Look how she had infuriated Old Madam Qin — and yet there was nothing the old woman could say.

Deeply satisfying!

After Lady Li departed, Wang Furen also wanted to rush back and discuss things with her husband...

But Old Madam Qin wanted to keep her, hoping to get her assurance that this marriage would proceed without incident.

Wang Furen, however, was unwilling to make any such promise.

She simply said she had things to attend to and took her leave.

Old Madam Qin, hearing she was going back to see to her affairs, felt a measure of relief.

Going back to attend to affairs — what affairs could those be?

The only matter of real importance in the Wang household just now was Wang the Second taking a new bride. She was going back to see to that, naturally.

Thinking it over, and wanting to keep the Wang family from causing any trouble, she clasped Wang Furen's hand and said: "Wang Furen, of all my many granddaughters, I love Fifth Niang the most!

"Let me also give you a frank account today — the spending-money I have set aside in Qin Fifth Niang's trousseau chest amounts to ten thousand taels.

"I have already told her: since Mian Er holds her dear, she is to use whatever I have given her for Mian Er's needs."

Old Madam Qin's heart was bleeding inwardly — she had originally been willing to give Qin Fifth Niang five thousand taels at the very most...

But in order to hold this match with the Wang family together, she had been forced to double it. A hemorrhage indeed!

Wang Furen's heart stirred at these words.

Heavens! This Old Madam Qin was a true miser of a fortune-keeper — sending off a legitimate granddaughter with ten thousand taels of spending money in her trousseau alone!

She understood inwardly that Old Madam Qin was telling her, in so many words, that marrying Qin Fifth Niang would not be a loss...

She wavered inside, but her mouth spoke pleasantly.

"How can the Qin Taifu Ren say such a thing? Our Wang family would never touch a daughter-in-law's dowry — I've said as much before!"

Wang Furen's high-minded words inadvertently stabbed Old Madam Qin right in the spine.

The old woman's face fell again.

Wang Furen herself felt vaguely bewildered — the Wang family was saying they would not touch the daughter-in-law's dowry, which was surely good news for the girl's family. Why was the old woman still so displeased?

"Qin Taifu Ren, please do rest and recover — I won't disturb you further. I'll be on my way." Wang Furen gave a bow and took her leave.

......

After Lady Li returned to the West Courtyard, she recounted everything that had happened in Shouhé Hall to her family.

"My goodness! How delightful! Tsk, tsk... you have no idea..." Lady Li covered her chest and laughed with abandon.

Lin Xi pressed her lips together, smiling. "The Wang family is no innocent party either — not a decent one among them!"

Meng An, whose personality was more spirited, said with great satisfaction: "Wonderful! Let them be dogs tearing at each other — fur flying everywhere!"

......

Before long, Qin Rong Cheng sent word that all the trunks and boxes had been loaded onto the carriages.

The ladies were invited to board the carriages and make their way to the new residence.

Before the evening meal, the Qin First Branch had completed their move.

The new residence had spacious courtyards and many rooms.

The First Elder of the Qin family and his wife took the East Courtyard.

Qin Rong Cheng and Qin Rong Lie and their respective wives chose the North Courtyard.

They left the South Courtyard — the finest one — for the Qin family's unmarried young ladies.

Qin Ru Yin, Fourth Niang, and Fifth Niang tried to decline, but Lin Xi and Meng An held all three of them in place.

"This is not just for you — Ru Jin and Ru Xiu's rooms are arranged in the South Courtyard too! Once all three of you have married, you'll be our most honoured young aunts — what's wrong with staying in the South Courtyard?"

Lin Xi finished speaking and smiled warmly at the three younger sisters-in-law.

Lady Li added from the side: "Your father and I are still here, and when we are eventually gone, the East Courtyard will belong to the brothers. You young ladies are treasured guests in your own family home — you only have these dozen or so years of ease in your parents' house. Your brothers and sisters-in-law want to pamper you, so you just accept it. Besides, your father and I won't shortchange them — so no more refusing, any of you!"

Seeing their mother speak, Qin Ru Yin and the others stopped resisting.

They thanked their sisters-in-law, then went off to settle their own belongings and arrange their staff.

The servants who attended the masters of the Qin First Branch were all capable, well-disciplined people.

By the time the evening meal was served, they had already finished tidying each master's boxes and belongings.

The following morning, Qin Ru Yin had just risen and begun to wash and dress when Lady Li sent someone to summon her to the East Courtyard.

"Third Young Miss, the Madam asks you to hurry with your washing and dressing — Madam Jiang from the Jiang family is here at the house!"

"Ah?" Qin Ru Yin was taken aback.

chapters.title: Jiang Women Come to Warm the New House; the Third Sister-in-Law is No Easy Character
chapters.content:
The First Elder of the Qin family had announced at the previous evening's dinner that from that day forward, the children of the household would be given new birth-order titles. The servants were to address their masters by the new order accordingly.

"The Jiang Taifu Ren is here?" Qin Ru Yin was still fuzzy-headed.

She was marrying into the Jiang family tomorrow — surely Jiang Taifu Ren must be in the thick of preparations right now?

"Yes, Third Young Miss — and it's not only Jiang Taifu Ren. The Jiang Second Madam, Third Madam, and several Senior Madams from the collateral branches have all come too."

Qin Ru Yin was surprised. "Such a grand showing... for what purpose?"

"Third Young Miss, don't worry — this is a happy occasion! The Jiang Taifu Ren has brought the ladies of the household to present a house-warming gift!"

Qin Ru Yin breathed a sigh of relief. "Oh! I see..."

Feng Mama, standing to the side, said with a smile: "Then Miss should quickly have a few bites of cake — it'll be difficult to have a proper breakfast with distinguished guests about."

Qin Ru Yin nodded. Her future mother-in-law had come in such force to bring house-warming gifts — she certainly could not spare much thought for breakfast.

She blamed herself for having been too excited the night before, what with the clan split finally settled and the move to the new house complete, and because Seventh Niang and Eighth Niang had come to chat with her, she had gone to bed very late.

She hastily made do with a few bites of cake, rinsed her mouth, and brought Feng Mama and Jú Hóng with her to the East Courtyard.

Jiang Taifu Ren was chatting warmly with Lady Li. When she saw Qin Ru Yin come in, the smile on her face deepened even further.

This girl looked even healthier than the last time she had seen her — her rosy cheeks were lovelier than peach blossoms.

Dressed in a lotus-pink brocade cape, wearing a set of pale-violet crystal hair ornaments, she carried herself with even more grace than before.

Thinking that the day after tomorrow this girl would be married into her family and become the Fourth Son's bride, Jiang Taifu Ren found that the corners of her mouth simply refused to be pressed down.

After Qin Ru Yin had paid her respects to the Jiang elders and exchanged greetings with the ladies of her own generation, Jiang Taifu Ren warmly pulled her down to sit beside her.

She then delighted in showing off the girl to the collateral Senior Madams who had come with her.

Those Senior Madams, seeing how much Jiang Taifu Ren adored this future fourth daughter-in-law, naturally had no intention of spoiling her pleasure.

The words of praise came tumbling out as if they cost nothing.

They also busied themselves pressing greeting gifts into Qin Ru Yin's hands.

The Jiang Second Madam and Third Madam each smiled and took a slow look at Qin Ru Yin from head to toe, then exchanged a quiet, understated glance.

Whatever else one might say, this Qin Sixth — no, Qin Third Niang — had a face that was truly in a class of her own among all the daughters-in-law of the Qin family!

No wonder the Old Madam valued this Qin Third Niang so highly and was so fond of her.

As for the Fourth Son — he was a man who never gave any woman a second glance... whatever was wrong with him was anyone's guess!

It seemed the Old Madam was simply hoping that a beauty like this, once she became the Fourth Son's wife, might draw that one's detached and unworldly heart back down to earth.

Truthfully speaking, the Old Madam made such a show of favouring this girl — and they were daughters-in-law themselves — so naturally a flicker of jealousy stirred within them.

But they were guests in someone else's home, so of course they could not let it show.

Not only could they not show it — they had to wait until the elders finished their praises and then rush to add their own.

Once they had praised her, they also had to present greeting gifts, since they were after all her sisters-in-law.

Lady Li was already very pleased with the Jiang family's evident regard for her Yin Niang.

Now, seeing that they had only just split from the clan and moved into the new house, yet Jiang Taifu Ren had come straight away with the household ladies to bring a house-warming gift — she was overjoyed beyond all expectation.

She had not dared to even hope for this before!

After all, the Jiang family was far busier receiving a new bride than the Qin family was sending one off.

Even so, in the midst of such hectic preparations, Jiang Taifu Ren had brought the Senior Madams from the collateral branches, along with her Second and Third daughters-in-law, to warm the Qin family's new home.

They were also the very first relatives to come to the new house.

Of course, the Wei family — her own maternal relatives — had also sent a card first thing in the morning, and would be coming to warm the house today.

But the Wei family was large and needed time to prepare — they would arrive later, in time for the midday meal.

After Qin Ru Yin greeted the distinguished guests, she could see that the elders still had much to say among themselves, so she excused herself and, with Lady Li's nod, withdrew to her own courtyard.

"Please don't take offence, Qin Furen — my First Daughter-in-Law had also intended to come, but she manages the household accounts... so I did not have her accompany me today." Jiang Taifu Ren said to Lady Li with a cheerful smile, raising her teacup.

Before Lady Li could reply, the Jiang Third Madam spoke up: "Qin Furen may not know — with our Fourth Brother bringing home a bride, no one in our household is busier than my eldest sister-in-law."

Jiang Taifu Ren's brow gave a faint, cool tightening, and she glanced at the Third Madam with quiet restraint.

The Third Madam behaved as if she hadn't noticed, her smile perfectly unchanged.

Lady Li raised her brows in surprise, then graciously expressed her thanks toward the absent First Madam and offered her a few words of praise.

Jiang Taifu Ren was very satisfied that Lady Li had taken the gracious route and preserved the Jiang family's dignity.

She said, smiling: "My First Daughter-in-Law is a capable woman. That I can be a carefree matriarch without a care in the world is entirely thanks to her hard work running the household."

Lady Li understood that Jiang Taifu Ren was deliberately elevating the First Daughter-in-Law, Lady Fang, to put the Third Daughter-in-Law — who had just interjected with what seemed to be a provocative remark — in her place.

Of course, there was likely also an element of testing the Qin family's intentions.

After all, with so many sons in the Jiang family, the most accomplished was the Fourth, Jiang Jiuhao.

It would not be an exaggeration to say the Jiang family rested entirely on Jiang Jiuhao's shoulders.

Jiang Taifu Ren also worried that the Qin family might be dissatisfied with not getting control of the household for the Fourth Branch.

Lady Li turned the thought over several times, then smiled and congratulated Jiang Taifu Ren on her good fortune, once again praising the First Daughter-in-Law, Lady Fang, effusively.

When she had finished, she sighed and said: "Come to think of it, it's not only the Jiang Taifu Ren who has good fortune — with such a capable and generous sister-in-law, my Yin Niang is also immensely blessed!

"What I hope is that when my Yin Niang marries into your household, the First Daughter-in-Law of the Jiang family will simply treat her as a beloved little sister."

The meaning in Lady Li's words was clear to every Jiang lady present.

Lady Li was signalling that the Qin family had no intention of letting Qin Ru Yin compete for power or authority within the Jiang household...

Jiang Taifu Ren's smile deepened considerably, and she was more satisfied than she could say.

She was thoroughly pleased with this match — with the Qin First Branch as in-laws.

And at the same moment, she felt profoundly grateful — how fortunate it was that the Fourth Son had agreed to the exchange of brides at the time!

Events had proven that the Fourth Son's eye was razor-sharp.

If there had been no exchange of brides, they would still be getting the Qin Second Branch...

Never mind. Never mind!

Ill-omened thought!

The Jiang Third Madam, upon hearing Lady Li's words, allowed a flicker of shadow to cross her eyes.

The Second Madam lowered her gaze, her thoughts unreadable.

The collateral Senior Madams of the Jiang family had no particular feelings about it one way or the other — it had nothing to do with their branch of the family. Their own sons and grandchildren were not especially distinguished, and they all depended on the Jiang main branch to get by.

And the Jiang main branch depended on the Fourth Son.

The Fourth Son was also most filial — for any major matter in the Jiang family, he did not go to his brothers, but to Jiang Taifu Ren, his mother, to discuss it.

So these old collateral-branch aunts-in-law naturally stood firmly on Jiang Taifu Ren's side.

......

After another quarter-hour of pleasantries, Jiang Taifu Ren glanced out the window at the sky, then said to Lady Li: "It is getting on in the morning, and our household is a little busy just now — I won't take up more of your time. We'll take our leave!"

Lady Li could not persuade her to stay. She had no choice but to prepare generous parting gifts and personally escort Jiang Taifu Ren and her party of ladies to the Qin family's front gate.

As the Jiang family's carriages pulled away, Lin Xi, who was supporting Lady Li's arm, said with worried eyes: "Mother, it seems Yin Niang's Third Sister-in-Law is going to be no easy character!"

Meng An nodded repeatedly — she had seen it too.

Lady Li gave a sound of dismissal and looked at her two daughters-in-law. "That's not all — I'd say Yin Niang's Second Sister-in-Law is even less easy to deal with."

"Then..." Lin Xi grew more worried. "I can see that Jiang Taifu Ren protects the First Madam of the Jiang household quite staunchly...

"We've also heard that the Jiang First Madam, though capable, comes from a less distinguished background — which inevitably makes one feel slighted. I fear she may see Yin Niang as a threat to her authority over the household and make things difficult for her at every turn!"

chapters.title: Is the Sun Rising in the West?
chapters.content:
Lady Li reassured her First Daughter-in-Law: "Don't worry — our Yin Niang has grown up, and she's no longer the kind of person that just anyone can bully."

Meng An also told her elder sister-in-law: "Sister, I actually think Jiang Taifu Ren likes our Yin Niang best of all!"

Eyes never lie.

"What worries me are those sisters-in-law of hers — I've heard that while the Jiang ladies don't dare fight openly among themselves, they do plenty of scheming in the shadows..." Meng An said.

Lady Li picked up the thread.

"All of you, stop worrying! The entire Jiang family lives off Jiang the Fourth — Jiang Taifu Ren knows this perfectly well.

"It took so much for the Fourth Son to finally agree to take a wife. As long as Yin Niang follows Jiang the Fourth and lives well, Jiang Taifu Ren will only ever pamper our Yin Niang!

"Whoever tries to make trouble for our Yin Niang will have Jiang Taifu Ren herself to deal with. And besides, she still has all of us from her own family standing behind her..."

After Lady Li had reassured her two daughters-in-law, she led them to the back courtyard.

The Wei family was confirmed to be arriving for the midday meal today.

She also wanted to keep the Wei family in the house for several days — staying at an inn was simply too inconvenient.

All of this needed to be arranged in advance.

When they reached the back courtyard, the Wei family had not yet arrived — but the birth mother of Fourth Niang Ru Yan and Fifth Niang Ru He, the former Concubine Lu, had come to call.

One could no longer call her Concubine Lu — she was to be addressed as Madam Lu now.

At the time, Madam Lu had wished Third Master Qin to give her a letter of manumission, and the First Elder of the Qin family had personally gone to Third Master Qin to discuss it and persuade him.

Though Third Master Qin was reluctant to let her go, he nonetheless chose to respect Madam Lu's wishes and wrote her the letter of manumission, along with settling a fairly generous dowry upon her.

The First Elder further suggested to Third Master Qin that since Madam Lu had no blood relatives of her own in the capital — only distant cousins — it would be best to let her remain in the city.

Madam Lu was also skilled at making noodles and dumplings, so the First Elder suggested that Third Master Qin buy her a small shop where she could open a noodle stall and make her own living.

Third Master Qin agreed at once and immediately handed over the money for a servant to go and arrange it.

At the time, when Zhou Shi heard the news, she had flown into a terrible suppressed rage and wanted to go make a scene with Third Master Qin, but her two sons held her back.

Her eldest son, Qin Rong Guang, had even said to her: "Mother, please stop making trouble — let us just live peacefully!

"Madam Lu is after all the birth mother of both our younger sisters. They may not have been born of you, but they are still my and Rong Feng's sisters..."

Her second son, Qin Rong Feng, had also said: "Our sisters are still our sisters... Even for our sake and Elder Brother's sake, you should not have pushed Madam Lu too hard!"

Hearing even her own sons speak this way, Zhou Shi thought about it and decided that more fussing was pointless, so she let it go.

As for Third Master Qin — he still refused to speak to her, and ever since their row that day, he had not set foot in her room again.

Madam Lu was now a free woman. She had registered as an independent female householder and was mistress of her own affairs.

Though her little noodle stall had only been open a few days, her skill was excellent and she used generous, quality ingredients — business was booming.

Today, she had overheard customers chatting and learned that the Qin family had split from the clan and moved to a new house. She immediately asked after the Qin First Branch's new address, found out it was on Zǐ Jǐng Lane, and at once offered her apologies to the customers, left the noodle stall in the hands of two helper aunties, and came to bring a house-warming gift.

Lady Li received her personally and specially had someone fetch the Ru Yan and Ru He sisters as well.

When mother and daughters were reunited, all three of them had tears brimming in their eyes — though every one of those tears was joyful.

Seeing that the sisters addressed Madam Lu as "Madam Lu," Lady Li waved her hand decisively.

"Though the two of you call me Mother, Madam Lu is your birth mother — to tell her apart, it is only right that you should call Madam Lu your 'Mama.'"

Madam Lu had been keeping her composure up until this point, but when she heard these warm-hearted words from Lady Li, her eyes turned red all at once.

Unable to stop herself, she rose from her seat, knelt on the floor, and knocked her head against it again and again, with solid, resonant thumps.

Ru Yan and Ru He, seeing this, immediately knelt before Lady Li as well. (TL: I think this the the first time the author has given, Madam Lu's daughters names.)

Lady Li was so flustered she stood up in a rush — but there was no avoiding it.

She quickly directed those around her: "Quickly, quickly! Help Madam Lu and the two young ladies up!"

Then to Madam Lu she said: "What... what is all this for? There's no need for this!"

Madam Lu said: "The First Elder of the Qin family and the First Madam have not only been like second parents to Fourth Young Miss and Fifth Young Miss — they have been no less than second parents to me as well!"

She then turned to the sisters Ru Yan and Ru He and admonished them to be certain to honour and serve their parents well in the future.

The sisters Ru Yan and Ru He promised without hesitation.

Without their Mama needing to say a word, they had every intention of honouring their father and mother, living in harmony with their brothers and sisters, and caring for all their nieces and nephews.

Madam Lu did not stay too long before she made to leave, but Lady Li urged her to remain.

Her eyes bright, and with a hint of embarrassment, she said to Lady Li: "Thanks entirely to the First Elder of the Qin family and the Second Elder's support in helping me buy the shop and set up the noodle stall.

"...Business is quite good — there have been quite a few returning customers these past days. And it's nearly midmorning already — I ought to head back soon to start preparing for the midday rush."

Since she put it that way, Lady Li was happy for her — business came first, and one could hardly keep someone else's livelihood waiting.

She thanked Madam Lu for coming to warm the house, and they arranged that once Qin Ru Yin had married, the Qin family would hold a proper housewarming banquet and would send an invitation for her to attend.

Madam Lu agreed delightedly.

Lady Li had the sisters Ru Yan and Ru He see Madam Lu out — she thought it only fitting to let the mother and daughters share a few private words along the way.

Past mid-morning, the Wei family arrived by carriage.

Since many of the Wei family's younger generation were visiting for the first time, the Qin family had arranged for firecrackers to be set off in welcome...

The welcome was thorough and resounding.

The esteem shown to the Wei family came through in a way every one of them felt, and each felt genuinely welcomed.

Having made the long journey to the capital and arrived at this splendid outcome, they felt it had been well worth the trip.

The First Elder had also arranged privately with the Wei family's Grand Uncle to encourage talented members of the Wei clan to come and establish themselves in the capital going forward, now that there was someone here for them to rely on.

The Grand Uncle of the Wei family was naturally delighted to agree.

It was something the Wei family had long hoped for.

The elder Wei men in particular — having lived through the grief of what had happened to the First Elder's late wife — placed tremendous importance on the clan's younger men pursuing the examination path.

And the younger generation within the Wei clan, having witnessed the heartbreak of their kinswoman's marriage into the capital only for the Wei family to be powerless against her in-laws' bullying, had driven all the scholarly-minded ones to throw themselves into their studies.

After all, they had sisters of their own to protect...

The Qin Third Branch was still at the old Qin compound.

Third Master Qin had at the time firmly resolved to follow the First Elder wherever he went.

As a son born of a concubine with neither particular personal distinction nor notably promising children, the Qin clan had no reason to oppose his following the First Elder in the clan split.

Second Master Qin, overwhelmed by his own troubles at the time, had no energy to concern himself with whether Third Master Qin was splitting from the clan with the First Elder. And from his point of view, since First Master Qin had already slipped beyond his control, there was no great reason to forcibly hold Third Master Qin in the family either — it even saved him the cost of keeping Third Master Qin's whole household.

Third Master Qin had in fact quietly purchased a small residence for his family without telling anyone.

At that moment, Zhou Shi was pacing restlessly back and forth in her room.

Her eldest son Rong Guang had come with second son Rong Feng to tell her they were going to help warm their uncle's new house.

The two brothers knew their mother was in a quarrel with their aunt — they certainly did not expect her to be willing to come along.

After Zhou Shi heard the reason for their visit, she immediately seized her eldest son's arm. "You're all going — why didn't you tell your mother? I'll come too!"

"You... you want to come?" Qin Rong Guang was somewhat startled.

"How could I not?" Zhou Shi's face flushed with embarrassment. "Our family and your uncle's family are all one house now — we've all split from the clan together. We're going to be depending on your uncle's family from here on!"

These words made the brothers Rong Guang and Rong Feng uneasy.

"Mother! Please never say anything like that again! We have hands and feet — why on earth would we need to depend on Uncle's family?" Qin Rong Guang frowned, his expression displeased.

He might not amount to much — he was no scholar and had not the stomach for the hardships of military training.

But he had his hands and feet. Even opening a shop and doing business could feed a family, couldn't it?

Madam Lu was a woman on her own — she had left without anything, and already she was supporting herself by her own efforts. What reason did a grown man like him have to say he couldn't do it?

Qin Rong Feng added: "Elder Brother is right. And Father is actually very capable — even Uncle said this time's promotion was in no small part due to Father's contributions.

"As long as Father is willing to teach me and Elder Brother properly, we can surely make something of ourselves!"

Zhou Shi stared wide-eyed.

Were these really the same two sons of hers who only ever came to her for money?

For them to say something like this... Even if they were still just talking a good game, it was enough to bring tears to her eyes at this moment!

It seemed... it had been right to follow the First Branch and split from the clan!

"Children! You're not just saying this to fool your mother, are you? Are you truly willing to turn over a new leaf?" Zhou Shi gazed at her two sons imploringly.

The brothers Qin Rong Guang and Qin Rong Feng both turned red in the face at the memory of who they had been.

In the past, they had been utter rascals!

But their father had never disciplined them, and all their mother had taught them was how to take advantage of others and how to flatter the Second Branch...

They had been ashamed of themselves too!

So they had drifted into the habits of idle young wastrels — drifting through one day at a time.

But then their uncle had brought them out of the clan in the split, and their father had talked to them for most of last night... and for the first time, they had seen hope.

And once a person has hope, how could they bear to go back to the aimless days they had lived before?

The two of them, however poor they might be, at least had their father standing behind them.

And their uncle was a kind and generous man — he had not only formally adopted the two concubine-born sisters as legitimate daughters, but had also told their father that he would not give up on the two nephews either...

What did they have to fear?

"Mother, my brother and I have always wanted to do better for ourselves! But back then with the Second Branch pressing down on us, how could we dare? Even Uncle's two sons could only take the path of military service — and my brother and I aren't cut from that cloth, and certainly aren't scholars... so we went astray."

Zhou Shi suddenly broke into loud, ugly sobs.

The brothers Qin Rong Guang and Qin Rong Feng rushed to help her into a chair.

"If both of you truly have this in your hearts, then... then your mother cannot be the one holding you back... wuu, wuu, wuu..."

Before her sons could even comfort her, she abruptly sat upright and wiped her face with her sleeve in one rough swipe.

Then she looked at her sons and said: "The two of you, wait for your mother — let me go find a few good things. We're going to bring your uncle's family a proper house-warming gift!"

The two sons: "..."

Is the sun rising in the west today?

chapters.title: The Third Branch's Transformation
chapters.content:
Their mother, Zhou Shi — in former days, she had been extraordinarily tight-fisted.

Never mind bringing good things to their uncle's family as house-warming gifts — even her own sons, her very flesh and blood, had never managed to pry anything worthwhile from their mother's hands...

"Oh, and — your Sixth... no, your Third Sister is getting married tomorrow. The gift I prepared for her trousseau was rather thin. Now that our two families are as close as brothers can be, we ought to give your Third Sister a more generous addition to her trousseau."

Qin Rong Guang shot his brother a look of startled disbelief.

To his amazement, his brother's expression was even more alarmed than his own.

"And, and — bring something nice for your Fourth Sister and Fifth Sister as well. Even if they are now the First Branch's daughters, they are still blood siblings to you two!"

Zhou Shi kept rattling on as she briskly called her old nursemaid to fetch the key and open the storeroom.

The two sons: ...

Is this really their mother? Have they been looking at the wrong person? Has she been possessed by something?

Yet Zhou Shi was perfectly clear-headed at this moment.

She knew she was selfish!

But she was also a mother who loved her children more than her own life.

Previously, Lady Li had scolded her for being miserly even over her sons' betrothal gifts — but hadn't that been because she could see her two sons were so useless, all they did was spend money?

She had thought that since the two of them were such a hopeless lot, and their branch was concubine-born and good for nothing, what prospects could they have of marrying anyone of standing?

And if they couldn't marry anyone of standing, what was the point of preparing a lavish betrothal gift — just throwing money away?

But now everything was different!

The more Zhou Shi thought about it, the more she felt that only good days lay ahead.

Perhaps she might even dare to hope that her two sons would one day achieve enough to let her become a prosperous and pampered matriarch, too!

Even if her sons didn't amount to much, she could ask her sister-in-law to arrange good matches for them — if she couldn't count on her sons, perhaps her grandsons...

The more Zhou Shi thought, the more excited she grew, until she found herself laughing out loud.

This so alarmed her sons that they genuinely wondered if she had been possessed by something — Qin Rong Cheng exchanged a look with Qin Rong Feng, signalling him to go and fetch their father...

While he himself tested the waters and asked: "Mother, you never used to be like this... Are you trusting that Uncle and Aunt will take care of our family?"

Zhou Shi glared at him. "I know — plenty of people in the compound whispered behind my back that your mother was a fool! But even a fool still has eyes that work, haven't I?

"...I don't trust your great-uncle and great-aunt — am I supposed to trust that Feng Shi and Tong Shi instead? Or your Second Uncle and those three vipers?"

Qin Rong Guang, hearing his mother put it that way, could not help but let out a silly laugh.

......

Third Master Qin listened carefully to what his second son had told him, and knitted his brow in thoughtful contemplation.

He had not expected Zhou Shi to change her mind so quickly.

But this was a good thing, of course.

After considering it, he followed his second son to Zhou Shi's courtyard.

He would go see for himself — if Zhou Shi was genuinely turning over a new leaf, then for the sake of his two sons, he ought to give her a way to step down gracefully.

When Third Master Qin arrived at Zhou Shi's courtyard and saw that she had truly unlocked the storeroom and was picking out many fine things he had never even seen before, he knew the answer.

The finest things among them must have been the best items from Zhou Shi's own dowry — along with things she had quietly purchased with her own savings over the years.

She was willing to bring these out...

"My lord?"

Zhou Shi had still been directing maids and servants to arrange the house-warming gifts for the First Branch, the new trousseau additions for Qin Ru Yin, and the gifts for Qin Ru Yan and Qin Ru He in separate piles.

When she saw the maids and servants suddenly freeze and not dare breathe, she looked back in surprise — and found her husband had come. Her eyes went red immediately.

Third Master Qin acknowledged her and said he had heard everything from Rong Feng.

Zhou Shi's grievance poured out, and through her tears she said: "My lord... yes! I was tight-fisted before! But I had no choice — the way our family was, someone had to be saving up a foundation for us, didn't they?"

Third Master Qin, seeing her cry with such wounded feeling, was deeply moved — and felt deeply guilty as well.

Heedless of the presence of their sons and servants, he stepped forward and took his wife's hands in his. "It was not your fault. It was mine."

Zhou Shi shook her head repeatedly. "No! It was not your fault, my lord! It was the Second Branch's fault! It was that scheming old witch Feng Shi's fault..."

"My lord, can you forgive me?" She clutched his hands tightly.

"Elder Sister-in-Law said — as long as I listen to you in the future, you would be willing to continue as my husband... I promise I will listen to you in everything from now on!"

Zhou Shi was crying so hard the makeup on her face ran in streaks.

The two sons: ...

They felt their mother was being an absolute simpleton...

Time to make themselves scarce! Scarce!

"I have put you and the children through hardships these many years. And also..."

"Also Madam Lu!" Zhou Shi said it for him, and added with guilt: "I have wronged her, too — those years I competed with her for your affections and did many things to harm her...

"Now that she has asked for the letter of manumission and left, I realise I was truly no match for her. She is a good woman — she has always known, from the very beginning, what she wanted.

"Seeing that she is well now, I am happy for her. It is only that I think she never wishes to see me again.

"I cannot face her either... so I can only think to make it up to Ru Yan and Ru He..."

Third Master Qin sighed.

For Zhou Shi, a woman of her nature, to be able to speak these words — she was truly different from before.

Zhou Shi thought about it and then said to Third Master Qin: "If you still wish Ru Yan and Ru He to come home, I agree.

"Though I have also been thinking — Ru Yan and Ru He will have far better marriage prospects following Elder Brother and Elder Sister-in-Law. So perhaps..."

"You are right. Ru Yan and Ru He have found their good fortune — let them follow their elder uncle and aunt. But I will say this first: their dowries are my responsibility to prepare!"

Hearing him say this, Zhou Shi showed not the slightest displeasure, and nodded in agreement: "That goes without saying — you are their father, of course you should prepare for them. And I have also been preparing on my side, though..."

She was a little embarrassed — what she had previously prepared was genuinely too paltry to present.

Third Master Qin was already very satisfied.

He told her: "Just prepare whatever you feel comfortable with — what you need to focus on is setting aside more for our two sons' betrothal gifts. The rest is on me."

"I will do whatever you say, my lord! What I had before was... it really was too little. I didn't think they had any hope of marrying into good families..."

Third Master Qin said: "It's not impossible for them to marry well — it all depends on them. Both of them are still young — one is barely past twenty, the other barely seventeen. There is no rush."

"Mm!" Zhou Shi nodded heartily, her eyes shining. "I'm not rushing either — I'm just counting on my two sons to have a change of heart and truly make something of themselves!"

"You won't need to worry about that — Elder Brother has already spoken to me about it, and he wants them to put in serious effort these next two years and try to pass the clerk's examination."

Zhou Shi's eyes lit up, then worry came rushing back. "But... will Rong Guang and Rong Feng agree?"

Third Master Qin nodded. "I talked to them for most of last night — they're both willing."

"Amitabha Buddha! Bless them, bless them, the ancestors bless them!" Zhou Shi rattled off her prayers in a jumble of excitement.

Third Master Qin watched with amusement but did not interrupt her nonsensical chanting and flailing about.

"All right — once everything is packed up, let's go and deliver the house-warming gift to Elder Brother and Sister-in-Law." Third Master Qin said, and Zhou Shi nodded emphatically.

"Oh, and my lord — Yin Niang is getting married tomorrow. Surely our family won't go home tonight? We should stay at Elder Brother's house to help!"

Seeing she had even thought of this, Third Master Qin felt truly comforted, and told her: "Your willingness is the best thing of all."

Zhou Shi immediately said: "Of course I'm willing — as long as Sister-in-Law doesn't find me too much trouble!"

She was now also willing to follow Third Master Qin in calling the First Branch couple Elder Brother and Elder Sister-in-Law.

One thought suddenly struck her, filling her with resentment again.

"My lord, shouldn't we move out soon as well? That old witch Feng Shi is still sick in bed and won't settle down — she sent an old crone over here first thing this morning to sneer and mock and push us out.

"We don't have a house yet, so we could rent a small place to make do for now. After Yin Niang's wedding, I'll take money and go buy ourselves a small house to live in."

Third Master Qin heard this and smiled. "Then after we deliver the house-warming gift to Elder Brother today, we can come back and pack for the move."

Zhou Shi was stunned. "My lord?"

"Before Elder Brother bought his house, he spoke to me... and with his connections, I also managed to buy a small house for our family.

"Let me say first — it really is small. Only three courtyards, since my funds are somewhat limited..."

"My lord! Having a house at all is wonderful! Three courtyards is not small! We are in the capital — finding a three-courtyard residence is already remarkable. I'm not particular!"

Zhou Shi's voice rose several notches, her face alight with excitement.

Heavens above!

Who would have imagined she'd live to see a day like this — not even in her dreams!

"My lord, tell me how much you spent, and I'll make it up to you! Don't refuse — I only just found out from the children that you have actually been quietly doing great things all these years... Going out into the world, you need money too."

Third Master Qin sighed inwardly, but his smile deepened as he held her hands. "Keep your money for yourself and the children. I'm a grown man — I can hardly be spending your money."

"My lord, now you're treating me like a stranger!" Zhou Shi would not hear of it.

Third Master Qin, seeing her insist, conceded at last: "Then set aside some money for Madam Lu — call it compensation from you."

Zhou Shi's face went red at once, and she murmured: "I'm afraid she won't..."

"Don't worry — she understands things more clearly than either of us. If she won't accept the money as compensation, then give it to Ru Yan and Ru He as spending money for their trousseau chests."

In truth, Third Master Qin had already privately given Madam Lu one thousand taels of silver as compensation — in addition to the small shop he had bought for her.

He was not a wealthy man and could only manage one thousand taels for now, intending to compensate her further when his circumstances improved.

But Madam Lu was a woman of firm dignity — after accepting the thousand taels, she had made clear that they were now fully quits, and there was no need for him to give her anything more.

"Then I'll choose a day and go to see Madam Lu myself." Zhou Shi thought it over and said.

Third Master Qin nodded.

This was a matter between his wife and Madam Lu — it was not his place to interfere.

With the Third Branch couple having untied the knot between them, the Second Branch's side of things flared up again.

Old Madam Qin had taken to her sickbed, so Qin Ming Jie had invited the Fourth Branch's wife, Madam Yin, to preside over Qin Ru Yue's wedding ceremonies.

Qin Ru Yue, of course, was not about to accept this quietly.

She wrote a long letter and had it sent to her maternal grandmother.

Her grandmother had known nothing of what her daughter, Tong Shi, had gone through in the Qin household — and when she learned of it, she was so furious she nearly stopped breathing.

Once she had calmed down, she immediately summoned all her sons and daughters-in-law and drove in high dudgeon straight to the Qin compound.

Old Madam Qin was no longer in any condition to receive visitors.

Qin Ming Jie was left to steel himself and receive his enraged in-laws personally.

chapters.title: Qin Fifth Niang Has Finally Gotten to Prince An
chapters.content:
Before Qin Ming Jie could even bow and offer greetings to Tong's Old Grandmother, she pointed a finger at his face and sobbed out a torrent of curses calling him a heartless wretch.

The Tong family had been an eminent clan for hundreds of years, and Tong's Old Grandmother was herself of very distinguished birth.

Qin Ming Jie had never imagined that this high-born mother-in-law of his — once the pride of all well-bred young ladies — would come at him the moment she arrived and berate him to his face without ceremony.

And the Tong family had come in considerable force.

Not a scrap of dignity had been spared for him.

His face darkened immediately, and his acknowledgements of the Tong uncles and others were perfunctory at best.

Tong's Old Grandmother had finished venting and now demanded to see her granddaughter Qin Ru Yue.

Qin Ming Jie had no choice but to send someone to summon Qin Ru Yue.

The moment Qin Ru Yue arrived, Tong's Old Grandmother seized her and wept over her — lamenting her bitter fate: getting married the next day with her mother still locked away in the countryside.

Qin Ru Yue understood inwardly that her grandmother and the Tong party had come to stand up for her mother — not for her.

If they were truly here for her sake, the Tong family would have come long before this, not waited until she had been forced to send that letter herself.

Of course, the Tong family was also standing up for her mother because they had no wish to see that Rui Niang benefiting from the situation.

If that Rui Niang were to have a son in the future, her good father would surely shower affection on the child as well — which would harm her brothers' interests.

The Tong family could disregard her, but they had interests bound up with those brothers of hers.

Qin Ming Jie was making significant gestures from the side, silently urging Qin Ru Yue to quickly find a way to soothe Tong's Old Grandmother.

Qin Ru Yue gave a cold inward laugh — but outwardly she looked gentle and obedient as she said to her grandmother: "Grandmother, please don't grieve. My mother's luck has been poor — she was caught up in trouble because of the matter of that Seventh Sister who left through the clan split.

"My grandmother and my father have spoken of it before — they only wanted my mother to retreat to the countryside for a time...

"It may be that with so many things happening in our family of late, and with Grandmother's health declining, Father has been so overwhelmed that he simply forgot to send someone to bring Mother back to the house."

She needed to use her maternal grandmother's family to bring her mother back home — but she could not afford to offend her own father.

Her paternal family, after all, as long as their interests remained intertwined, would be sure to stand up for her.

Her maternal grandmother's brow furrowed slightly upon hearing her granddaughter speak this way.

Qin Ru Yue's heart lurched — she hurriedly let her gaze fly toward her father with an expression of fear.

Tong's Old Grandmother and Qin Ru Yue's several uncles and aunts-by-marriage all saw it, and they came to understand why she had spoken as she had.

Tong's Grand Uncle wore a cold expression as he regarded Qin Ming Jie. "Brother-in-Law, since Yue Niang has put it this way, our Tong family — out of consideration for her being married tomorrow — will not press the matter with you.

"Brother-in-Law, send someone at once — bring my sister home today! It is only proper that a daughter's mother preside over her own wedding ceremony!"

"Quite! Having an aunt by marriage preside — what kind of arrangement is that?" Tong's Second Aunt-by-Marriage suddenly cut in.

Qin Ming Jie's gaze hardened, and he shot Qin Ru Yue a dark, sinister look.

He had discussed this matter with Old Madam Qin the night before and only reached a decision then.

He had only told the Fourth Branch couple and Qin Ru Yue.

The Fourth Branch couple could not possibly have spoken to the Tong family about it...

Qin Ru Yue was so terrified by that venomous look from her father that her heart nearly stopped — her mind raced frantically for a countermeasure.

She also silently cursed that Second Aunt who had let it slip.

Though Qin Ming Jie suspected his daughter, this was not the moment to make a scene.

He understood: the Tong family still cared about their own dignity. Having allowed the elder of the family — his old mother-in-law — to curse him out thoroughly, they now simply wanted him to capitulate and bring Tong Shi back.

In truth, Old Madam Qin had also pushed herself out of her sickbed the night before to urge him to bring Tong Shi back quickly to manage affairs.

But he was now treating that Rui Niang as though she were his life itself, and she had only recently become pregnant — barely over a month along.

If Tong Shi returned at this juncture, with her methods, that Rui Niang would be no match for her.

The child in Rui Niang's belly would likely not survive Tong Shi's machinations either — and naturally he could not bear that!

He had made his concern clear to Old Madam Qin, and for the sake of the grandchild Rui Niang carried — the child of the son's favourite woman — Old Madam Qin had capitulated.

After all, Qin Ru Yue was just a granddaughter.

Even if she was legitimate-born, that grandchild in Rui Niang's belly had been conceived by the son's most cherished woman!

With his mother agreeing, Qin Ming Jie had naturally not wanted to bring Tong Shi back.

But he had not expected the Tong family, who had said nothing upon learning why Tong Shi was sent to the countryside, to come storming through his door in such force this time.

After the rupture of Lady Sun's marriage and the cold shoulder the Crown Prince's side had given his eldest son, his footing was growing ever more precarious.

He certainly could not afford to fall out with the Tong family right now.

"Grand Brother-in-Law is absolutely right. It had been Ming Jie's intention all along to bring Yue Niang's mother back to preside over her wedding — I was only just sitting here thinking of it...

"It seems your party arrived, Grand Mother-in-Law, before I had a chance to act."

Qin Ming Jie's words sounded fine, but not a single member of the Tong family believed them.

It was nothing more than two families playing a game — and Qin Ming Jie had lost.

......

Zǐ Jǐng Lane.

The Qin Residence.

Third Master Qin, Qin Ming Sheng, brought his whole family with generous gifts to warm his elder brother's new house.

As they arrived, they found the street in front of the Qin Residence already lined with many carriages.

Word had reached well-connected official and noble households that the Jiang family had come early in the morning with generous gifts to warm the Qin First Branch's new home — and so various households had sprung into action.

The Ministry of Works colleagues of the First Elder in particular — led by the Minister of Works himself — had all come to the Qin residence to bring house-warming gifts.

The Minister of Works was in fine spirits about the whole matter.

Because of the First Elder's remarkable achievements while holding a lowly fifth-rank sinecure post, the Emperor had praised him and both his deputies at some length.

The First Elder was also a man who got things done — and the Minister of Works very much liked that.

He was the head of the Ministry of Works, and when he showed esteem for the First Elder, the others naturally had to follow their superior's lead...

Zhou Shi, seeing how the Qin First Branch had suddenly become so sought-after and influential in the capital, was filled with envy.

She tugged at Third Master Qin's sleeve and murmured: "Heavens... Elder Brother has truly become formidable! Just look at all this grandeur..."

Third Master Qin was genuinely happy for his elder brother as well, the smile in his eyes warm. "This is what Elder Brother deserves!"

The women of the inner household naturally knew nothing of the details.

All those years his elder brother had been quietly investing his energy in painstaking work — all of it to arrive at this day!

And even so, it owed something to the future Qin son-in-law, Commissioner Jiang.

Without Commissioner Jiang giving him a hand — what reason would the retired Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, that old gentleman, have had to present before the Emperor's desk all the unrecognised achievements Elder Brother had accumulated over the years, right before his retirement?

The First Elder of the Qin family was very glad to see Third Master Qin's whole family arrive.

With so many guests in the house, he had already drafted even the Wei family cousin-brothers to help him receive visitors.

When Third Master Qin and his two nephews came over, he quickly pressed them into service receiving guests as well.

Qin Rong Guang and Qin Rong Feng, though they were commoners, were the sons of their host's own family — it was perfectly appropriate for them to receive the young gentlemen who had come with their elders.

Zhou Shi watched her two sons, though nervous, muster up their courage and go to help their uncle receive guests, and felt her eyes go hot with emotion.

She herself was leading her maids and servants carrying the gifts to the back courtyard.

Lady Li, seeing her come, was only happy — she had not the slightest expectation of her bringing anything generous.

But when she saw the scale of what Zhou Shi had brought, she was taken aback.

Zhou Shi pulled her aside and offered her an earnest and wholehearted apology...

Lady Li was magnanimous as well. Seeing Zhou Shi acknowledging her wrongs and willing to change, she comforted her: "Our two families are true flesh and blood — what grudge can last past the next morning?

"Say no more of it — today I am dying of busyness; the best help you can give me is to join in receiving the guests!"

Zhou Shi nodded emphatically and agreed with great cheer.

The Wang Residence.

Wang Furen, returning from the Qin compound, got into a blazing row with the Master.

She wanted to dissolve the engagement — the Master was furious and demanded to know whether she wanted to destroy the Wang family's hundred-year reputation.

Wang Furen shot back that it was his insistence on having everything that had destroyed the Wang family's hundred-year reputation.

The husband and wife raged at each other and at last simmered down.

As for the engagement with the Qin family, the Master had come to regret it himself by now.

But calling off an engagement on the very eve of the wedding was indefensible by any measure.

And they had no grounds — no evidence of any misdeed on Qin Fifth Niang's part.

He absolutely could not do something that would so shame the Wang family's name.

Wang Furen said to him in a fury: "Your wanting everything all at once is going to destroy our Mian Er in the end!"

The Master, upon hearing this, immediately called out: "Fine! Let's bring Mian Er here — let Mian Er speak for himself!"

And so Wang Huai Mian was summoned by a servant from Wang Furen's courtyard.

When he heard the cause of his parents' dispute, he frowned and looked at Wang Furen: "Mother, Father is right. Tomorrow is the wedding — going to the Qin family today to call it off is entirely unreasonable on our part."

"Besides, the Qin family's troubles all arose from specific causes — what does any of that have to do with Qin Fifth Niang, a woman of the inner household? She is a good girl!"

Ever since he had investigated through multiple channels and confirmed that the Qin Sixth Niang of the First Branch had nothing remarkable about her origins, he had lost interest in her.

So what if her father had recently been promoted? So what if her father's maternal family had come to the capital to help them preside over the clan split?

The very fact that they had needed the Wei family to come manage the clan split showed that their family was still weak.

The Qin Second Branch was still more than capable of keeping the First Branch firmly in check.

It was just that the Qin Second Branch hadn't bothered.

As for Qin Fifth Niang — not to mention her stunning looks, she had also privately written him a letter full of tender feeling. That foolish girl was willing to tell him anything.

She had even told him beforehand that she was bringing twenty thousand taels of spending money in her trousseau chest...

And had made clear it was for him to use.

He might not care to use it himself, but his children certainly could.

His mother also prided herself on coming from a family of scholars — which sounded well enough, but left her children in threadbare poverty...

He never wanted his own sons to endure the same kind of pinched, meagre life he had lived!

The Qin First Branch had what, exactly?

The Qin Sixth Niang had even needed the Qin Second Branch to supplement her dowry — what kind of family was that!

Wang Huai Mian was, after all, only a scholar — not well-connected enough to catch all the news. And with his wedding the next day he was frantically busy, and no one had thought to pass on to him what had nothing to do with him.

Had he known that the Qin First Branch had just moved the whole family into a spacious house on Zǐ Jǐng Lane the day before, he would certainly not still be thinking of the First Branch as poor and shabby.

"Mian Er? Is that what you truly mean?" Wang Furen was silent a long while, and when she looked at her son again her eyes were full of disappointment.

Wang Huai Mian frowned. "Mother, of course I mean it! And our Wang family's hundred-year reputation cannot be destroyed by my hands!"

The Master was very gratified that his son cared so much for the family's honour — though he had some misgivings as well.

He could only hope that after his son married Qin Fifth Niang, the Qin Second Branch would not cause any more trouble!

Wang Furen drew a slow, deep breath and looked with grave seriousness at the second son she was most proud of. "Mian Er, let Mother ask you one more time — you truly will not regret this?"

As long as her son said he wanted to dissolve the engagement, she would throw her dignity aside and beg the Qin Second Branch to agree to breaking it off.

"I certainly will not regret it!" Wang Huai Mian said without hesitation.

He had one more secret: Qin Fifth Niang was no ordinary girl — she could have prophetic dreams.

This secret he would tell no one!

Just the night before, he had dispatched someone to pass a message from Qin Fifth Niang to Prince An's side. In less than half a month, most likely, his father's position would see a promotion.

And besides — he did want to see what kind of grand affair Jiang the Fourth and Qin Sixth Niang would make of their wedding...

chapters.title: Today She Is Getting Married
chapters.content:
The midday meal at the Qin residence on Zǐ Jǐng Lane was a lively affair.

Fortunately, both of the Qin sons' wives were capable women.

Even when yet more guests arrived after the earlier wave, they managed to prepare a feast that left nothing to be criticized.

After the midday meal, the Jiang family sent someone to the Qin family with news.

That very morning, Jiang Jiuhao had received his official promotion document.

Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

Second rank, first grade.

The highest post in the Ministry of Personnel.

After the previous Minister, Elder Cheng, had retired, the position had sat vacant for several days.

But as far as the court was concerned, the answer had been clear for some time.

Elder Cheng had long admired Jiang Jiuhao.

And in his later years, it was Jiang Jiuhao who had been running the Ministry's main affairs.

The document simply hadn't come down yet — and until it did, there was always a chance of a surprise.

After all, it was not unheard of for the Emperor to issue an edict personally appointing someone to head one of the Six Ministries.

The court had been watching and waiting.

Now the other shoe had finally dropped.

The Qin household was overjoyed without exception.

A future son-in-law receiving a promotion the day before the wedding — what a delightful and unexpected piece of good fortune!

In the eyes of those who believed in fate, this meant the bride, Qin Ru Yin, was born under a prosperous star — a star that brought good fortune and blessings to her husband.

The Wei family was equally happy for Qin Ru Yin.

The guests who had come to warm the house had also brought trousseau gifts for Qin Ru Yin.

Upon hearing the good news from the Jiang family, they all felt as though they had shared in the celebration, and their joy was mingled with envy.

Other households that had been sitting on the fence, upon learning that Jiang Jiuhao's promotion document had officially come through, all sent their stewards hurrying to the Qin residence with house-warming gifts — along with trousseau additions for Qin Ru Yin.

As a general rule, gifts were to be presented in the first half of the morning.

Now that it was well past the midday meal, each of these latecoming households found their own excuse.

Lady Li had no particular wish to accept gifts from those who only came to flatter the powerful — every single one of them was sizing things up before committing.

But the Wei family's Grand Elder Aunt persuaded her.

"Accept all of them. Never mind what those households are thinking — accepting the gift makes no enemies. As for the return of favours, surely you won't have trouble finding opportunities?"

Lady Li knew this was sound reasoning.

Her husband had only just been promoted to fourth rank, and he worked in the gruelling Ministry of Works — she could not afford to make enemies.

As the common saying went: the king of hell may be easy to deal with — it's his imps that are hard to manage.

Fortunately, the Wei family had come in large numbers, with many young women and brides-in-law among them.

Lady Li enlisted their help, and the recording of gifts and arranging of presents was carried out with perfect order.

The most pressing matter for the Qin family at this point was sorting out Qin Ru Yin's trousseau.

When they had moved, Qin Ru Yin's trousseau alone had taken up most of the West Courtyard.

And today had brought in yet more trousseau additions — all of which were placed in the West Courtyard as well.

At the Qin residence on Shun Yi Lane.

Tong Shi had only just returned home when she heard the news of Jiang Jiuhao's appointment as Minister of Personnel.

The Tong family, staying at the Qin compound for Qin Ru Yue's wedding the next day, had not yet departed.

So when Tong Shi returned through the main gate, Qin Ru Yue herself had come with her people to welcome her mother at the gate.

"My child! What fortune has deserted you so completely?"

Tong Shi had grown considerably thinner. But seeing her daughter looking equally haggard, she felt a pang in her heart.

"Jiang the Fourth has received his appointment as Minister of Personnel on the very eve of his wedding...

"That makes him the youngest Minister of Personnel in the entire history of our Great Ying dynasty!"

Originally, this man was supposed to have been her own son-in-law! The husband of her Yue Niang!...

How had every stroke of good luck landed squarely on that Qin Sixth Niang of the First Branch?

It was clearly meant to be her Fifth Niang's good fortune — that Qin Sixth Niang must have stolen it from her Fifth Niang...

Qin Ru Yue burned with hatred deep inside!

She had already been reborn into this life with foreknowledge and had secretly laid plenty of schemes — so why did one piece of good luck after another keep falling into Qin Ru Yin's lap?

Could it truly be that she was unable to change her own tragic and pitiable fate from her previous life?

No!

In this life she absolutely would not end up as tragic and pitiable as she had before!

Prince An's side must surely have already set things in motion!

She would wait.

She would wait and watch Qin Ru Yin make a fool of herself.

Watch her — a woman who should have been a Minister of Personnel's wife — ultimately sink to become a mere concubine in Prince An's household.

A concubine was nothing but a slave.

......

After the evening meal, the Qin residence on Zǐ Jǐng Lane received yet another distinguished guest.

The eminent monk Huì Qīng came with his fellow disciple, the abbess Huì Yuán, to offer blessings to the Qin family — primarily for Qin Ru Yin, who was about to be married.

The reason given was that the methods for repairing and dredging waterways that the First Elder of the Qin family had devised had saved the lives of countless common people...

And so on the occasion of his daughter's wedding, he had come to offer her his blessings.

As for Huì Yuán — she was the most gifted reader of faces among them all.

Having heard that the Wei family had brought many young ladies to see Qin Ru Yin off at her wedding, she divined that one among them had a karmic connection with her.

And so she had come along with her elder fellow-disciple Huì Qīng.

Hearing this, the First Elder of the Qin family at once ordered an incense altar to be set up.

Huì Qīng first blessed the Qin household as a whole, then offered a separate blessing for Qin Ru Yin specifically.

Huì Yuán, meanwhile, read the faces of the young ladies in Lady Li's flower hall.

In the end, she selected one of the Wei family's young ladies to be her lay disciple.

She only needed to observe a vegetarian diet on the first and fifteenth of each month and spend an hour reciting Buddhist scriptures in the shrine room on those two days.

The Wei Grand Elder Aunt was filled with joy — it was her very own little granddaughter, Wei Zi Yi.

The name of Abbess Huì Yuán was known to every family of any standing in the entire Great Ying dynasty.

To have a karmic connection with her, and even to be taken on as her lay disciple — what an honour that was!

A lay disciple only had her name recorded — she was free to marry as she wished.

Now that Wei Zi Yi had become Abbess Huì Yuán's lay disciple, far from affecting her marriage prospects, it would actually enhance them.

Word would likely reach the noble households of the capital before the next day was out — any family with a son of suitable age would be scrambling to send a matchmaker.

Wei Zi Yi herself was delighted as well — she was a clever girl and understood perfectly well what this meant.

She said privately to her grandmother that this was all thanks to her Sister Yin Niang's reflected glory...

After reading the faces of the Wei family's young ladies, Abbess Huì Yuán also mentioned that she had a half-teacher's karmic tie with the Qin Fourth Young Miss.

As it was already growing late, Lady Li invited both masters to stay the night.

Both declined graciously.

Abbess Huì Yuán thought for a moment and expressed her wish to say a few words to the Qin Fourth Young Miss.

Feng Mama, who attended Qin Ru Yin, whispered a few words into her ear.

Qin Ru Yin then had Feng Mama hurry to attend to Qin Ru Yan and tell her not to be afraid — just to speak truthfully.

Feng Mama was inwardly full of admiration for her young mistress's quickness and cleverness, and went to Qin Ru Yan's side and murmured to her softly.

......

Huì Qīng and Huì Yuán spent about an hour at the Qin residence before departing, the fellow disciples going to an inn together.

Jiang Jiuhao was already at the inn waiting for them.

Because Qin Ru Yin's wedding was the next day, the whole Qin household went to bed late.

Qin Ru Jin and Qin Ru Xiu did not go to their own arranged rooms that night — both of them crowded into Qin Ru Yin's room instead.

The three sisters talked for a long while, until at last the eldest, Ru Jin, fell quiet.

Qin Ru Yin considered a moment and then said: "Elder Sister, these past few days you've been home you've only been sharing good news — but I can see something is still not quite right with you."

Qin Ru Jin looked up at her little sister and gave a small shake of her head. "You're overthinking it, Yin Niang — tomorrow is your happy day; you shouldn't be worrying about anyone else..."

Qin Ru Xiu suddenly looked at Qin Ru Yin and asked: "Yin Niang — I nearly forgot to ask — still no sign of your monthly visiting?"

"Which?" Qin Ru Yin was baffled for a moment.

Qin Ru Xiu, seeing her staring back like a goose with its head full of straw, nearly burst out laughing. "What else? That thing — the one that comes every month!"

Qin Ru Yin let out an "oh."

So that was what she was asking about.

She gave a grin and shook her head without a care: "Not the slightest hint of it coming..." She added a moment later: "Which is all for the better!"

Qin Ru Xiu felt almost provoked into laughter by her. "And you don't mind? Ru Yan is younger than you and has already had it for over a year!"

Qin Ru Yin spread her hands. "I can't make it come if it doesn't want to!"

Inwardly she was actually pleased — later it came, the less suffering for her.

This was not the era she had once lived in, and the sanitary products here were genuinely too dreadful to endure...
