But a fire was already going in one brazier, and the whole thing had been done with practiced ease.

chapters.title: Afraid to Answer Me?
chapters.content:
Song Zhang entered with a chill clinging to him.

He walked quickly, his frame long and upright, but he slowed his step when he caught sight of the figure behind the screen. With a gesture of his hand, he dismissed the person following behind.

Colonel Wang, who had been in the middle of reporting something at Song Zhang's back, swallowed the words back and withdrew obediently outside.

Song Zhang stepped around the screen and walked in to find Shen Weici just rising to her feet. She was slender and willowy, her dark hair gleaming softly under the lamplight.

Shen Weici looked up at the sudden appearance of Song Zhang and was momentarily taken aback.

She collected herself and turned to him: "The charcoal fires have all been lit."

Song Zhang said nothing. He looked steadily at Shen Weici's face.

On that smooth cheek there was a small smudge of black — faint in color, but vivid against the extraordinary whiteness of her skin. It had probably gotten there when she was pushing her hair back.

He looked at her again — soft and jade-like where she stood, her gaze still carrying the same composure she had shown when exchanging couplets with Shen Zhaohao.

His eyes swept down to the charcoal braziers on the floor. They had been lit and were now arranged neatly in the corners of the room. The entire space had grown warm.

Shen Weici noticed Song Zhang was watching her without saying a word. Though she didn't understand his intention, she had done what she was asked to do, and meant to take her leave.

But as she made to pass by him, her wrist was suddenly caught in his grip. She looked up at Song Zhang in confusion, and found him looking back down at her: "You lit all of them yourself?"

Shen Weici met his eyes calmly: "If Young Lord Song doubts it, feel free to ask the maidservant."

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici evenly, then raised the hand he was holding up to his eye level. Her small, fair palm had a faint dusting of charcoal grey on it.

The silver-thread charcoal he burned was coated in a white layer — touching it briefly wouldn't leave much black. Unless one had handled quite a bit of it.

He let her hand go, but couldn't resist one last barb: "Shen Third Miss handles things like this with such familiarity."

Shen Weici looked at Song Zhang with an undisturbed expression: "Surely Young Lord Song already knew — I am not a cosseted young mistress who grew up in a Marquis's household. Doing these things is not difficult."

Song Zhang paused, and studied Shen Weici for a moment more. The scent of her drifted over again, and those full red lips were right before him — he almost couldn't hold himself back from leaning toward her.

Song Zhang couldn't understand why, with Shen Weici alone, he couldn't suppress that impulse. Perhaps it was because he had never seen anyone who was both so fragile and so seemingly unbreakable. Or perhaps it was because she had, all along, been subtly pulling him toward her without even trying.

He asked suddenly: "You draw Zhang Yuanheng to you — is it because you like him?"

"Or because you want to marry into the Earl's estate."

Shen Weici heard Song Zhang ask this strange question again and frowned slightly.

She had never given her heart over entirely, not to anyone — not unless she could be sure that person had given theirs entirely to her as well.

She didn't know whether she loved Zhang Yuanheng, but she did genuinely want to marry into the Earl's estate. It was the best choice available to her.

But at this moment, Shen Weici thought it was a strange and unreasonable thing for Song Zhang to ask, and she had no desire to answer him or to explain herself.

She truly had nothing that needed explaining.

Her gaze dropped, and she moved to step past Song Zhang. But her wrist was caught again. His cool voice sounded at her ear: "Afraid to answer me?"

Shen Weici had no choice but to turn her head and look at Song Zhang: "I care for Young Master Zhang and I want to marry into the Earl's estate. Is that answer satisfactory to Young Lord Song?"

Song Zhang looked down at Shen Weici's upturned face. His expression darkened. He let out a cold laugh and released her.

"Don't forget the time tomorrow, Shen Third Miss. I will not show you any leniency."

Shen Weici's fingers tightened slightly, and she lowered her gaze: "Young Lord Song need not worry."

And with that, she walked out from beside Song Zhang.

Song Zhang turned and watched Shen Weici's retreating figure — graceful steps, growing smaller through the layers of gauze curtains.

Only once she had completely disappeared from sight did his expression darken entirely.

He stood in his black robe by the window, looking out into the courtyard. He watched Shen Weici below, holding a lantern, walking toward the courtyard gate. A breath of wind carried her scent past him. Song Zhang's fingers, clasped behind his back, gave the faintest movement.

Meanwhile, Shen Weici walked home alone in the night, lantern in hand, the cold biting down hard on the way — worse still in the deep of early winter.

She pulled her cape tightly around herself and hurried along with her head bowed.

Halfway back, she happened to come face to face with Shen Rongshen, who was walking in her direction.

Shen Weici startled, and quickly called out: "Father."

Shen Rongshen was equally surprised to see Shen Weici at this hour, and came closer quickly: "What are you doing here at this hour? Were you looking for your stepmother?"

Shen Weici shook her head: "I left something here this morning and only just remembered to fetch it."

She turned to ask Shen Rongshen: "Has Father only just returned from outside?"

Shen Rongshen shook his head: "I've been in the study for a while."

He looked at Shen Weici and opened his mouth as if to say something, then seemed to think better of it. He only let out a sigh and said: "It's cold at night. Go on back quickly."

Shen Weici sensed that her father had something he wanted to tell her but was holding back. Her heart gave a jump. She asked: "Does Father have something to tell me?"

Shen Rongshen only sighed again: "Nothing. Go and get some rest — other things are not for you to worry about."

He took his attendants and left.

Shen Weici stood in place watching her father's departing back, and felt a creeping unease.

She turned and walked on. Her mind stayed busy with her thoughts the whole way back.

But she was so lost in them that when she reached a flight of steps, she misjudged her footing and lost her balance — her body pitched off the path and she tumbled to the ground.

A searing pain shot through her knees and elbows. The lantern in her hand went out as it hit the ground.

Darkness closed in completely.

Shen Weici bit her lip and pressed her hands against the ground, pushing herself up. She groped for the lantern and picked it up.

She tilted her head up to look at the moon. She did not feel sorry for herself or aggrieved — only a quiet, oppressive heaviness in her chest.

A thin wash of moonlight spread across the sky, cold gusts of wind blowing one after another. She looked at the winding, uneven path ahead, then leaned against the rockery for a while, watching the mist of her breath slowly dissolve, and walked the rest of the way back by the pale thread of moonlight.

She had not gone far when a weak glow of lantern light appeared ahead. She squinted at it for a moment and called: "Yuedeng."

The figure ahead heard her voice and hurried over, lantern swinging. "Miss!"

Yuedeng had not been able to put her mind at ease after going back, and had turned around to meet Shen Weici on the path. She hadn't expected to run into her out here.

She noticed the mud on Shen Weici's cape and asked quickly: "Miss — did you fall?"

Shen Weici leaned against Yuedeng, fighting down the pain in her body, and said in a hoarse voice: "Let's talk when we're back."

Yuedeng saw the pale, strained look on Shen Weici's face and didn't dare ask more. She steadied her and helped her walk home quickly.

chapters.title: The Marriage to Zhang Tingyi
chapters.content:
Back at Linchun Courtyard, Yuedeng helped Shen Weici out of her cape and discovered that the outer robe was caked with mud. When she rolled up the sleeves, she found a raw red wound across the delicate palm.

The other places still ached, but the heavy winter clothing had cushioned most of it — leaving only faint bruising.

Yuedeng was heartbroken and hurriedly called for the maidservants to bring hot water to clean the wounds.

Shen Weici, for her part, felt nothing much. She watched Yuedeng and Hexia rushing about in front of her, her thoughts already elsewhere.

She looked at the blue-green porcelain vase on the table beyond the curtain, the red plum branches inside releasing a faint and quiet fragrance. She turned her eyes away with a trace of melancholy.

Yuedeng's voice broke through her thoughts: "The medicine in the bottle is all used up. Should I go find the estate physician now to get another bottle?"

Shen Weici glanced at the small cut on her ankle — made by a branch, nothing serious.

She sent Hexia to sleep, then looked at Yuedeng: "Do you remember when you and I used to climb the mountain to gather herbs for my mother? I'd come home with worse injuries than this."

She sighed quietly: "This is nothing. And it's not as though becoming the Third Miss of a Marquis's household has made me any more delicate."

"What worries me right now is that the betrothal with Young Master Zhang may not go as smoothly as I hoped."

Yuedeng was startled. She looked at Shen Weici: "What does Miss mean?"

"Has Young Master Zhang gone back on his word?"

Shen Weici unpinned the silver hairpin at her temple and placed it in Yuedeng's hand. Her dark hair fell loose. She lay back on the bed with weary eyes, looking up at the canopy: "It's only a guess of mine."

"But perhaps things aren't as bad as I think. Don't worry yourself either."

She closed her eyes: "Yuedeng, you should sleep too."

Yuedeng looked at Shen Weici's slight, solitary back, heard the exhaustion in her voice, silently tucked the quilt corner in more snugly, and finally let down the bed curtain.

The following morning, after Shen Weici went to pay her respects to Madam Wen and was about to leave, Madam Wen unexpectedly held her back: "The estate is having two sets of winter clothing made for all the young ladies in each courtyard. Stay with me for a while. Later, you and Zhaohao can choose your fabric patterns together."

Shen Weici made no objection and stayed, sitting beside Madam Wen, remaining in the Second Courtyard to have breakfast with both Shen Zhaohao and Madam Wen.

Shen Zhaohao had reined in her hostility toward Shen Weici considerably of late. Though still cool and distant, she no longer actively sought trouble — even when the two of them sat together, she did not take a jab at her.

After a short while, several matrons brought in bolts of fabric for Shen Weici and Shen Zhaohao to choose from. Shen Weici didn't make a move, intending to let Shen Zhaohao choose first, but Madam Wen spoke up: "Zhaohao, you're the elder sister — let your younger sister go first."

Shen Zhaohao glanced at her mother, then said with clear reluctance to Shen Weici: "Hurry up and choose."

Shen Weici noted Shen Zhaohao's expression — she was forcing herself to comply and barely keeping her feelings in check. Shen Weici let her gaze rest there for just a moment and turned back. She looked at the fabrics before her and casually pointed to a bolt of unremarkable pink with purple magpies and another of white with sparrow patterns.

Madam Wen smiled and had a matron take the two bolts away to have winter garments made for Shen Weici.

She then asked warmly after Shen Weici's illness: "I told you to rest a few more days before coming to pay respects, and you only rested one day. Have you recovered these past two?"

Shen Weici raised her handkerchief to her lips and gave a small, staged cough, then said quietly: "Second Madam need not worry — I'm much better."

Madam Wen heard her say "Second Madam" and smiled: "Why so formal? Your mother is gone. From now on, just call me Mother, the same as Zhaohao does."

Shen Weici hesitated shyly, then obediently called out: "Mother."

Madam Wen was pleased by the address. She added: "There's no need to be distant with me from now on, either. You've called me Mother — I'll look out for your good as well."

"As long as you listen to me from now on, I'll certainly find you a good match. Whatever comfortable life you could want will be within your reach."

Shen Weici's heart sank at those words.

But she could not bring up the matter with Zhang Yuanheng yet.

Zhang Yuanheng had not come in two days, and had not even sent a letter. Shen Weici didn't know whether something had gone wrong on his end. If she said it now and Zhang Yuanheng still failed to come for the proposal, Madam Wen would have cause to say she had been meeting with a man in private without sanction.

She could only raise it when her father was present. Shen Weici decided to wait one more day.

Then she heard Madam Wen's voice continue: "Tomorrow the estate is expecting a distinguished guest. Wake up early and dress yourself nicely, and come meet the guest with the rest of us."

Shen Weici looked at Madam Wen, puzzled: "What distinguished guest is coming tomorrow?"

Madam Wen gave her a look: "Someone you've already met. The Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review, Master Zhang."

Shen Weici asked quietly: "If Master Zhang is coming to the Marquis's estate, surely it must be on important business. Would it be appropriate for me to be there?"

Madam Wen smiled: "What's inappropriate about it?"

She looked at Shen Weici with meaningful eyes: "You've already met him. His younger sister is now the Imperial Consort, dearly favored by the emperor. At a single birthday banquet, how many dignitaries rushed to pay their respects?"

"To be seen by him again would be a blessing for you."

Shen Weici said nothing more. She rose, curtsied to Madam Wen, and said: "The estate physician told me to take two more doses of medicine this morning and I still have one dose to take. I worry I might bring some sickness into the gathering tomorrow. I'll excuse myself now."

Madam Wen heard her out and didn't press. She simply nodded: "Go and take care of your health. You've looked haggard these two days — rest well."

Shen Weici lowered her head respectfully and withdrew from the room.

The moment she lifted the curtain and stepped outside, Shen Zhaohao looked at her mother in displeasure: "Why are you being so nice to her, Mother? Her marriage is yours to arrange. Even if she doesn't want it, she'd have to go along quietly."

"And she has no backing of any kind. Even if she used Zhang Tingyi to retaliate someday, the interests of gentry families are bound up together so tightly that she'd never have the means to do anything. If she had the skill to get back at people, she wouldn't have come looking for refuge at the Marquis's estate in the first place."

Madam Wen leaned back in her chair, leisurely sipping her tea. She looked at Shen Zhaohao and smiled: "Zhang Tingyi is coming tomorrow, and he's clearly taken with Shen Weici. Wouldn't it be a shame if she came in and started crying?"

"Besides, it doesn't hurt to let her feel a little gratitude right now. Being kind to her for a while costs nothing."

Shen Zhaohao rested her head against her mother's shoulder and pouted: "I can't wait for her to hurry up and marry that old man. Whenever I see her face, I feel ill-omened."

Madam Wen patted her daughter's hand: "Why the rush? Zhang Tingyi is coming tomorrow precisely to discuss the marriage arrangement. I'll settle it on the same day. If Zhang Tingyi is in a hurry, after the three letters and six betrothal rites, she could be married off in half a month — perhaps even before the new year."

Shen Zhaohao smiled: "That would be best."

"Who knows, maybe she'd actually be secretly pleased to marry Zhang Tingyi with her background."

chapters.title: What Are You Thinking About?
chapters.content:
Back at Linchun Courtyard, Yuedeng fetched more wound medicine from the estate physician and applied it to the cut on Shen Weici's palm.

As she worked, she looked up at Shen Weici: "Miss, what did the Second Madam's words mean?"

Shen Weici leaned back in her chair and said nothing, only sipping her hot tea slowly.

That afternoon, Shen Weici sent Yuedeng to the front gate to ask whether her father had come home yet.

Yuedeng hurried out and came hurrying back to report that the Second Master had not yet returned.

Shen Weici looked at the sky, which had already grown heavy with dusk. The courtyard lanterns at the outer gates were lit, and before long, full dark would descend.

She looked at the sheet of paper spread open before her, deliberated for a long while, and finally decided to write to Zhang Yuanheng.

She didn't want to be always pressing him to come for the proposal, but at the very least she wanted to know why he had said he'd come and then not come — and not even sent a letter. If she had some sense of what was happening on his end, she could figure out how to deal with things herself.

She thought carefully for a long time before at last putting brush to paper.

Yuedeng stood beside her the whole time, attentively grinding ink, the inner room quiet, the window shut, candles burning, shadows wavering — a sparse and lonely silhouette.

After some time, Yuedeng saw Shen Weici set down her brush and asked: "Are we sending it today?"

Shen Weici held the letter paper over the flame to dry it. The white of her fingers caught the amber glow, and one cheek was half-swallowed in the candlelight — her expression quiet, clear, yet steeped in silence.

Her eyes were still in the candlelight — steady, composed — but she said nothing for a long time.

Yuedeng saw that Miss wouldn't speak. She watched her lower her head and slip the thin sheet of paper into its envelope, then hand it to her: "Give Laifu a little extra and ask him to take this over right away."

"And tell the gatekeeper at the front gate that if Father comes home, to come let me know at once."

Yuedeng nodded and hurried off.

Once Yuedeng had gone, Shen Weici looked at the practice characters spread across the desk, but felt no desire to write any more.

Her eyes landed on the half-finished pouch beside the inkstone. She reached out and picked it up, then set it back down on the table.

Shen Weici waited for news of her father's return all the way until it was time to go to Song Zhang's courtyard — and still no word came from the front gate.

Yuedeng draped the cape over Shen Weici's shoulders: "This time I'll wait outside for Miss."

Shen Weici thought it wouldn't take long and nodded. She gave her other cape to Yuedeng.

Yuedeng was startled and protested: "How could I wear Miss's cape?"

Shen Weici looked quietly at Yuedeng: "I didn't take you in to be my servant. All these years, having you by my side taking care of me — you've been more someone I lean on than anything else. I don't know how I'd have gotten through everything without you."

She patted Yuedeng's hand and turned to lift the curtain and step outside first.

Yuedeng stood where she was for a moment, looking at Shen Weici's retreating figure. Her eyes grew warm. She pressed her sleeve to her eyes, then wrapped herself up quickly and followed her out.

The weather had grown colder and colder. Shen Weici pulled up the hood attached to her cape, covering most of her face.

From not far away, a voice called out: "Hey, who are you?"

Shen Weici stopped and looked down another path, where she saw Shen Zhaohao heading this way.

Shen Zhaohao wore a large purple cape trimmed with silver and grey squirrel fur, a winter hat on her head, a hand warmer tucked in her palms, and four or five maidservants trailing behind her — imperious and well-dressed, with all the wealthy ease of an official daughter.

This was the fork in the path, and Shen Zhaohao had apparently just come from Madam Wen's quarters. Running into each other here was chance.

Shen Weici loosened her grip on the cape and raised her face: "Second Elder Sister."

Shen Zhaohao saw it was Shen Weici and was briefly surprised, then frowned: "This path leads to Young Lord Song's Guansong Residence. Why are you walking this way?"

Shen Weici's expression remained unchanged: "This goes to Guansong Residence? It seems I've taken the wrong path."

"I was going to the Second Courtyard to find Father. Has Second Elder Sister just come from Mother's quarters? Has Father come home?"

Shen Zhaohao looked at Shen Weici with a skeptical expression: "Why do you want to find Father at this hour?"

Shen Weici smiled: "Just a small matter."

Shen Zhaohao glanced at her dismissively: "Father's attendants came back to say he has a social engagement tonight and won't be back until late."

Shen Weici nodded: "I see, then never mind."

She turned to Yuedeng: "Didn't the wind blow your handkerchief away? Go and pick it up — I'll wait here."

Yuedeng paused for just a moment before nodding and going to fetch the handkerchief.

Shen Zhaohao gave Shen Weici one more look, then without any intention of walking back with her, took her maidservants and went on her way without another word.

Once Shen Zhaohao was out of sight, Yuedeng came back to Shen Weici's side and said: "Second Master has gone to a social engagement — Miss won't be able to see him tonight."

Shen Weici kept her head down and walked on, then said quietly when she heard: "Let's talk about it when we're back."

When she arrived, Yuedeng stood waiting under the covered walkway at the courtyard gate, while Shen Weici went in alone. She had expected that Song Zhang would again be absent as he had been before, but to her surprise, she walked in to find him already there — half-reclining against the chair behind his desk, both feet propped up on the tabletop with complete disregard for propriety.

His appearance suggested he had just bathed — a white underrobe inside, with a large red cloak embroidered with cranes draped loosely over his shoulders, the collar slack and wide open. His hair was pinned up with a jade pin, though some of it had fallen loose and still looked slightly damp.

From the moment she entered, those cool, languid phoenix eyes had not once left her — carrying a faint chill, and something of a careless, flippant ease.

Shen Weici noticed the maidservant standing behind Song Zhang who had been massaging his shoulders. In her impression of him, Song Zhang always had beautiful attendants nearby, always wearing that same cold and aloof expression. He had not left a particularly good impression on her.

She didn't want to say much, or pay attention to Song Zhang's watching gaze, and just quietly bent down to light the charcoal.

But her heart was heavy with worries, and even though her hands moved quickly, there were moments when she drifted.

When lighting the last brazier, her finger grazed the scalding copper surface. She let out a small cry and pulled back, and found two large blisters rising on her fingertip.

This hand had not been fully healed since that business with Song Zhang — the scrape now had a burn on top of it. She endured the pain and stood up. She looked at Song Zhang to say she was leaving, but found him already standing right in front of her, without knowing when he had moved.

His tall frame loomed oppressively close, especially with that open chest directly before her. Shen Weici froze for a moment and stepped back. But then her wrist was caught in Song Zhang's grip, and he lifted it before his eyes to examine it.

Shen Weici stared at him in bewilderment. She tried to pull her wrist free but couldn't, and could only raise her eyes to ask: "Could Young Lord Song release my hand first?"

Song Zhang tilted his head, looking down at Shen Weici — the faint pallor on her face, and just a flicker of agitation in her expression.

From the moment she had come in today, she'd been distracted. He looked into her eyes: "What are you thinking about?"

chapters.title: I Simply Enjoy Tormenting People
chapters.content:
Song Zhang's voice was low and quiet, and the warmth of his palm was almost scalding.

Shen Weici knew she had been a little hasty just now, eager to finish and get back to see whether any letter had come from Zhang Yuanheng.

But even if she had moved faster than usual, she hadn't made any mistakes.

She looked at him in confusion, tilting her face up to meet his eyes: "I wasn't thinking about anything in particular. My only thought was to light the charcoal as quickly as possible."

Song Zhang's tone, which had just been low and even, suddenly turned mocking. A snort: "Letting your mind wander while working for me — no one working under me has ever dared to be so halfhearted."

This was nitpicking, plain and simple — deliberately finding fault.

She kept her patience and answered him in the same even voice: "I am not under Young Lord Song."

Song Zhang looked at Shen Weici coldly: "Yet right now you are lighting charcoal for me."

Shen Weici closed her eyes, drew a slow breath, and genuinely couldn't understand how she had ended up in this unreasonable man's path.

She was by nature mild and unwilling to argue over matters of right and wrong. But just now, a sliver of real irritation stirred in her.

Since coming to the Marquis's estate, she had been pushed and stepped on from every direction. She had swallowed her anger and held her tongue, and what she had earned in return was only more and more brazen mistreatment.

It was exactly like her mother's brother's family back in Yuyang — every quiet concession she and her mother made had only invited the others to go further, and it had never won them a good ending.

A mild person moved to anger — she raised her eyes to Song Zhang: "There are things I have kept pressed down and preferred not to argue about, but Young Lord Song makes things difficult for me at every turn. At its core, isn't it simply that you see I am easy to push around?"

"The first time we met, Young Lord Song pointed a sword at me. The second time, you set a dog on me. May I ask — even if I am not well-regarded here in the Marquis's estate, did I go out of my way to provoke you or anyone else even once?"

"That charcoal was left in my corridor. My maidservants didn't recognize it for what it was and used it by mistake. I knew it was not right that it was used without asking, so I apologized to Young Lord Song — and yet Young Lord Song showed not the slightest regard for that and chose to humiliate me deliberately."

"I have endured all of it. I only wanted to live out my days in the Marquis's estate quietly, without making trouble or causing anyone grief. And yet whatever I do appears to be wrong in Young Lord Song's eyes. Even though I did light all the charcoal properly, Young Lord Song still found the absurd reason that I was "halfhearted" as an excuse to pick at me."

"Even a clay figure has three parts of temper. Does Young Lord Song not feel any unease in his conscience, bullying me like this?"

Song Zhang rarely heard Shen Weici string together such a long speech. Before this, whenever he had seen her, she was always quiet and composed — even when Shen Zhaohao deliberately set her up, she remained gracious and restrained in front of everyone, never rising to the bait.

In the couplet exchange, she neither led the field nor finished last, always placing herself in an unnoticeable position. When she spoke to people, she wore that warm, steady smile and used that gentle, unhurried voice.

In the sleepless hours of the night, Song Zhang often thought to himself that he was surely bewitched — because the moment he closed his eyes, it was Shen Weici's quietly smiling face. He had never seen anyone so gentle before, and kept wondering: what would a person like this look like when angry?

He had honestly begun to think she had somewhat the nature of a clay figure.

Now, watching that face become just slightly more alive with expression, he noted with interest: no powder, no rouge, natural features smooth as white jade, delicately arched brows with a hint of distant mountains, the only striking things those eyes — half-feigning anger, half-genuinely it, heavy with feeling, like the hazy moon emerging from clouds, at once languorous and bewitching.

Song Zhang, who had seen countless beauties, could not help but acknowledge that Shen Weici's looks were rare. Even the tribute women from Loulan, a land renowned for producing beautiful women, were nothing more than pretty on the surface when you looked closely. What he saw in her was something unadorned, that quality of beauty that needed nothing added — one glance and you were caught.

For the first time in his life, he found himself drawn to a woman in something like the way his soldiers always went when they encountered a beauty — he'd spotted her and simply wanted to tease her, even if it meant making her angry, even if it meant showing cold indifference right to her face.

An unassailable young lord was always more inclined to let the other person come to him. She needed only to crook a finger and give him one heated, alluring look — a young man still new to these feelings would perhaps have his blood running hot.

But Shen Weici was quiet by nature — even a thunderclap wouldn't stir her — which left Song Zhang, still finding his footing in these unfamiliar feelings, equally unsure whether what he felt was truly liking.

The only thing clear to him was that he wanted to find ways to see her more often.

Even if those ways amounted to doing nothing but tormenting her.

Song Zhang gave a low laugh, his brow arched as he looked at Shen Weici with deliberate provocation: "I feel not the slightest unease in my conscience. I simply enjoy tormenting people. What of it?"

These words, overheard from his hiding place in the shadows, made even Minghe give a long, slow shake of his head. The general was a man who had walked through a garden of ten thousand flowers without a single petal sticking to him — surely he hadn't sunk this low. Even if he'd never had the knack for winning a woman's heart, surely he hadn't become this hopeless.

He couldn't bear to keep looking. These past days he had seen it clearly enough: the general plainly had feelings for this person, and was being the most stubborn, thickheaded fool about admitting it to himself. Otherwise, why would he have run over just now the moment he saw her burn her hand?

With the way things were going, the general would never find himself a wife.

Shen Weici had not expected that Song Zhang could say such shameless words with such ease.

But then — she had spent a month in the Marquis's estate, and though she didn't know Song Zhang well, she knew he was imperial kin on his mother's side, a duchess's son, who had sailed through life unchallenged and rose to his current position untouched by failure. Why would she have imagined he'd have a sudden crisis of conscience?

Shen Weici felt that continuing to speak with Song Zhang was pointless. She could barely help herself at the moment — why waste any more breath on him?

She swallowed her feelings again and looked at Song Zhang: "Then what would Young Lord Song need from me, before he would let go of my hand?"

Song Zhang's thumb idly moved against that smooth skin — those slender fingers, delicate as spring onion, the more he looked the more his eyes burned. She was close enough that her scent was curling around him, and before he'd quite caught himself, he'd pulled her a step closer, tilting his head as he looked at her with studied amusement: "My clothing has come undone. Put me right, and I'll let you go for today. What do you say?"

Minghe, in the shadows, wanted to gouge out his own eyes. This was indistinguishable from harassment.

Shen Weici heard Song Zhang's words and froze. Her fingers curled inside her sleeve. The humiliation of it was enough to make her lose her composure entirely. Anger and mortification flared in her eyes, and her voice came out wavering: "I am not your servant."

Song Zhang saw the fury in Shen Weici's expression and frowned. In all his experience, women had fallen over themselves for any chance to be near him. He had never given any of them the opportunity — and here she was, actually angry about it.

And then he saw her eyes slowly reddening. In the candlelight, those glittering eyes glared at him with a shimmer of unshed tears. He paused.

The moment Song Zhang released her, Shen Weici turned and walked out without looking back, leaving Song Zhang standing in place, uncharacteristically caught off guard.

He thought of the blistered fingertip he had seen just moments ago, alongside those small scrapes. Against the whiteness of her skin, they had been impossible to miss.

He watched the retreating back of Shen Weici's angry departure, and Song Zhang felt a restlessness settle over him. He dropped back into his chair, and a maidservant hurried forward to resume massaging his shoulders, only to be frightened half to death by a single, flat "get out," and fled.

Minghe stepped out from the shadows and looked at Song Zhang's grim face, weighing carefully what he was about to say: "Earlier, this subordinate noticed that Third Miss's fingers were burned. Would it be appropriate for me to send her a bottle of wound medicine?"

Song Zhang's dark eyes settled on Minghe, cold and flat: "You think I need to court her favor by sending medicine?"

That one sentence shut Minghe's mouth entirely. He didn't dare say another word.

Song Zhang's gaze drifted to the letter on the desk that Shen Weici had sent to Zhang Yuanheng. He let out a quiet snort of contempt, expression darkening again.

His fingers toyed with the envelope. He remembered the distracted look she'd worn just now, and Song Zhang's eyes grew colder.

Rushing to write to Zhang Yuanheng like that — was she afraid she'd never get married?

chapters.title: Zhang Tingyi Comes to Propose
chapters.content:
Yueleng saw Shen Weici come out from inside, her expression visibly troubled, and hurried over to ask quietly, "My lady, what's wrong?"

Shen Weici shook her head. "Let's go back quickly first."

Once they were back, Shen Weici looked toward the entrance and then called Hexia over to ask, "Has anyone come from the front gate with a message?"

Hexia shook her head. "No one has come since you left, my lady."

Shen Weici paused for a moment, then nodded and went inside.

Meanwhile, Song Zhang tossed and turned in bed through the night. Every time he thought of the two large water blisters on Shen Weici's fingers, and of her bare and cheerless little courtyard, his expression darkened further. He finally sat up from the bed, grabbed the black outer robe hanging on the rack, threw it over his shoulders, and strode outside.

The night-watch attendant at the door, seeing Song Zhang heading out in the middle of the night still dressed in his sleeping robe with nothing but a single cloak over it, hurried after him with a lantern. "Second Young Master, shall I go and rouse Steward Qi?"

Song Zhang pressed his lips together without a word, his expression as cold and sunken as frozen ice. He simply took the lantern from the attendant's hand and walked away with long strides.

The next morning when Shen Weici woke, Yueleng came in to help her dress and suddenly noticed a translucent white porcelain bottle sitting on the bedside table. She picked it up and held it before her eyes, then looked at Shen Weici and asked, "Is this yours, my lady?"

Shen Weici heard the words and glanced at it, then took it and looked more carefully—she did not recognize the bottle at all.

She uncorked it, and a medicinal smell drifted out. She frowned and looked at Yueleng. "Did you get this from the mansion physician?"

Yueleng shook her head. "The one I got from the mansion physician was green—it wasn't this colour." She went to the chest behind her and brought out another bottle to show Shen Weici. "This is the one I got from the physician."

Shen Weici set the two bottles side by side and looked at them for a moment, then put them both down on the bedside table. "Let's not worry about this for now. We need to tidy up and get to the Second Courtyard, or we'll be late."

Yueleng quickly said yes and busied herself helping Shen Weici get ready.

Just before they left, Yueleng was fastening Shen Weici's cloak and asked, "My lady, we forgot to put medicine on your fingers. Shall we apply it before we go?"

Shen Weici drew her hand out from inside the cloak and looked at her fingertips. The blisters that had been so red and swollen the night before had gone down by more than half, and the other scrapes had healed considerably as well.

She curled her fingers inward and said quietly to Yueleng, "It's not urgent right now. Come with me."

The two of them walked the whole way to the Second Courtyard, but halfway there they came upon Song Zhang again.

He was standing on the main path without moving, as though waiting for someone. Seeing Shen Weici approach, he actually addressed her: "How are the fingers?"

Shen Weici looked up in surprise. The sky was still dark, and even with the lantern it was hard to make out faces clearly.

Song Zhang's expression was equally hard to read in the dimness, but she could feel the weight of his eyes looking at her from the shadows.

She was startled for only a moment before answering softly, "Much better."

She added, "Thank you for your concern, Second Young Master."

Shen Weici had long since trained herself to speak without giving anyone cause to fault her. Even though the two of them had parted on unpleasant terms the previous night, she still responded with her usual mild courtesy.

Song Zhang listened to her words and looked down at her gaze, half-lowered again—lashes long and gentle, always like the scent of an orchid, quietly entering the heart like the warmth of a spring breeze.

He found himself thinking of that time he had seen her in her old moon-white robe, how she had passed him by like a snow lotus blooming on some high mountain peak.

And her fingers, warm and soft in the cradle of his palm the night before.

Something stirred in the chest of this generally dissolute man, but he only returned to his usual arrogance and walked past without another word.

Shen Weici watched Song Zhang go, then pulled her cloak tighter and quickened her steps toward the Second Courtyard.

When she arrived, the serving woman at the gate went in to announce her. She waited outside, and when she heard her father's voice calling her in, her fingers stilled for a moment. Then she lifted the curtain and stepped inside.

In the main hall, Madam Wen had just come out and was serving tea to Shen Rongshen, while Shen Rongshen exchanged a few casual words with Madam Wen.

Both of them looked up in surprise at Shen Weici's abrupt entrance. Shen Rongshen set down his teacup and asked, "Why are you here so early today?"

Shen Weici caught Madam Wen's displeased look from the corner of her eye—she seemed annoyed that Shen Weici had come in directly.

Shen Weici stood quietly with her sleeves gathered before her and looked toward her father. "Young Master Zhang sent word yesterday that he would be having a matchmaker come today to formally propose. I had meant to come and tell Father yesterday evening, but Father returned late, so I thought I would come early this morning to let you know."

Madam Wen, standing behind Shen Rongshen, heard Shen Weici's words, and her face changed entirely. She crossed the room in a few steps to stand before Shen Weici, her expression ugly. "What nonsense are you talking? Young Master Zhang—which Young Master Zhang?"

"Are you saying you have been carrying on secretly with some man?!"

"Something this shameful, and you have the nerve to bring it up in front of your own father."

Madam Wen's tone was sharp and accusatory, her spittle nearly flying into Shen Weici's face, so that Shen Weici instinctively took a step back.

If she had not been forced to, she would never have chosen this moment to raise the matter.

Once Father left today, Zhang Tingyi would arrive, and once Madam Wen arranged the match with the Zhang family, there would be no escaping it on her own.

She had seen enough of the Zhang household's wealth and prestige to know even Madam Wen would want to ingratiate herself with them.

It had always been the parents' word that decided a daughter's marriage—Madam Wen was her nominal stepmother, and she had every right to dispose of Shen Weici however she pleased. There was nothing irregular about it. She need not ask Shen Weici's opinion at all.

She endured Madam Wen's tirade to the end, and then turned her eyes toward Shen Rongshen.

Shen Rongshen also felt Madam Wen's reaction had been excessive. He stepped forward to intercept her, saying, "That's going too far."

"The Second Young Master Zhang of the Yiyong Earl's Mansion is the match I chose for Weici. Zhang Yuanheng and Weici met in my own study. There was nothing improper about it—nothing like what you're suggesting."

"If the Earl's Mansion intends to come and propose formally, that is a good thing."

"When she and Zhaozao can both get married at the same time, won't that take one burden off your hands?"

At Shen Rongshen's words, Madam Wen's face transformed. She pointed at him in fury. "She has only been here a month, and behind my back you already arranged a match for her?!"

"Were you ever this attentive to Zhaozao?"

Shen Rongshen looked at Madam Wen with a headache, unsympathetic to her unreasonable tantrum. "Zhaozao's engagement was arranged from childhood—what would I need to worry about?"

"The Zhang family are sending a matchmaker today—you should make preparations. Once Weici's marriage is settled and she goes to live in the Earl's Mansion, doesn't that reflect well on you too?"

"People will praise you as a stepmother who did not wrong a concubine's daughter."

Madam Wen had not anticipated any of this. And Zhang Tingyi was also coming today—this was going to descend into chaos.

She jabbed a finger at both Shen Rongshen and Shen Weici, trembling with rage. "You two have kept this thoroughly hidden from me. I absolutely will not agree to this match!"

Shen Rongshen's expression shifted. He frowned at Madam Wen. "This isn't as simple as you think, woman. I was the one who brought about the match with the Earl's Mansion in the first place..."

"What do you mean, who brought it about first? If no betrothal has been formally agreed, there is no question of who came first!"

Shen Rongshen flung his sleeve. "What do you know, you shrew? If word gets out, my reputation will be ruined!"

Madam Wen gave a cold laugh. "Think carefully about which is worse—offending Zhang Tingyi, or offending the Yiyong Earl's Mansion."

"The Earl's Mansion has been in decline for years. Among the younger generation, only Second Young Master Zhang is worth anything. The eldest son of the Zhang family is a sickly man—there's no future there."

"But Zhang Tingyi is a favourite of His Majesty. As long as Zhang Tingyi has the Emperor's ear, who outside would dare whisper a word? And with Imperial Consort Zhang still in great favour, who would dare gossip about the Zhang family's affairs?"

Shen Rongshen stared at Madam Wen. "You hold your tongue for a moment!"

Madam Wen pulled her sleeves tightly together and said coldly, "Hold my tongue? Zhang Tingyi will be here any moment with a matchmaker, and you want me to hold my tongue?"

"I'd like to see how you handle this!"

With that, Madam Wen flicked her sleeve, took Shen Zhaozao by the arm, and swept out of the room.

Before leaving, Shen Zhaozao did not forget to cast a triumphant glance at Shen Weici.

Shen Rongshen watched Madam Wen's retreating figure, then turned to Shen Weici. "Go back for now. I need to think this over."

Shen Weici lowered her head and murmured a quiet assent. She looked once more at her father's slightly hunched shoulders, let her expression settle, and headed for the door.

chapters.title: All schemes
chapters.content:
Madam Wen's words crashed through the room like a clap of thunder.

Even though Shen Weici had long suspected as much, hearing it spoken aloud from Madam Wen's own lips made her feel, with bone-deep certainty, that this grand household devoured people whole.

She had traveled a thousand li, going round and round, yet in the end she still could not escape this fate.

Thinking on it, she could only marvel at how cruelly fortune toyed with people.

Shen Rongsheng stared at Madam Wen, his face a picture of shock. "When was this decided?!"

Madam Wen let out a cold snort and shot Shen Weici an icy glance before turning back to her husband. "At this point, what does it matter when? Shen Weici marrying Zhang Tingyi is no hardship for her."

"And you — have you forgotten that Chen He submitted that memorial impeaching you? Those people have no intention of letting it go. The Emperor may suppress it once or twice out of regard for Song Zhang and the main branch, but he cannot do so every time."

"And if you offend Zhang Tingyi on top of all that, you will be nothing!"

Shen Weici, who had been standing with her gaze lowered, stilled at those words. She raised her eyes and looked toward her father.

Shen Rongsheng was pointing a trembling finger at Madam Wen, his face flushed crimson. "You woman — a matter this grave, why did you not speak to me first?"

Madam Wen snorted again. "Keeping it from you was not my idea. It was entirely the Old Madam's."

"The Old Madam said you are indecisive and cannot make up your mind, so hiding it from you was her way of forcing your hand."

Now that everything had been laid bare, Shen Weici finally understood the reason behind the Old Madam's attitude toward her.

So from the very moment she had set foot in this household, it had all been calculated. No wonder the Old Madam had been so unusually amiable, making arrangements on her behalf without raising a single objection.

Shen Rongsheng fell silent, frozen where he stood.

Madam Wen looked at him and laughed coldly. "Do you still want to keep asking? No matter who is listening, the fact remains — Zhang Tingyi is bringing a matchmaker today. I am not afraid to say it plainly."

"As for what you choose to do, that is none of my concern. If you disagree, go speak to the Old Madam yourself."

The color drained from Shen Rongsheng's face.

After everything Madam Wen had said, what was left to misunderstand? It was all the Old Madam's doing.

He cast a troubled glance at Shen Weici standing beside him, then grabbed Madam Wen by the arm and pulled back the curtain, steering her inside. "Come in here," he muttered under his breath. "Don't say these things in front of the child."

Madam Wen's lips curved into a cold smile as Shen Rongsheng dragged her through the curtain.

Shen Weici knew she had been too slow. If Zhang Yuanheng had kept his word and come to propose two days earlier, things might have played out differently — either Madam Wen and her father would have quarreled and refused this match, or her father, out of whatever thin thread of paternal feeling he still possessed, would have let her marry Zhang Yuanheng.

At the very least, Zhang Tingyi's people had not yet arrived — it would not have been much of an offense.

But now that it had all come out, and with Madam Wen's words still hanging in the air, she found herself anxious about what her father would decide.

Just then, the outer curtain of the main hall was lifted. Shen Zhazhao and Shen Yanli came in to pay their morning respects, and finding Shen Weici standing alone inside, they began undoing their cloaks and asked the maidservant nearby, "Have Father and Mother not risen yet?"

The maidservant looked flustered and fumbled for an answer, her hesitation plain enough that Shen Zhaozhao sensed something was off. She glanced at Shen Weici, then swept the inner curtain aside and walked straight through.

Shen Yanli watched his sister disappear inside, then turned to Shen Weici. "Why are you here so early?"

Shen Weici was not in the mood for conversation, but she answered quietly all the same. "I came early without realizing I had."

Shen Yanli gave a long, drawn-out "Ah," then took her by the arm and steered her toward a seat. "Why are you just standing there? Come sit."

Shen Weici glanced at him and settled down without a word.

Shen Yanli looked at her — quiet, closed off, offering only one word for every one he gave — and found little pleasure in the exchange. He was just about to lift the curtain and go inside himself when he saw Shen Zhaozhao being ushered back out by Madam Wen's personal maidservant.

The maidservant leaned close and said softly, "Second Young Miss, the Master and Mistress are discussing something. Please wait out here for a little while. What tea would you like? This old servant will go and brew it for you."

Shen Zhaozhao had no interest in tea. She tilted her head curiously. "What exactly are Father and Mother talking about? Why can't anyone hear?"

The maidservant flicked a barely-there glance at Shen Weici sitting in the chair, then looked back at Shen Zhaozhao with a small smile. "If you don't know, Young Miss, how would this old servant know? You can ask the Mistress afterward."

That put an end to Shen Zhaozhao's questions. She looked over at Shen Weici, settled into the seat beside her, and thinking that today this girl was to be betrothed to a man nearly fifty years old, felt a creeping, shameful satisfaction rise in her chest.

Zhang Tingyi's reputation in the capital was known to all.

Leaving aside whether he had driven his wives to early graves — he was an inveterate lecher. In his younger years he had indulged so excessively that his health had long since been ruined, and now that he was older, he had found other ways to torment women. The concubines he took in were carried out again at regular intervals. Most were household-born servants, or beauties bestowed by the Emperor from tribute states, or women redeemed from the pleasure quarters — and when they died, no one cared.

No decent family would dare send a daughter through his doors.

Shen Zhaozhao shot Shen Weici a glance that was almost pitying, then leaned back against the chair and spoke to her. "Little sister, why are you still dressed so plainly today? The household has an honored guest coming — shouldn't you put some effort into your appearance?"

Shen Weici heard the words, looked at Shen Zhaozhao's expression, and felt contempt stir quietly behind her eyes. She lowered her gaze and said nothing.

Shen Zhaozhao was taken aback that Shen Weici dared not reply, and her brow furrowed. "I am speaking to you. Are you deaf?"

Shen Weici looked at her. The warmth that usually lived in her eyes was absent, but she was still, as ever, a person of composure — and so even now her voice carried a quiet elegance. "Second Sister need not concern herself with how I am dressed. Honored guests do not necessarily care about such things."

The words stopped Shen Zhaozhao cold. For a moment she couldn't quite collect herself.

Shen Weici almost never spoke back to her. In the ordinary way of things, she yielded in everything — words, actions, all of it. Yet today she was behaving entirely out of character, as though Shen Zhaozhao was beneath her notice. A slow, rising anger began to kindle in Shen Zhaozhao's chest.

She shot to her feet and pointed at Shen Weici. "How dare you speak to me that way?"

Shen Weici did not move. She looked at her, and felt only the beginning of a headache — not the slightest inclination to bother.

It was Madam Wen's maidservant who stepped forward to intervene, steadying Shen Zhaozhao with a hand and murmuring, "The Master and Mistress are in the middle of something important, Second Young Miss. A scene right now would not look well."

"Besides, there are guests arriving this morning. Please, bear with it a little."

That was enough to take the fire out of Shen Zhaozhao. True enough — Shen Weici was about to be brought by her mother to meet Zhang Tingyi. Making a scene now would indeed be poorly timed.

She swallowed her temper, gave Shen Weici a cold and pointed huff, and sat back down.

Across from them, Shen Yanli looked toward the maidservant. "They've been talking in there for ages. When are they coming out?"

The maidservant smiled at him. "It shouldn't be much longer."

Shen Yanli leaned back in his chair without much interest and sipped his tea at leisure. He was thinking of the gathering he had arranged today with a few friends at Zuixiang Tower — word had it that several new performers had recently arrived there, young women who played stringed instruments beautifully, and the thought had been nagging pleasantly at him ever since. He was nearly out of patience for waiting.

He was already planning it in his head: go back, change into something presentable, eat breakfast, and head out with his attendants.

Behind Shen Weici, Yue Deng's hand tightened anxiously around her sleeve.

Shen Weici did not move. Her eyes remained fixed on the curtain ahead.

chapters.title: She Was Never the Important One
chapters.content:
As soon as she stepped outside, Shen Zhaozao moved to block her path with a gloating smile. "About to be engaged to Lord Zhang, are you? You must be thrilled."

"Marrying into the Zhang household—what a windfall. Though I do wonder whether that constitution of yours can hold up to the wear and tear."

Shen Weici looked at Shen Zhaozao without expression, not allowing the girl's words to stir so much as a flicker of anger. "If it's such a windfall, why doesn't Second Elder Sister trade places with me?"

Shen Zhaozao's face stiffened, then she let out a cold laugh. "I'll leave that fortune to Younger Sister. It's only right—I'm the elder, after all."

Shen Weici's lips pressed together evenly. "True enough. I'll remember how good Second Elder Sister has been to me. Even if I do end up marrying into the Zhang household, I won't forget."

Shen Zhaozao's expression shifted sharply. She glared at Shen Weici. "Are you threatening me?"

Shen Weici's voice was quiet, her tone perfectly bland, her eyes as placid as a pale winter moon. "Saying I'll remember how good Second Elder Sister has been—that's a threat?"

She stepped past Shen Zhaozao. "Think whatever you like, Second Elder Sister."

Shen Zhaozao stood there blankly. She had expected Shen Weici to collapse into weeping and make a scene in front of her mother, getting herself dragged off by the serving women. What she had never anticipated was that Shen Weici would be so calm.

So calm that even her provocations could not penetrate it.

Like a pebble dropped into water that raised not a single ripple.

She turned and looked at Shen Weici's retreating silhouette, and gave a quiet, sinister smile. She would wait and see how much longer she could keep up that composure.

Once Yueleng was outside with Shen Weici, she couldn't help but ask, "My lady, you said a moment ago that Young Master Zhang would be sending a matchmaker today—was that true?"

Shen Weici shook her head. "If I hadn't mentioned Young Master Zhang coming to propose, how else was I to let Father know that Madam Wen planned to marry me off to Zhang Tingyi?"

Yueleng's face fell with worry. "But what do we do now? What if the Master also decides to give my lady to Zhang Tingyi?"

"Should we go and beg the Old Madam?"

Shen Weici gave a bitter smile and looked at Yueleng. "Didn't you hear clearly this morning? It was the Old Madam's idea to begin with."

Yueleng was stunned. "Then what do we do?"

She gritted her teeth in indignation. "This Marquis Mansion truly is a place that devours people everywhere you turn. If they really go through with something this unconscionable, my lady might as well slip away and escape."

Shen Weici murmured softly, "Escaping isn't so easy. The mansion has guards posted everywhere, and I don't know my way around the capital."

"Besides, in the worst case, it would be treated as fleeing an engagement. The Zhang household would not let that rest."

Yueleng grew frantic, very nearly in tears. "Then what on earth do we do?"

"Young Master Zhang still hasn't come to propose—is my lady really going to be married off to that old man?"

Shen Weici patted Yueleng's hand. "We take it one step at a time. Let's go back first."

But Shen Weici did find herself thinking of one person: First Madam, Princess Huimin.

Princess Huimin was the daughter of a Grand Princess and the Emperor's own niece by blood. She had no need whatsoever to defer to Zhang Tingyi. As long as she stepped in, the matter could be resolved.

Shen Weici had this thought and went with Yueleng toward the First Branch's courtyard—but the serving girl at the gate said that Princess Huimin had gone to Chanxin Temple to pray two days ago and would not return for another month.

Shen Weici was taken aback, and her heart sank several degrees further.

On the walk back, she passed the water pavilion and stood on the stone bridge, looking at the rockery half-hidden among the banana leaves. A wave of cool air swept over her, and her heart grew colder by degrees.

Once back in the courtyard, she asked Hexia again, "Has anyone come from the front gate with a letter?"

Hexia shook her head. "No one has come from the front gate at all."

Shen Weici nodded again in silence and went inside.

Zhang Yuanheng had not even sent a reply—she could not understand what he meant by it.

The serving girl brought breakfast. Shen Weici looked at the simple dishes, her appetite long gone.

She stirred the porridge listlessly with a silver spoon and forced down a single bite. The sweet jujube congee tasted like nothing in her mouth.

Beside her, Yaner, seeing Shen Weici eating only reluctantly, fretted, "My lady should eat a little more. At least it will warm you up."

Shen Weici had no appetite, but she heard Yaner's words and silently finished the bowl all the same.

She rinsed her mouth slowly, then sat back in her chair, cradling the warm tea and gazing sideways out at the courtyard.

The hanging blinds swayed gently in the stillness, serene, as though nothing at all had happened.

A cold draft moved through the hall. Yueleng came over. "Come inside, my lady. It's cold out here."

Shen Weici held her hands close to the coal brazier and said quietly, "It's stuffy inside."

Yueleng looked at her. "My lady's embroidered sachet isn't finished yet."

Shen Weici looked up at Yueleng, her light-coloured eyes as still as ever. "Do I have the heart to embroider a sachet right now?"

"There's been no word from Young Master Zhang. He won't say if he's coming, and if he's had second thoughts, the least he could do is tell me—I'm not so desperate that I'd insist on marrying him."

Yueleng quickly tried to comfort her. "Perhaps Young Master Zhang has been very busy and forgot to write back."

Shen Weici gave a quiet, rueful sound. "However busy he is, he ought to know I'm waiting on him."

"If he had come to propose a few days ago, my marriage might already have been settled. But now Zhang Tingyi has come first, and I'm being roasted alive over a fire with no one to help me."

"He doesn't know a thing about my situation, yet he neither comes nor sends word. I don't understand what he means by it. I no longer understand him at all."

Yueleng's throat tightened. She took Shen Weici's cold hands in hers. "Young Master Zhang won't break his promise."

chapters.title: Willing or Not, She Must Be Willing
chapters.content:
When the morning hour was almost at its peak, a serving woman came from the Second Courtyard with a message, asking Shen Weici to come to the front reception hall.

The moment she heard this, Shen Weici understood that her father had already made his choice.

It made sense. Given a choice between offending the Yiyong Earl's Mansion and offending the Zhang household, he would almost certainly choose the former.

Shen Weici looked at the serving woman and said softly, "Please go ahead, Auntie. I'll tidy myself up first and follow shortly."

But the serving woman folded her hands together and stood squarely in front of Shen Weici, tilting her chin up with a trace of arrogance. "Second Madam's orders, miss—I am to wait here and escort Third Miss over myself."

Shen Weici was still leaning back in her chair, fingers resting on the armrest. She took in the serving woman's words, looked at her, and let no expression cross her face.

She stood, made no effort to tidy herself, walked past the serving woman, and went out.

Yueleng also wore a cold expression. She cast the serving woman a look and fell in behind Shen Weici.

The whole way there, Shen Weici's face was tranquil—no emotion readable in it.

When she arrived at the main reception hall and stepped inside, she immediately felt a sticky gaze crawling over her.

At the upper end of the hall sat the Old Madam. Madam Wen and Shen Rongshen sat to one side; on the other sat Zhang Tingyi.

Shen Weici kept her gaze low and paid no attention to the stare fastened on her. As she had always done, she folded her hands before her and greeted the people in the hall with proper ceremony.

The Old Madam sat in the seat of honour and smiled with her customary affection. "Weici, greet Lord Zhang as well."

Suppressing the revulsion that rose at the Old Madam's words, Shen Weici responded and stepped forward to pay her respects to Zhang Tingyi.

Zhang Tingyi watched the beauty drifting toward him and nearly lost the use of his eyes. Though he had lived more than half his life already, he had never laid eyes on a woman of this quality.

Her bearing and features combined the seductive with the pure—cloud-soft hair, vermilion lips, brows like delicate brushwork in faint ink, lotus steps steady and unhurried, waist as slender as bound silk. She had depths of charm that far exceeded those of women who possessed only a pretty face. A single glance was enough to feel one's soul taken from one's body.

In his agitation he leapt straight up from his chair, his eyes riveted on Shen Weici, all but pressing himself forward. "A young lady such as yourself graces me by accepting my greeting."

As he said it, he craned his neck even further to look her over.

The Old Madam at the upper end of the hall took in Zhang Tingyi's spellbound response with great satisfaction. This foundling girl had turned out to be of some use after all.

Madam Wen sat beside him with a full smile, privately delighted to be rid of this thorn in her side in a way that also benefited the family. She let her eyes slide toward Shen Rongshen beside her, saw that he still wore that look of helpless reluctance—his face turned away as though he could not bring himself to watch—and felt a fresh surge of irritation.

The more he agonised over this daughter, the more it proved he still thought of that woman.

She stretched out a finger and pinched Shen Rongshen's arm, warning him not to make a poor showing in front of Zhang Tingyi.

Shen Weici raised her eyes, met that pair of slightly slack, besotted eyes, then dropped her gaze and quietly stepped back to find a seat.

The Old Madam at the head of the room smiled at Zhang Tingyi. "It is Weici's good fortune that Lord Zhang has come to seek her hand. We naturally give our consent..."

Zhang Tingyi only then peeled his gaze from Shen Weici and smiled at the Old Madam. "The Old Madam is too kind. At my age, to take such a beautiful girl from the Marquis Mansion—it is my good fortune as well."

"The betrothal gifts naturally will not be lacking. Tomorrow I will have my men bring one hundred and twenty loads of gifts over."

"As it happens I have some free time today—why don't we settle the matter right now?"

Zhang Tingyi looked across at Shen Rongshen and smiled. "Lord Shen, what do you say?"

Shen Rongshen stood up hastily. "Lord Zhang is too generous. Since that's the case, then let us..."

But before Shen Rongshen could finish the sentence, Shen Weici suddenly began to cough. She pressed her white handkerchief tightly to her lips—and within moments, the handkerchief was stained red.

The sight of it was shocking.

Immediately after came Yueleng's cry of alarm: "My lady! My lady!"

"Don't frighten me like this!"

Shen Weici slumped into Yueleng's arms, her face drained of all colour, her fingers trembling against her lips. Then she brought up another mouthful of blood.

Shen Rongshen's expression changed at once. He stood up and looked at Yueleng. "What is the meaning of this?!"

Yueleng clutched Shen Weici tightly and sobbed, "My lady has suffered from spitting blood for some time. Whenever her emotions run too high, she cannot stop herself from coughing it up."

"After my lady returned from the Second Courtyard this morning, she has been despondent all day. A letter came from Young Master Zhang, asking why she was unable to receive the matchmaker today as planned—he said that Second Master had already agreed to the match and that everything was prepared. He couldn't understand why today was suddenly not possible."

"My lady read that letter and brought up blood on the spot—but she made me keep it quiet so as not to worry Second Master. When the serving woman came to call her, my lady rallied herself to come over. I don't know why she has just now brought up blood again."

Yueleng looked up at Shen Rongshen through her tears. "I beg Second Master to call a physician for my lady."

"Otherwise something terrible will happen to her."

Shen Rongshen's expression shifted through several changes; he knew only too well why Shen Weici's emotions had run so high.

He immediately instructed his personal attendants in a grave voice to go and summon the finest physician in the capital, and then directed several serving women to support Shen Weici and take her back.

This sudden turn had caught everyone off guard—including the Old Madam.

But Shen Rongshen understood all too clearly how matters had come to this pass.

Madam Wen looked coldly after the departing Shen Weici. The timing was a shade too convenient—if it was distress over the situation, why had she not vomited blood the moment she heard about it that very morning, instead of coming here to do it? It was simply inauspicious.

Zhang Tingyi had equally not anticipated this turn of events. He had heard every word from that serving girl just now, and his cold, displeased gaze swept briefly over Madam Wen before fixing on Shen Rongshen. "Lord Shen, what is going on here?"

"And who is this Young Master Zhang that the girl mentioned just now? Don't tell me you had already made some other arrangement? If so, what did Second Madam Shen mean when she came to the Zhang residence and spoke those words to me earlier?"

"To make sport of me like this—mark my words, this is not finished!"

Shen Rongshen saw what was happening and quickly stepped in front of Zhang Tingyi to intercept him, bowing low. "Lord Zhang, please—this has all been one great misunderstanding."

"I have never agreed to any other match. The girl was talking nonsense. Please pay her no mind, Lord Zhang."

Zhang Tingyi looked at Shen Rongshen with a cold laugh. "Nonsense?"

"Then why did she vomit blood out of nowhere?"

"Would a servant dare speak nonsense on an occasion like this?"

"Do you take me for some fool you can play games with?!"

Sweat beaded on Shen Rongshen's forehead. He hastened to explain, "Weici has never had this condition before—it may be that she has caught a chill. We ourselves only found out just now."

Zhang Tingyi sneered. "She is your daughter, and you only just found out?"

"Shen Rongshen—you have made a mockery of me today. This is not over!"

With that, Zhang Tingyi flung his sleeve again and walked out cold-faced.

The threat from Zhang Tingyi frightened Shen Rongshen into abandoning all dignity. He rushed after him, apologizing every step of the way.

Madam Wen stood inside the hall, watching this scene, and her own expression had gone ugly. She had not imagined it would end like this.

Zhang Tingyi had departed in fury, and Shen Rongshen had chased after him. Only now did the Old Madam turn her fierce gaze on Madam Wen—so angry she could barely draw breath—and demand sharply, "What on earth has happened?!"

"And what is this about an arrangement with the Zhang family from the Earl's Mansion?!"

"Which Zhang family are we talking about?"

Madam Wen, hearing the Old Madam's stern voice, hurried to her side and recounted the whole story from beginning to end, without concealing so much as half a detail—she dared not, for fear the Old Madam would lay all the blame at her door.

When she had finished, she felt a twinge of private regret. She should never have called Shen Weici here. Knowing the girl was unwilling, she ought to have expected trouble. In the end, she had underestimated her.

chapters.title: Vomiting Blood
chapters.content:
When Madam Wen's account came to an end, the Old Madam set her teacup down on the small side table with a sharp crack.

Every serving girl in the room went silent as a cicada in winter—they all knew the Old Madam's temper was about to break.

Then came a stern voice: "I don't believe a word of that story about her coughing blood from emotional distress. Why would she cough blood early but not late—why now, of all times, coming here to cause trouble?"

"It's simply that Second Young Master Zhang has taken a fancy to her, and she has her heart set on marrying into the Earl's Mansion. That's why she staged this whole performance."

The Old Madam's aged eyes sharpened into something cold and merciless. "When the physician comes, go along and see what he says. If she dares try any tricks on me, I will not let her off."

Everyone in the Marquis Mansion knew the Old Madam's true temper bore no resemblance to her benevolent surface. Her husband had died young, and she had raised three sons alone, held the household together until all three branches had wives and children—that kind of iron endurance was rare indeed.

Madam Wen, for all her heavy-handed management of Second Master in her own courtyard, did not dare breathe out of turn in the Old Madam's presence.

She heard the Old Madam's instructions and immediately nodded. "Do not worry, Old Madam. I will go personally to observe."

While they were still speaking, the serving woman who had accompanied Shen Weici back returned. She went to Madam Wen's side, then turned to the Old Madam and reported quietly, "I followed along to Linchun Courtyard. Third Miss appears to have fainted—she is genuinely without colour. And blood cannot be faked; the smell of it is real enough."

"The serving girls in Linchun Courtyard were all in tears, and those tears were quite genuine."

The Old Madam, having heard this, gave another cold sniff. "I don't care about any of that. What I care about is what the physician says when he comes."

She paused, then added, "And not just any physician—what the imperial physician says is what matters."

She looked at the serving woman beside her. "Is the First Master in the mansion today?"

The serving woman replied, "Today is a day off from court—First Master has surely gone to Chanxin Temple to see Princess Huimin. He goes whenever he has free time."

The First Master of the First Branch and Princess Huimin had known each other since childhood and had harboured feelings for one another since their youth. But circumstances had forced things in another direction, and the Emperor had bestowed Princess Huimin in marriage upon the young lord of the Duke of Song's Mansion—while First Master had never taken a wife.

After the young lord of the Duke's Mansion died, Princess Huimin had remarried into Jian'an Marquis Mansion.

In all the years since Princess Huimin had come to the Marquis Mansion as a remarried wife, First Master had cherished and doted on her without reservation. The warmth between them was known throughout the entire household.

It was said that purely out of consideration for Princess Huimin's devotion to Buddhism and her fragile health, First Master had never pressed her to conceive another child.

The Old Madam also knew how devoted her son was to Princess Huimin, and she was not in a position to say much on the subject. She only gave a low sound of acknowledgment and said, "When First Master returns tomorrow, have him summon an imperial physician from the palace."

"I want to hear what the imperial physician has to say."

The serving woman quickly replied, "Don't worry, Old Madam—I will remember."

After a few more exchanges, another serving woman appeared at the door. "Old Madam, Second Madam—the physician has arrived."

Madam Wen looked at the Old Madam. "I'll go to Linchun Courtyard then."

The Old Madam waved her hand, and Madam Wen withdrew.

The moment she left the main reception hall, Madam Wen's expression hardened completely. She clenched her hands tightly, her face darkening. "If I find that little wretch has been deceiving everyone, I will make sure she suffers for it!"

Tan Mama beside her said hesitantly, "Third Miss probably wouldn't dare, would she?"

Madam Wen gave a cold snort and strode toward Linchun Courtyard.

Inside Linchun Courtyard, Shen Weici lay on the bed utterly without colour, not a spark of vitality in her—she had clearly fainted away.

Yueleng knelt at the bedside and wept without stopping, barely short of fainting herself.

The serving woman who followed Madam Wen everywhere—Chang Mama—frowned and bent close to study Shen Weici's face, even giving her palm a hard, covert pinch. When Shen Weici did not react in the slightest, she straightened.

There was blood at the corners of her lips; a few drops of it had fallen onto the pink-tinged collar of her garment; and her fingertips, from pressing the handkerchief to her lips, were stained a vivid red. The sight of it was arresting.

The faint smell of blood, too, was not something that could be faked.

Chang Mama reached out and collected a small smear of the blood from Shen Weici's lips, held it to her nose and sniffed—it was indeed blood.

The serving girls of Linchun Courtyard were all bustling around, fetching hot water to wipe Shen Weici's face and hands. Chang Mama took all this in and then retreated from the bedside.

From the corner of her eye, Yueleng saw Chang Mama step back—but still standing inside the room, watching the bed. She cried all the louder for it. "Poor my lady, born with this terrible illness since childhood, and then sold off by her maternal grandmother to be some old man's concubine."

"She came to the Marquis Mansion with such a sincere heart, hoping for a place to belong—and then to think that now, within barely a month..."

She did not dare go on. What remained of her words became only ragged, broken sobs.

Everyone in the room understood perfectly well what she meant. If it were said plainly, the person with cause to be ashamed would not be anyone in Linchun Courtyard.

Chang Mama's expression changed. She lingered no longer, lifted the curtain, and went out.

The moment Chang Mama left, Yueleng's crying quieted.

Hexia, however, began to cry in her place. After wiping down Shen Weici's hands and face, she stood looking at Weici's bloodless face and could not stop blotting her tears.

Yueleng gripped Shen Weici's hand and said to Hexia, "You all step outside for now. I'll watch over my lady here—let her have a little peace and quiet."

Hexia and Yaner, not wanting to disturb her, carried out the basin and wiped their faces as they went.

The moment the two of them were gone, Yueleng called out softly, "My lady."

Shen Weici opened her eyes—and then tilted her head to one side, and the moment she parted her lips, a fresh trickle of blood came from the corners of her mouth.

Yueleng was startled. She quickly grabbed a handkerchief and pressed it to the blood running from the corner of Shen Weici's mouth, watching it follow the line of her jaw down into the hollow of her neck, and fumbled in teary-eyed distress. "How did this happen?"

Before going to the reception hall, Shen Weici had wrapped some vermilion pigment in a handkerchief and held a mouthful of water in her mouth to moisten it. When dissolved, the pigment turned the handkerchief red. But to make it more convincing, she had bitten her own tongue to add a genuine tinge of blood—real blood and vermilion mixed together would be far harder to see through.

The wound on her tongue had been seeping blood steadily. Shen Weici had coughed twice in the middle of the proceedings, producing blood in full view of Madam Wen's serving woman. Then, when she fainted, she had gathered a mouthful of blood in her cheek, intending to ask Yueleng for a handkerchief—but the blood had run out before she could speak.

The pain in her tongue was such that sweat beaded on her brow, but she murmured to Yueleng, "The words I taught you—do you still remember them?"

Yueleng nodded quickly. "Don't worry, my lady. I have them all by heart."

Shen Weici closed her eyes slowly, swallowed another mouthful of blood, and then gave a small nod.

Yueleng looked at Shen Weici's face with worry. "But what about my lady's tongue?"

Shen Weici had Yueleng leave the blood-stained handkerchief on the pillow beside her—so the physician would see it straight away and be appropriately alarmed—and then said, "Tear me a small strip of clean cloth. I'll hold it in my mouth. We can deal with the rest after the physician leaves."

Yueleng promptly found a clean handkerchief that had been washed, tore it into four strips, and brought one to Shen Weici.

Shen Weici placed the cloth strip in her mouth and fell silent. She gave Yueleng's hand a brief, reassuring squeeze.

chapters.title: Spitting Out Blood
chapters.content:
Shortly afterward, Hexia came hurrying in to say that the physician had arrived—and that, from a distance, she had spotted Madam Wen coming as well.

Yueleng heard that Madam Wen was on her way and paused, then nodded and quickly pulled down the bed curtains.

The physician entered soon after. Yueleng dabbed her tears and went forward to explain the circumstances.

By then Madam Wen had lifted the curtain and come in as well. She listened to Yueleng's account with a detached air and settled herself unhurriedly into the chair a serving woman brought forward.

The physician, having heard Yueleng out, stroked his beard and said, "Based on what the young lady describes—emotional distress—this is typically caused by depressed lung qi."

"However, the specifics can only be determined after taking her pulse."

Yueleng quickly went over and drew back a corner of the bed curtains, extending Shen Weici's pale, limp fingers.

The physician sat on the stool and concentrated on feeling her pulse for a long while, his expression growing somber as he tried to formulate what to say.

Madam Wen crossed the room, her eyes sharp as she looked at the physician. "Are you finished?"

The physician looked at the aristocratic lady before him and chose his words carefully. "From the pulse, the six positions show a taut and slow rhythm. This arises from accumulated depression—as the heart qi gradually weakens and emotions suddenly surge, blood follows the qi and naturally forces its way upward."

The physician's words were brief, but their meaning was reasonably plain.

Madam Wen's expression fell. She looked at the physician. "Are you saying it was caused by emotional suppression?"
