The physician stroked his beard. "From the pulse, it would appear so."

Madam Wen asked again, "Can it be treated?"

"I can prescribe a suitable remedy," said the physician, "but really, the surest cure is simply a lighter heart. Once the mind is at ease, the condition will naturally resolve."

Madam Wen's brow creased. She glanced at Shen Weici on the bed, her expression unpleasant.

At this point Yueleng stepped forward. "Would the physician please write out a prescription?"

The physician nodded and went to the writing table to compose one.

Madam Wen, seeing this, had no wish to linger. She took her serving women with her and left.

Once Madam Wen had gone, Yueleng looked at the prescription in the physician's hand and began to weep again. "If my lady takes this medicine, will she not bring up blood again?"

The old physician, taken aback by the serving girl's sudden intense weeping, frowned and said, "Actually, when I took your lady's pulse just now—while there is accumulated depression, the pulse alone would not normally cause spitting of blood. Why did she suddenly cough blood today?"

Yueleng then sobbed through the full explanation, wiping her tears as she spoke. "My lady was about to be betrothed to the man she loves, with the Master's blessing—and then Madam decided to give my lady to the Honourable Zhang, who is the Imperial Consort Zhang's own brother. Lord Zhang even came to propose today. My lady's heart was so overwhelmed that this is what happened."

Zhang Tingyi's reputation was known well enough to the people of the capital.

The apprentice trailing behind the old physician heard Yueleng's sobbing account and immediately stepped forward in outrage. "How could such a thing happen?!"

Yueleng went on weeping. "My poor lady, with no one to depend on, and her mother just passing away not long ago—she was already gravely ill from the grief, and then to come to the Marquis Mansion after only a month..."

She left the rest unspoken, but the apprentice was furious, casting his eyes around the bare little room. "The Second Madam of this Marquis Mansion is truly too vicious."

Yueleng wiped her tears and moved to stand beside the apprentice, choking out, "Please keep these words in your heart. I say this only because I cannot bear to see my lady wronged."

"But what can one do when one is at the mercy of the Marquis Mansion? One can only let Madam do as she pleases."

The apprentice, about to say more, was quieted by the old physician's restraining hand. The physician addressed Yueleng: "The prescription is written. Fill it according to these instructions. Perhaps it will bring some improvement."

Yueleng said nothing further, pressed her handkerchief to her eyes, and then went to show the physician out.

After seeing the physician far enough away, she turned and went back inside.

She handed the prescription to Hexia. "Go to the mansion physician's dispensary and have these medicines filled. Say it's what the physician prescribed for my lady."

Hexia nodded and went.

Yueleng told Yaner to go and heat water so she could fill two hot-water bottles for the young lady, then went inside herself.

She lifted the curtain and sat down beside the bed, then said softly, "My lady—telling the physician all those things—will he really pass them on?"

"I could see just now that he seemed quite guarded about it. He may not dare go around spreading gossip about the Marquis Mansion."

Shen Weici looked at Yueleng, enduring the pain in her mouth, and said, "Who could sit on a piece of gossip this juicy and say nothing? The old physician might hold his tongue—but that young apprentice almost certainly won't."

Yueleng was still uneasy. "But what if they do talk and Madam finds out and makes trouble for them?"

Shen Weici closed her eyes slowly, her pale cheeks a stark contrast to the vivid red at the corners of her lips, a barely perceptible trace of blood still on her face. "If you don't want others to know, don't do it in the first place."

"Zhang Tingyi came to this mansion today with a matchmaker—how many people saw it? With so many servants and serving women in the Marquis Mansion, someone will always talk. Even if Madam wanted to make trouble for everyone who speaks, she couldn't possibly catch them all."

"Besides, this is already known to a great many people. At dinner, you can mention it in passing, seemingly by accident—the serving girls will carry the word along, and eventually the First and Third Branches will hear of it. Once everyone is talking, Madam won't have the energy to chase down who first said it."

"What I need now is to stay ill a little while longer, and wait to see what the talk outside amounts to."

Yueleng felt her heart settle at last. She looked at Shen Weici and said, "My lady always has a plan. Otherwise we'd truly be at Madam's mercy and my lady would end up married to that old man."

"My lady's whole life would have been ruined."

Shen Weici was quiet for a moment. Her brow and eyes held the muted calm of a distant mountain, and her voice was very soft. "I never wanted to do any of this. I had no wish to put anyone in a difficult position. But when others put me in a difficult position, all I can do is protect myself."

Yueleng nodded, and was about to say something more when she heard footsteps approaching outside. She quickly lowered the bed curtain.

Shen Rongshen walked in. He looked first at the closed curtains of the canopy bed, then turned to Yueleng standing at the bedside, frowning. "What did the physician say?"

Yueleng held back her tears and replied, "The physician said my lady's heart qi has weakened—that when her emotions became unsettled, the blood followed the qi and surged upward, causing her to spit blood."

"I've already sent someone to the mansion dispensary for the prescribed medicines. They should be back shortly."

Shen Rongshen looked at the closed curtains, something lodged in his throat, and then asked Yueleng, "How is she now?"

Yueleng's tears came harder. She said in a choked voice, "My lady has not yet woken. The physician said to let her rest quietly, and I didn't dare call out to her."

Shen Rongshen gave a long, heavy sigh. The situation with Zhang Tingyi was now thoroughly ruined—he would have to wait until Shen Weici recovered, then bring her to the Zhang residence in person, and hope it might placate the man's anger.

He could see plainly that Zhang Tingyi still wanted to marry Shen Weici—he was furious only at the intrusion of the Zhang family from the Earl's Mansion.

Behind Zhang Tingyi stood not only Imperial Consort Zhang, but the Fourth Prince—who currently had the broadest support among civil officials. Even Song Zhang's paternal second-uncle maintained close ties with the Fourth Prince. He could not afford to make an enemy of Zhang Tingyi.

He let out another long sigh, then told Yueleng sternly, "Look after Third Miss carefully. If anything is the matter, come to me at once."

Yueleng heard Shen Rongshen's firm instructions and nodded quickly.

Shen Rongshen said no more. He walked out, intending to wait until Shen Weici had recovered and then speak some gentle words to bring her around.

chapters.title: If You Don't Want Others to Know, Don't Do It
chapters.content:
That night, inside the Chengde Hall, the palace was alive with song and dance. The Emperor sat at the head of the celebration with Imperial Consort Zhang nestled against him, laughing and drinking, while below them sat Zhang Tingyi and several of the Emperor's favoured officials, all pouring out compliments and flattery.

Song Zhang sat with folded arms not far from the Emperor, watching it all without expression, and then glancing at the hour—already past the xu hour—he felt a faint but unmistakable urge to go back.

Otherwise he would miss her.

The Emperor's voice broke through his thoughts, as he called out to Song Zhang with a laugh: "Don't sit there so stiffly—come drink with the others."

"You love a beautiful woman more than anyone I know. I've saved one especially for you tonight. Stay with Us and drink until neither of us can stand."

Song Zhang glanced at the Emperor, then rose and bowed with his hands clasped. "Your servant still needs to go and station the Feathered Forest Guard afterward to ensure Your Majesty's safety. I dare not drink."

The Emperor gave a great laugh. "So principled all of a sudden."

"I hear from outside that you still haven't touched a woman. Is that true?"

The Emperor had blurted this out in front of the whole hall, and everyone fell quiet at once, turning to look curiously at Song Zhang.

Song Zhang's decisive, ruthless manner in all things was well known—but while beautiful women had always approached him willingly and he had always played along, no one had ever heard of Song Zhang keeping a woman through the night. Those sent by various households had all been passed on to his subordinates; he had never touched a single one of them himself.

This rumour had been in circulation ever since Song Zhang returned to the capital. At the height of his prestige, with the Emperor's complete trust, his elevated rank bringing constant invitations and flattery, Song Zhang had been casual about all of it—he went where he was invited, accepted the company of beautiful women as they came—and yet always seemed to stop short of going further. When leaving, he never cast a backward glance, let alone took anyone with him.

And so people had begun to say he had been injured at the frontier in a way that left him unable to perform as a man.

Though no one had dared say it openly this past year, there had been plenty of whispers.

The Emperor's asking it aloud now was tantamount to giving voice to everyone's unspoken curiosity.

After all, Song Zhang was already twenty-two—not a young age. Many men had women in their chambers at sixteen or seventeen. Song Zhang had followed his grandfather in the army from childhood, where there were no women—but that hardly explained why, at twenty-two, he had neither a concubine nor a chamber companion.

He certainly didn't look like a man indifferent to feminine beauty.

Song Zhang, feeling the eyes of the whole room on him, smiled. "Surely Your Majesty doesn't believe those rumours. How could your servant possibly not have known a woman?"

"The truth is simply that ordinary women don't interest me."

When Song Zhang said this, expressions of sudden comprehension spread across every face in the room. Of course—apart from lacking the status of an imperial prince, Song Zhang was still the Emperor's most prized subject. How could the women of the pleasure quarters ever catch his eye?

No doubt he kept who knew how many beauties out of sight at home.

The Emperor, hearing Song Zhang's answer, was at ease again. He looked at Song Zhang and said, "Your mother had your maternal grandmother petition me to arrange a match for you not long ago, saying it was time to settle you. As long as there's nothing physically wrong with you, half a year—don't forget your promise."

Song Zhang felt the helplessness of it. Since returning to the capital, he had been urged on from his grandfather's side, his mother's side, his maternal grandmother—and now the Emperor too. Thinking about it, the frontier had been far more peaceful.

The Emperor was determined that Song Zhang should drink with the company that night, and had a beauty sent over to sit with him, and a place specially prepared for him to sleep, saying that if he liked the girl, he was welcome to take her away.

This woman was no ordinary person—she was a princess from the small kingdom of Loulan, renowned for producing beautiful women, who sent tribute beauties every year. The Emperor, seeing that this one was of good birth, had set her aside specifically to give to Song Zhang. The Old Duke of Song had been waiting to hold a grandchild so urgently that he was making himself ill—the Emperor felt he had to help him along somehow.

The poor Old Duke of Song, well into his years, with only this one grandson from the main line of the household, and still no grandchild to carry on the family line—how could he not be anxious?

The Emperor also had an old friendship with the Duke from their youth, and considered him his most loyal general. It had been precisely with the intention of giving the Duke's household honour and imperial grace that he had once bestowed Princess Huimin in marriage upon the young lord of that mansion.

Song Zhang was pressed by the Emperor into accepting the woman—unable to refuse, he had no choice but to agree.

The banquet did not end until past midnight. When Song Zhang left the palace, he carried a faint smell of wine, and though he had drunk a fair amount, his steps were still steady.

Song Zhang drank occasionally and good wine was often sent to him as tribute from his subordinates. Ordinary spirits posed no difficulty.

Outside the palace gates, Song Zhang took the riding crop from his guard and made to mount. Minghe quickly called out, "General—there is still the Loulan princess that the Emperor gifted you."

In the night, Song Zhang narrowed his eyes and looked sideways. There indeed stood beside Minghe an exquisite beauty—skin like smooth jade, eyes like autumn water, who had waited on him very attentively throughout the banquet.

Song Zhang, born tall and straight, had the clean, spare elegance of white crane and green pine. When he did not smile, he was cold and forbidding; when he smiled, his brow cleared and his eyes brightened into something of exceptional handsomeness—and that pair of cool, hooded phoenix eyes, half-smiling and never quite committing, made people want to draw near while simultaneously fearing to come too close.

The woman was somewhat afraid of Song Zhang. He had let his hand rest on her without scruple during the banquet, had smiled and accepted the wine she poured him, had occasionally exchanged a playful word with her—and then the moment the feast ended, he had turned into someone else entirely. Not a single glance in her direction. He had simply walked away alone and left her behind.

If the Emperor had not told her to follow, she would have had no idea what to do with herself.

She took a careful step forward, tears trembling in her eyes. "His Majesty has given me to the General as a concubine. From now on I belong to the General—I beg the General to take me in."

She had been a princess raised in every luxury—who could have imagined she would travel all this way to Dayu, and though she had escaped the fate of becoming a consort of the old emperor, the man before her clearly felt very little for her. For the first time in her life, she found herself doubting her own beauty.

Song Zhang frowned with a fair degree of impatience. This was not the same as the ordinary women he usually passed along to others—this was a concubine the Emperor had specifically bestowed on him. It wasn't so simple to just dismiss her.

He stood at the palace gate, gave the reins a pull and mounted, then said to Minghe from the saddle, "Have two guards escort her to the Marquis Mansion and settle her in."

It would also serve the purpose of stopping his mother from sending women to his room. The woman would at least be useful for that.

With that, Song Zhang gave a flick of his crop and rode off in a trail of dust.

Minghe looked at his general's complete lack of any tender feeling toward the woman and felt it was a shame to waste someone so beautiful.

He glanced involuntarily at the Loulan princess—and honestly, looking her over, she was no less lovely than Third Miss of the Marquis Mansion.

But he did not dwell on it. He summoned two guards, asked them to see the woman safely to the Marquis Mansion and treat her properly, then mounted his own horse and followed.

Song Zhang returned to the Marquis Mansion, entered Guansong Residence, and crossed the threshold with the intention of bathing immediately.

But as he passed the inner chamber and found the brazier cold—not a trace of warmth in it—he paused and frowned, then called over the serving girl on duty. "She didn't come tonight?"

Xunmei knew at once who Second Young Master was asking about. She quickly stepped forward. "Today there was a great commotion at Linchun Courtyard—word is that Third Miss coughed blood this morning, and Second Master even called for a physician to come and see her."

"Tonight during the xu hour, when Third Miss hadn't come, I went over to check—I was afraid she might have forgotten. Linchun Courtyard's Yueleng said Third Miss was still unconscious and hadn't woken. That's why I didn't..."

But before she could finish, a gust of air swept past—and when she came back to herself, all she saw was Song Zhang's back as he strode away.

chapters.title: She Didn't Come Tonight
chapters.content:
Inside Linchun Courtyard, Shen Weici's sleep was far from peaceful.

She dreamed again of a heavy snowfall. She was crouched in front of the west-room stove, boiling medicine—but no matter how long she cooked it, the pot held nothing but clear water. A voice repeated at her ear, over and over, "It's no use. Your mother is dying."

She clapped her hands over her ears and screamed back, "My mother is not going to die!"

"My mother is not going to die!"

Covering her ears could not muffle that maddening voice. It went on calling to her: "Your mother is dying."

"You'll have no mother very soon."

Shen Weici strained to see who was speaking. She ran out into the courtyard, tilting her head back to look up at the white-blanketed sky as snow fell and fell. Then she lowered her head—and found a face grinning at her from directly in front, a wide, sinister grin.

Shen Weici's eyes flew open.

She stared blankly at the brocade coverlet before her, her heart still hammering in her chest. That face—she could not forget it.

She let out a long, slow breath and closed her eyes again, exhausted.

Song Zhang sat on the edge of the bed, quietly watching Shen Weici curled in on herself. Her dark hair fell soft and obedient, and only the gentle fragrance that drifted from her could have made him—a man of no fixed inclinations—actively seek out the company of any woman.

His gaze settled on her trembling lashes; clearly she was sleeping badly. The shadows under her eyes told of exhaustion—which was why she hadn't noticed him yet.

Song Zhang drew a calming incense sachet gently past Shen Weici's face, and before long the person who had been sleeping so uneasily settled into a deeper rest.

He bent close to look at the bloodstains on Shen Weici's moon-white collar—only a few scattered drops—but in Song Zhang's eyes, accustomed to bloodshed as they were, this was the first time he found such a sight difficult to look at.

He studied Shen Weici's face. Those features—always seeming to hold something of clouds and rain, some gathering weather—Song Zhang could not help but admit that his feelings for her had been stirred.

He looked at the small curve of her ear showing through the dark strands of her hair, at the subtle allure hinted at below her neat collar, at those full lips—each detail pulling at him.

His slender fingers trembled slightly. He laid them against her soft cheek, and his lips began to lean toward her—when the sleeping figure shifted, and those dark brows drew together with a small frown, as though something were hurting.

Song Zhang felt he was taking advantage of her. Shen Weici had coughed blood, and here he was with his head full of improper thoughts—he had even been on the verge of sliding his fingers under the coverlet to feel the warmth of her.

His tall figure blocked most of the candlelight. He drew his hand back and took a deep, steadying breath.

When he thought of the letters that had passed between Shen Weici and Zhang Yuanheng—every single one of them was something he could not bring himself to see.

He suppressed that particular feeling. Song Zhang had not yet sunk so low as to grovel and ingratiate himself for the sake of a woman.

Nor had he any need to compete for a woman who knew only how to climb toward the highest branch.

He rose from the bed's edge—and yet couldn't bring himself to look away from Shen Weici quite yet.

He had hurried back in the middle of the night, hadn't he—and wasn't it for the sake of seeing her?

Even without a single word exchanged between them, knowing that her quiet presence was nearby gave him a small, nameless ease.

His steps slowed. Song Zhang exhaled a breath of wine, and sat back down on the bed's edge.

He sat in silence, watching her, and still could not quite decipher what he felt for Shen Weici.

His gaze drifted to her fingers. He lifted them—the wounds had healed mostly, leaving only faint impressions.

His eyes passed over the white porcelain bottle on the bedside table. He reached for it and applied a little more medicine to her fingertips.

He let his touch brush through a strand of her hair, and his gaze deepened, briefly.

When Song Zhang left, the hem of his deep purple official robe swept past the candlestand, and the flame shivered once, then was still—just as he had come without a sound, he left without a trace.

Minghe waited outside in the night, lantern in hand, and watched his general emerge from Linchun Courtyard with a subdued expression—and in those eyes that were always cold, for just a flicker, something tender.

But it was more like snow beginning to thaw at the first hint of spring—gone in an instant.

Purple robe rippling, his bearing luminous as carved jade, Song Zhang was the kind of man who needed only to sweep past on horseback for women to throw themselves in his path. Minghe thought that if the General truly had feelings for Third Miss, he might as well just swallow his pride and show it a little—the lady might like him too.

Song Zhang, cold-faced, saw Minghe's look of restrained deliberation, then glanced back toward Linchun Courtyard and said quietly, "By morning I want to know exactly what happened at Linchun Courtyard. And have Chief Imperial Physician Lin summoned—tell him to take a proper look at the patient. If he can't do his job properly, he needn't stay at the Imperial Medical Bureau any longer."

With that, Song Zhang headed back to his courtyard, leaving Minghe behind with a long, quiet sigh.

chapters.title: Watching Her at Midnight
chapters.content:
Early the next morning, Minghe came in and reported everything he had learned.

"Word is that yesterday Zhang Tingyi came with a matchmaker to propose. The Second Branch intends to give Third Miss to Zhang Tingyi as a new wife. When they called Third Miss over, she seemed fine at first—paid her respects and everything—but the moment she sat down she vomited blood, and fainted on the spot."

"A physician was called and he diagnosed it as illness born of accumulated grief: depressed heart qi, and blood surging upward with the qi."

He clicked his tongue. "Who doesn't know the Zhang household is a pit of fire? And the Second Branch goes and throws their daughter into it. She may not have been particularly favoured, but there's no need to treat someone like that. It really is a waste of Third Miss, with her looks and her talents—to be matched with a man like that old thing. No wonder she vomited blood."

"Now the whole mansion is whispering that Third Miss had a suitor she cared for and was nearly betrothed, but the Second Branch tore apart the match for their own gain—selling their daughter to win favour. And they're dragging the Old Madam into it too, saying she has a kind face but a cold heart, and that the whole thing was her doing."

"I also heard that yesterday the Earl's Mansion was supposed to come and propose—but then somehow didn't. Nobody's spreading that part around; I only found out after a good deal of coaxing from someone in the Second Courtyard's staff."

"In hindsight, it's a good thing they didn't come. Otherwise everything would have descended into chaos."

Song Zhang stood straight before the folding screen, a serving girl kneeling before him to fasten his arm guard. He listened to Minghe's account, and his brow creased, his expression darkening. "The Earl's Mansion came to propose?"

Minghe thought about how much he'd just said and how Song Zhang had only picked up on that one detail.

He quickly replied, "That's what I gathered, but they ended up not coming—whether it's true or not, I can't say for certain."

"There's a lot of talk circulating below stairs right now, and Third Miss is really hard done by."

Song Zhang's eyes grew heavy for a moment, then suddenly he gave a short, contemptuous laugh, the corner of his lip curling. "Good. Let it spread. The more people who hear it, the better."

Minghe stared. "But it's the Marquis Mansion's affairs—if something this shameful gets out, the mansion's reputation..."

Song Zhang glanced at Minghe with a sidelong look. "What does the Marquis Mansion's reputation have to do with me? What does the Second Branch's business have to do with the First?"

His expression turned ominous. "Go and have the patrol street runners spread it through every lane and alley. And tell the storytellers in the teahouses to make a proper production of it. I'd very much like to see where the Second Branch will put their faces when this is done."

Minghe understood immediately and replied, "Leave it to me, General. I guarantee it'll be on every corner of the city within two days."

Candlelight flickered across Song Zhang's cold face. His phoenix eyes were sharp, his lips thin as a blade, his voice carrying a chill. "That old Zhang Tingyi—what nerve, at his age, to come and propose to a girl in the Marquis Mansion. Let him take a good look at whether he's worthy."

"I'll see to it that he gets a taste of what he deserves."

"That lecherous old fool."

Minghe looked up at those ominous words. Since their return to the capital, he had never seen Song Zhang display such obvious anger. To think he had been moved to rage over the matter of Third Miss—Minghe felt a cold jolt run through him.

Those outside might not know what he knew—but he understood his general all too well. The man's methods could be bone-chillingly subtle. Anyone who drew his genuine hatred would be lucky to come out of it in one piece.

He watched Song Zhang straighten his dress and head out, and quickly fell in behind him.

But Song Zhang had only gone a few paces when he stopped and looked at Minghe. "After the imperial physician has seen to her, have him find me in the palace. Whatever her condition is, I want to know all of it."

Minghe agreed to everything without reservation.

chapters.title: Illness Born of Accumulated Grief
chapters.content:
When Shen Weici woke that morning and was sitting up against the headboard drinking her medicine, Hexia suddenly came in to say an imperial physician had arrived.

Shen Weici's vomiting of blood—apart from Yueleng who knew the truth—was unknown to any of the other girls in the room. The medicine being decocted was still something she would need to drink and be seen to drink.

Hearing that an imperial physician had come did give her a small start. She wondered whether Madam Wen, suspicious, had arranged for one.

But she was not particularly worried. There were many reasons a person might vomit blood, and as long as no one could prove she had faked it, everything else could be explained.

She had also deliberately not changed the inner robe stained with blood—so whoever examined her would see it first and form the impression immediately.

She handed the empty medicine bowl to Yueleng and asked her to show the imperial physician in.

Yueleng was still a little anxious. She looked at Shen Weici worriedly. "What if the imperial physician sees something isn't right?"

Shen Weici met Yueleng's gaze, kept her eyes low, and murmured, "Unless he can prove that my vomiting blood was faked, if he cannot find signs of the condition, he can only admit his own medical skills are insufficient."

"This isn't as bad as you're imagining. Just behave normally."

Only then did Yueleng relax somewhat, nod, and let down the bed curtains.

When Chief Imperial Physician Lin was brought into the inner room by Yueleng, the first thing that greeted him as he entered was a faint, refined feminine fragrance—quite lovely.

He glanced around. The room's furnishings were plain, but neat and clear-aired; it was nothing like what one would expect for a young lady of the Marquis Mansion.

General Song's people had sent for him early this morning to come to the Marquis Mansion and examine Third Miss Shen. He had assumed it would be one of the main-branch daughters—he had not imagined he would find this small, tucked-away courtyard.

But Imperial Physician Lin only cast a brief glance around before taking his seat on the stool beside the curtained bed.

He looked at the slender wrist extended through the gap in the curtains—skin like smooth jade, fingers fine and tapered as carved scallions, and a small red mark on the palm. Very beautiful indeed.

He also noted that the moon-white sleeve visible at the wrist bore two drops of blood—likely fallen there when she had pressed the handkerchief to her lips during the coughing. Imperial Physician Lin looked at this, and his brow furrowed slightly.

Beside him, Yueleng said quietly, "My lady has vomited blood several times before now. We ask the imperial physician to please take a thorough look."

Yueleng's voice was thick with suppressed grief, and there were tears in her eyes. Imperial Physician Lin glanced at the little serving girl, saw what appeared to be a long-standing illness, and felt a twinge of concern. He hastened to take the pulse.

When he had finished, he released her hand and thought for a moment before turning to Yueleng and saying, "These next few days, Third Miss Shen should rest thoroughly. She must on no account allow herself to be disturbed emotionally. I'll study the matter and formulate a prescription when I return, and have it sent to the mansion."

Yueleng asked no further questions. She made the proper courtesies and saw Imperial Physician Lin out, thinking he would probably be going to the Second Courtyard next to deliver his findings.

When Imperial Physician Lin entered the palace, he went first to find Song Zhang.

Song Zhang was currently occupied with arranging the Emperor's winter hunt—selecting certain personal guards to accompany the party. When he saw Imperial Physician Lin approach, he beckoned him forward.

Imperial Physician Lin looked at the row of towering imperial guards lined up before Song Zhang, every one of them armed and standing with solemn authority, and could not help but soften his footsteps. He came before Song Zhang and bowed with his hands clasped. "General Song."

Song Zhang cut straight to the point. "How is she?"

Imperial Physician Lin replied, "From the pulse, Third Miss Shen's left cun position is weak and the qi movement deficient—this indicates illness born of accumulated grief. While there are supplementing medicines, they should not be administered abruptly; what is needed is gradual regulation."

"I will study the formula when I return and compound it into pills, which will be easier for Third Miss Shen to take."

Song Zhang recalled that this morning Minghe had mentioned the physician yesterday had also said Shen Weici's condition stemmed from accumulated unhappiness—in other words, she had simply been made miserable.

He looked at Imperial Physician Lin. "How many days until she's better?"

Imperial Physician Lin thought for a moment and replied, "Two to three days to compound the pills. If Third Miss Shen responds well, I can prepare more and send them over."

Song Zhang nodded, withdrawing his gaze. "Once they're ready, send someone to collect them."

He casually pulled a small brocade pouch from his person and tossed it to Imperial Physician Lin. His long brows and phoenix eyes settled on the physician with a look of warning. "Make those pills properly. Don't give me any mistakes."

Imperial Physician Lin had come with the intention of currying favour with Song Zhang—he had not expected to receive payment. But looking at those cold eyes, cold sweat broke out down his back; he did not dare demur, and responded repeatedly that he understood, pocketing the pouch.

He thought privately that the way Song Zhang was so attentive to that young lady, there must be some private connection between them. And yet if there were such a connection, how could she be living in such a run-down courtyard? Truly incomprehensible.

Meanwhile, shortly after seeing Imperial Physician Lin off, Madam Wen arrived at Linchun Courtyard with another imperial physician in tow—and the Old Madam had also come along.

Shen Weici was still leaning against the headboard, embroidering the sachet she had yet to finish. When Yueleng came rushing in to tell her, Shen Weici's hands paused and she looked at Yueleng. "Why is another imperial physician here?"

Yueleng was equally puzzled. "I don't know—I only saw him from a distance outside. He's wearing the same robes as the first one, but it's a different person."

"My lady should tidy up quickly—he'll be coming in soon."

Shen Weici heard this and frowned, then said quietly to Yueleng, "Doesn't Hexia have a close friend among the rough-work serving girls of the Third Branch? Tell Hexia to call her to our courtyard to help out—say she's pulling weeds in the garden. Then lead them to work beneath the window, and try to make sure that girl can hear what the Old Madam and Madam Wen say inside."

Yueleng heard this and immediately nodded.

Shen Weici quickly tucked her needlework under the pillow, and had just looked up when the inner curtain was swept aside in one swift motion—and Madam Wen came in, supporting the Old Madam, followed by Shen Zhaozao.

Shen Weici gripped her handkerchief and looked at Madam Wen. She gave a small cough and began to push herself upright to pay her respects.

The Old Madam saw Shen Weici's weak state and then noticed the bloodstain on the collar of her thin undergarment. Her expression became heavy and subdued. "You needn't get up—stay lying down."

Shen Weici settled back against the headboard. "Thank you for your mercy, Old Madam."

The word 'mercy' made the Old Madam's expression darken even further.

She did not know who had let it spread, but the servants throughout the Marquis Mansion were now all talking about what had happened the day before, whispering among themselves that she—the Old Madam—was heartless, that she had schemed against her own grandchild, had gone out of her way to flatter the Zhang family, and driven Shen Weici to vomit blood and faint, nearly costing the girl her life.

The serving girls who had witnessed Shen Weici vomiting blood were numerous, and Zhang Tingyi's arrival with a matchmaker had been seen by many as well—and so the story had spread.

That morning, the Old Madam had heard her serving women recount the servants' gossip, and in her fury had ordered all the serving girls who had been in the main reception hall that day dragged out and given twenty strokes of the rod.

But once a story is told, it cannot be untold. She could not rod every single serving girl in the entire mansion, so she could only issue an order forbidding anyone to speak of it further.

First Master had also come by that morning to say the matter had been badly handled and would invite censure from outsiders—that if the girl were simply to have been married off, that would have been one thing; but first tearing apart her betrothal and then forcing her on someone else made it impossible to contain the talk, and would cost the Marquis Mansion its face.

The Old Madam had nearly vomited blood herself from the aggravation.

Madam Wen, looking at Shen Weici, was barely containing the urge to drag her out of bed by force. The stories circulating through the mansion had made her look even worse—a wicked stepmother who abused her concubine-daughter, and now the story about cutting off her coal supply had come out as well, painting her as a venomous woman.

The Third Branch had even come around first thing that morning to gloat, murmuring the gossip into her ear with a tone that dripped with barbs.

But she could only endure it for now. The imperial physician was still outside—if she made a scene in front of him and it got out, there would be no way to recover from that either.

The Old Madam sat with a heavy expression, her piercing eyes fixed on Shen Weici as though trying to see straight through her. After a long pause, she said at last, "Bring the imperial physician in."

chapters.title: Coercion
chapters.content:
From the expressions on the Old Madam's and Madam Wen's faces, Shen Weici could already tell they were suppressing their anger.

She knew the gossip had already spread through the mansion. What it had reached of the world outside, she did not yet know.

But only when the talk beyond the walls spread wide enough might she have a chance of escaping the fate of marrying Zhang Tingyi.

Hearing the Old Madam's word, Shen Weici asked Yueleng to draw the curtains, then extended one hand outside.

While the imperial physician took her pulse, Madam Wen stood to one side, watching with rigid attention, terrified of some deception slipping past her.

And yet—he was a palace physician. It was unlikely Shen Weici had the means to fool one of them.

Besides, he had already heard from Chief Imperial Physician Lin when he returned. Imperial Physician Lin had seemed a little taken aback when the Jian'an Marquis Mansion sent for him too—and had carefully told him to simply say what he himself had said: no need to examine afresh. Their accounts must align, to show that Lin's original diagnosis had been correct.

Imperial Physician Lin was his teacher. He naturally took his teacher's word as law, and this visit would be easy enough to manage.

He repeated what Imperial Physician Lin had already diagnosed, then added, "Third Miss Shen's condition of vomiting blood is something that has built up over time. When the liver becomes agitated, coughing blood is not uncommon—it is a typical manifestation of qi deficiency combined with bodily weakness."

"Furthermore, Third Miss Shen has always had a constitution prone to cold. Only gradual regulation will help."

These words differed little from what the civilian physician had said the day before—both attributed the vomiting blood to emotional suppression. The implication of why was left unstated but perfectly understood.

Madam Wen's expression shifted unpleasantly. She looked toward the Old Madam. Before the imperial physician, the Old Madam had resumed her gracious manner, and she asked, "Can this condition threaten her life?"

The imperial physician paused briefly, then replied, "Vomiting blood is in itself a symptom that arises under acute distress. If the liver blood surges too forcefully upward during a fainting spell, it is not beyond the realm of possibility that it could prove life-threatening."

The Old Madam sighed, then asked the physician, "Can it be cured entirely?"

The imperial physician replied, "This type of condition ultimately comes down to excessive anxiety. As long as the mind is kept at peace, and the body is supported with tonics, it can gradually improve."

The Old Madam nodded and said, "Then please write out a prescription."

The physician, per his teacher's instructions, said, "The prescription will require some careful study when I return before I can formulate it. I will have it sent to the mansion."

Only then did the Old Madam nod and tell one of her serving girls to see the imperial physician out.

The moment the physician left, the Old Madam's sternness returned in full force. She had the serving women pull the curtains back open again, and asked Shen Weici directly, "Asking you to go to the Zhang household as a new wife—is that so wrongful to you?"

"So wrongful it has filled your heart with bitterness, and made you vomit blood?"

"The whole mansion is now speaking of how heartless this Old Madam is. Are you satisfied now?"

As she spoke, she struck the ground with her walking stick—one blow after another, each one ringing out like a blade driving into the floor.

Not one word of concern was in the Old Madam's tone, nor any trace of the warmth she had shown when she first took Shen Weici's hand to speak with her. What was there now was only a cutting, merciless accusation.

The message was plain: she should not have vomited blood; she should not have given the servants cause to gossip.

Shen Weici, though she saw clearly the nature of these people, arranged her features into an expression of frailty. Tears brimmed in her eyes as she pressed her handkerchief to them, and she choked out, her voice barely audible, "I only just woke this morning—I have no idea what is being said outside."

"And as for yesterday's vomiting—it was entirely beyond my control. If the Old Madam wishes to punish me, I accept it fully. Whatever Old Madam decides, I have no second word to say."

Shen Weici had been born with a delicately slender frame that stirred instinctive protectiveness in those who saw it. In her thin white garments, dark hair flowing loose, tears glimmering in her eyes, handkerchief raised to her face—she looked as though the next gust of wind through the window might carry her away.

Looking at her like this, who could not feel pity?

She had only yesterday vomited blood. If the Old Madam were to punish someone still lying in a sickbed today, who knew what the servants would be calling her by now.

The Old Madam wanted to lash out and discipline her, but found she could not. Watching Shen Weici wipe her tears and cough now and then, pale as a consumptive beauty—even she could see that if this girl were sent to Zhang Tingyi's household in this condition, she wouldn't last long.

But with things already set in motion, Zhang Tingyi could not be offended. One wrong move could trip up Shen Rongshen's official career—and First Master would probably be no match for the fallout. She had no choice but to steel herself and send the girl through.

At any rate, Shen Weici had not been diagnosed with anything incurable. As long as she could be regulated, it would do.

The Old Madam had no wish to waste any more words on Shen Weici. She gave her a cold look. "You've just taken ill—what would I punish you for?"

"But now that Zhang Tingyi has come to propose, that means he has chosen you."

"Rest and recover these next few days. Once you are well, the betrothal will be settled."

Then the Old Madam's gaze settled on Shen Weici intently. "Remember this: you are a young lady of the Marquis Mansion now. No matter whom you are to marry, the Marquis Mansion must give its consent."

"If you behave yourself, I will provide you a dowry. But if you have any other ideas in your head—do not expect me to show the slightest consideration then. Any thoughts of entering the Yiyong Earl's Mansion you can forget right now. Do you understand?"

Shen Weici, hearing the Old Madam's words, let her shoulders sag and drew in on herself slightly, her eyes showing a flicker of fear. She answered hoarsely, "I understand everything."

Having made her display of authority and seen Shen Weici's frightened, cowed expression—as though she had been sufficiently intimidated into compliance—the Old Madam's temper eased a fraction. She pulled her sleeves together and led the whole procession out with sweeping grandeur.

Madam Wen was the last to leave. She walked to Shen Weici's bedside and looked down at her from above, her expression carrying unmistakable contempt. "Don't try any more tricks in front of me. Giving you to Zhang Tingyi is the Master's wish as well."

"The Old Madam just made things perfectly clear. Once you're better, I'll take you to Zhang Tingyi's to apologize in person. Understood?"

Shen Weici's face was the very picture of docile submission—eyes glistening with tears, biting at the corner of her lip, head bowed. She nodded with a small sound of assent. She looked as though she had already given in.

Madam Wen was satisfied with Shen Weici's performance. When all was said and done, Shen Weici had come to the Marquis Mansion with nothing—she could only be bent to its will, bent to Madam Wen's will.

A concubine's daughter with no background, no connections—what waves could she possibly make?

Madam Wen gave a light sniff, pulled her sleeves together, and swept out with her chin high.

chapters.title: There Are No Walls Without Cracks
chapters.content:
The moment Madam Wen was gone, Shen Weici lowered the handkerchief from her eyes and leaned back against the headboard.

Yueleng, watching from the courtyard as Madam Wen swept out with her retinue of serving girls and women, came hurrying inside.

She went to Shen Weici's bedside, her face full of worry. "My lady, now the Old Madam, Madam Wen, and Second Master all want you to marry Zhang Tingyi. Is there any way out of this? If you stay sick too long, the Old Madam and Madam Wen are sure to grow suspicious."

Shen Weici looked at Yueleng quietly. "Did the Third Branch serving girl hear clearly what the Old Madam and Madam Wen said?"

Yueleng nodded. "She heard everything perfectly from under the window. She even whispered to Hexia afterward that Madam Wen had gone too far."

She looked at Shen Weici with some puzzlement. "Is my lady hoping she'll carry the talk to others?"

Shen Weici leaned against the headboard and nodded. "That girl came over to help at my courtyard. She'll have to say something to Third Madam before she goes. Once she's back, Third Madam will surely ask her what happened here, and she'll want to know what the Old Madam and Madam Wen came to say."

"I vomited blood and was taken to my sickbed over all this, and yet the Old Madam and Madam Wen came rushing here to press me into marriage—the Third Branch and the Second Branch only get along on the surface. How could they resist pressing their advantage and letting word of this reach beyond the mansion?"

"Using the Third Branch to carry the news is fine by me."

"And if Madam Wen ever traces it back, it was the Third Branch who spread it—Madam Wen may be furious, but she can't exactly go and flog the Third Branch's serving girls directly."

Yueleng nodded in understanding, then said, "But the servants inside the mansion are talking, and yet it doesn't seem to have done much. People outside still don't know."

Shen Weici took the half-finished sachet from under her pillow and spoke softly. "Wait a few more days."

"There are no walls without cracks. Gossip this good travels faster than one expects."

Yueleng murmured in agreement.

During the two days that Shen Weici was confined to bed, aside from Madam Wen and the Old Madam's visit on the first day, the only callers were Shen Yueshu and Shen Mingqiu of the Third Branch.

Shen Weici was mildly surprised that the two of them had come—but from the looks on their faces when they entered her room, they had not been expecting her courtyard to be so bare.

Shen Weici thought: a visit from the Third Branch was not a bad thing.

She called Yueleng to pour tea for the two of them, then looked at their faces—warm with genuine concern—and propped herself up with a little difficulty, offering a rueful apology. "Two younger sisters have come to see me, and I cannot even rise to greet you. Forgive me."

Shen Mingqiu quickly got up and came to press gently on Shen Weici's shoulder. "Third Elder Sister is ill—we could never expect her to come and receive us."

Shen Weici let her brows fall into a gentle furrow, her eyes heavy with unspoken sorrow. She coughed twice, softly.

Shen Mingqiu looked at Shen Weici's face. She had at first thought the vomiting blood had been somewhat too sudden to be entirely credible—but seeing Shen Weici's sickly look today, she felt that anyone who had found herself in such a situation could easily be driven to bring up blood.

And then there was Shen Weici's appearance—her dark hair tumbled to one side over her shoulder, a redness at the corner of each eye, her lips pale, her beauty at once poignant and arresting. The blood stain at her collar was startling against the pallor of the rest of her. Pale skin and vivid colour together—even the words 'peerless beauty' felt insufficient by two parts. Shen Mingqiu found herself staring.

To think that the Yiyong Earl's Mansion had been ready to propose, yet they refused, and instead wanted to give such a person to Zhang Tingyi—the Second Branch had a truly merciless heart.

Another soft, slight cough brought her back. She could not help but say with feeling, "Third Elder Sister was born with such a face—to be given to the Zhang family is a waste."

Shen Weici said quietly, "I am only a concubine's daughter. I can only follow my stepmother's lead. I dare not ask for too much—as long as I have somewhere to rest my feet, it is enough."

Shen Mingqiu, also a concubine's daughter, heard Shen Weici's words and felt a worried pang for her own future. With something of the feeling of two people sharing the same fate, she said softly, "Are you and I not in the same position—our marriages beyond our own control?"

She looked at Shen Weici. "Is Third Elder Sister truly resigned to this?"

Shen Weici sank softly into the cushions, her pale slender fingers tightening around her handkerchief, her gentle eyes meeting Shen Mingqiu's. "What is there to do but accept it? The Marquis Mansion took me in—that in itself is more than I can be grateful enough for. I dare not ask for anything more."

Shen Mingqiu gazed at Shen Weici's face, struck by how unreasonably gentle she seemed.

She said in a low voice, "Marrying into the Zhang household is a matter that touches Third Elder Sister's entire life. Does Elder Sister truly not feel even a trace of resentment?"

Shen Weici managed a wan smile. "How could I not feel it—of course I am grieved in my heart. But I have accepted it. Once I make peace with it, that will be that."

At this point, Fifth Miss Shen Yueshu cut in. "I certainly wouldn't accept it. If they really married me off to some old man, I'd rather die."

Shen Weici gave a soft, forlorn laugh. "With a body like mine, death and life are not so different."

Shen Mingqiu looked at Shen Weici's frail frame, which seemed to have grown even thinner since she last saw her. She thought of what she had heard the day before—that the Old Madam and Second Madam had come to press her into marriage while she lay ill in bed—and felt genuinely sorry for her.

Being a concubine's daughter herself, she could not help feeling a certain kinship.

She did not know what fate awaited her when she came of age—only that she was fortunate not to have Shen Weici's beauty. Perhaps that was a blessing.

Coming out from Shen Weici's courtyard, she looked back once at the desolate little yard, and in the deepest part of her heart, her contempt for the Second Branch had grown into something permanent.

Even concubine-born daughters in a great family were to be properly raised and cared for. Compared to daughters of the main line, they might have somewhat weaker maternal connections, and slightly fewer prospects in marriage—but it was not so very different. For the Second Branch to treat their concubine-born daughter this way, every word of those mansion rumours was true. They fully deserved to be called venomous.

Shen Zhaozao was waiting for them not far away. Seeing Shen Mingqiu and Shen Yueshu approaching, she hurried over. "Well? Is Shen Weici planning more tricks? I've long suspected she's been putting it all on. All those stories about the Second Branch flooding the mansion—it has to be her spreading them."

Shen Zhaozao had been seething inside, but her mother had told her not to go to Linchun Courtyard looking for trouble. If she let her temper fly and made a scene, with Shen Weici in her sickbed, the rumours would only get worse, and the Old Madam would scold her too. So she had found Shen Mingqiu and Shen Yueshu and sent them instead to find out what they could.

Shen Mingqiu had now seen how Shen Weici was living in Linchun Courtyard, and seen how the Second Branch had driven her into that state—and looking at Shen Zhaozao's expression now, she felt only contempt and disgust.

Always so self-important, always assuming the privileges of the main-line daughter, looking down on everyone, treating her and her younger sister as creatures to summon and dismiss as she pleased, as though being concubine-born meant they were there to do her bidding. It was insufferable.

When she got back, she was going to stoke the fire further—have her people carry the Second Branch's dirty business to the world outside, and cut Shen Zhaozao down to size.

But her face remained pleasant as she said softly to Shen Zhaozao, "Second Elder Sister is overthinking it. I went and spoke with Third Elder Sister just now—she seems genuinely very ill. You'd see it too if you went in person; even I found it difficult to look at."

"And Third Elder Sister has always had a gentle, fragile nature, and her health has never been good. After all that has happened, vomiting blood is not so strange."

"Besides—Third Elder Sister is just someone your mother can dispose of as she pleases, isn't that right? You and Second Madam always treated her as a concubine's daughter without any real standing. She just now admitted it herself and said she's accepted her fate. What is there for Second Elder Sister to be afraid of?"

Shen Zhaozao heard this and looked sharply at Shen Mingqiu's face—if she hadn't worn that same accommodating expression she always put on, Shen Zhaozao might almost have thought she was being mocked.

chapters.title: Going to the Earl's Mansion to Return His Things
chapters.content:
She gave a cold sniff. "She may be easy to handle, but right now the whole mansion is gossiping about the Second Branch, and my mother's reputation has been dragged through the mud. If I ever find out it was her spreading things, I'll make her pay for it."

Shen Mingqiu smiled. "But didn't Second Elder Sister already look into it? After the incident, Third Elder Sister never left Linchun Courtyard, and all the serving girls stayed quietly inside too—they haven't been anywhere. Where would they go to spread anything?"

She had almost gone on to add: if you don't want others to know, don't do it in the first place—but she swallowed it back down in the end.

Shen Zhaozao's gaze turned icy. "If not for the fact that she knows better than to let her girls run their mouths, I'd have had her flayed by now."

Shen Mingqiu let out a private, cold laugh. Shen Zhaozao was exactly this way—eternally convinced of her own superiority as the main-line daughter, as though the whole world was hers to command.

She smiled outwardly. "Second Elder Sister is the main-line daughter, and naturally Third Elder Sister would not dare be presumptuous in front of her."

Shen Zhaozao, mollified fractionally by this, gave one more cold snort, then stopped paying attention to Shen Mingqiu and walked off, pulling her serving girls behind her.

Shen Mingqiu stood and watched Shen Zhaozao's retreating back, contempt clear in her eyes.

The serving girl beside her couldn't help leaning forward. "Second Miss is truly too overbearing."

Shen Mingqiu's expression grew serious. "Did you hear everything that was said in Third Elder Sister's room today? We need more people to know about this. When you go back, pass it around the courtyard, and anyone visiting family should say it too. We might as well make the Second Branch sound like man-eating demons."

With that, she looked away from Shen Zhaozao's imperious, retreating figure and walked back with her girls.

On her side of things, the moment Shen Mingqiu was gone, Shen Weici let her guard drop, and stretched her fingers toward the bedside brazier, her expression drifting slightly.

After a moment she spoke to Yueleng. "Tell the girls in the courtyard not to bring up this matter anymore from now on—we're in the Second Branch after all, and Madam Wen can discipline any of my girls whenever she pleases. For these few days, no one should be going out; the Second Branch may well be keeping an eye on what moves in and out of my courtyard."

Yueleng nodded, brought Shen Weici a cup of hot tea, and then could not help but ask, "Is Young Master Zhang ever going to come and propose? There's been no news at all."

Shen Weici was quiet for a moment, then said softly, "After Father gets back this afternoon, you go to the Tingzhu Study and find him. Say you have a folk remedy for liver stagnation that I took back in Yuyang which gave some improvement—ask permission to leave the mansion and buy the herbs yourself, because you'd feel better choosing them personally."

"Once Father agrees, take everything Young Master Zhang gave me and go out. Head to the Yiyong Earl's Mansion and find Young Master Zhang. You must see him in person, and then return everything to him."

Yueleng looked startled. "My lady wants to return everything? Maybe Young Master Zhang has just been held up by something."

Shen Weici's pale face looked at Yueleng. "I've written to him, and he hasn't replied to a single letter all this time. He doesn't say if he's coming and he doesn't say why he isn't."

"If he had difficulties, he could have told me—I would not have clung to him stubbornly. If he was hesitating, I'm not going to wait for him anymore."

"When you go, say only that you're returning his things. He will understand what I mean. If he refuses to take them back, he'll give you an explanation. Whatever reason he gives, just come home and tell me."

"If he accepts them back, I understand what that means too. There's no need to say anything further. Once the things are given back, that's the end of it—don't say anything unkind. We'd both only lose face."

"My plan was to use the outside pressure to make Madam Wen and the Old Madam agree to my marrying Young Master Zhang, and so escape Zhang Tingyi. But if Young Master Zhang is wavering—or has other options—I'll simply have to find another way. Whatever you do, don't start an argument with anyone."

Yueleng quickly nodded. "My lady, don't worry—I'll be very careful with how I speak."

Shen Weici was reassured. She sat up and brought out everything Zhang Yuanheng had given her.

The jade pendant and earrings he had sent, and the calligraphy copy—she had kept everything in perfect condition. She had even kept every one of Zhang Yuanheng's letters.

Yueleng asked, "Should the letters all be returned too?"

Shen Weici had intended to do so, but after a moment's thought said, "Keep the letters for now. People's hearts are unpredictable—I'm afraid something he once said might be used against me later. The letters would be good to have as evidence."

"Though Young Master Zhang doesn't seem like that sort of person, Song Zhang mentioned something about him having accepted two servant girls. I don't know if that's true. And he made a promise, yet kept neither coming nor writing. I can't trust him entirely anymore."

"I have no intention of using the letters to harm him. I'm only keeping them as a safeguard."

Yueleng nodded, looking somewhat desolately at the boxes arranged on the table.

Just a few days ago, she had thought good days were right around the corner—that her young lady was about to become the proper mistress of an earl's mansion, finally standing on solid ground. Now it felt like it had all been a dream.

Shen Weici's fingers traced the finely carved lid of the box, and then she looked out the window.

That afternoon, Yueleng came back from the Tingzhu Study and immediately reported that Second Master's expression had been unpleasant.

Shen Weici kept working on the sachet and asked, "Did Father agree?"

Yueleng went to pick up the box from the writing table and nodded. "Second Master agreed—but his face was very dark. When I arrived, standing outside the door, I heard him throw something on the floor, like he was furious about something—I was so startled I almost didn't dare go in."

"And then when I went in, I saw Second Master pacing and pacing around the room, and every once in a while he'd slam the table hard. The boys serving him were so frightened they didn't dare look up."

"Luckily when I spoke up, Second Master didn't give me any trouble. He only asked two questions about my lady's health, and then gave me his pass token and let me go."

She looked curiously at Shen Weici. "I've always seen Second Master looking mild and good-tempered—he's never had a fit like this. What's set him off so badly this time?"

Shen Weici glanced at Yueleng and said simply, "Never mind what it's about—just remember what I told you to do."

She added softly, "Father is already back, so Young Master Zhang should have finished his duties too. Tidy yourself up and take Hexia with you. I'd rather not have you going alone—I'm worried something might happen."

"And remember what I said—don't be rash. Come back early."

Yueleng nodded firmly. "My lady, don't worry. I'll do it right. Even if Young Master Zhang has broken his word and doesn't plan to marry my lady anymore, I won't argue with him. I'll give the things back gracefully—my lady doesn't need him anyway."

Shen Weici smiled faintly in spite of herself, then waved her hand gently. "While it's still light out, go now. There should be a carriage—be careful on the road."

Yueleng gave a firm, heavy nod, then wrapped the items carefully in cloth, tucked the bundle tightly in her arms, and went out.

Shen Weici watched Yueleng leave, and the smile that had been on her face a moment before faded away.

chapters.title: Running into Song Zhang at the Earl's Mansion
chapters.content:
In the main reception room of the Yiyong Earl's Mansion, Song Qingxiu leaned back in his chair and said to Zhang Ping in an unhurried tone, "I have come today with all sincerity—and because I believe young Yuanheng is a man of substance. Once this match is settled between our families, we become relatives by marriage. Naturally I'll be pulling him along where I can."

Zhang Ping smiled warmly in return. "We are deeply honoured by Lord Song's favour. My Yuanheng would be most fortunate to take your esteemed daughter as his wife."

Song Zhang sat beside Song Qingxiu and glanced at Zhang Yuanheng, whose mind was clearly elsewhere, then smiled toward Zhang Ping. "Within and beyond the capital, there are many who seek to form ties with the Song family. My acquaintance with the Zhang family makes us already close—once this match between Yuanheng and my third uncle's daughter is settled, we'll be family, and even closer than before."

Zhang Ping, hearing Song Zhang speak up as well, felt a surge of honoured disbelief.

The Duke of Song's Mansion had stood for a century, producing illustrious generals generation after generation, always the Emperor's most trusted household, holding military power with the authority the Emperor himself had conferred. Even those who sought to undermine them had never succeeded. And with the Emperor dependent on the Duke's Mansion to guard the frontier, and this generation's Song Zhang being a rare talent—Song Zhang recalled to the capital and placed in command of the imperial guard, with influence that made even the Prime Minister tread carefully—an alliance with the Song family meant rapid advancement, and the chance to restore the long-diminished Earl's Mansion to prominence in the capital.

Even though Song Qingxiu was not from the main line of the Duke's Mansion and had not followed the family tradition of military service, taking a literary official's path instead—that in itself showed the Duke's Mansion reaching into the civil world of the court, and with the Emperor's trust, the Song family was the most formidable of the great houses.

Even for a daughter born of a concubine, other great families would be competing to seek the match.

He had never expected the Song family to come to them on their own initiative. A few days ago, when a messenger from Song Qingxiu had arrived early in the morning, he had thought he was dreaming—and now that Song Qingxiu and Song Zhang had come in person, he finally felt it was real.

He said quickly to Song Zhang, "It is Yuanheng's good fortune to be acquainted with General Song."

Song Qingxiu straightened in his chair, glanced at Zhang Yuanheng, who had not said a word, and then looked back at Zhang Ping. "Then let's consider the matter settled."

Zhang Ping was smiling, about to agree at once—when Zhang Yuanheng suddenly rose to his feet and bowed deeply toward Song Qingxiu. "Yuanheng is deeply honoured by Lord Song's kindness. However, there is already a woman in my heart to whom I am committed, and I have pledged to go and propose to her very soon. I can only beg Lord Song's forgiveness for failing him."

Zhang Yuanheng bowed with unhurried composure, neither servile nor arrogant. The quiet tenacity of the young man before him made Song Qingxiu regard him with a new kind of respect.

No wonder the Emperor had praised him.

He looked toward Song Zhang with a raised eyebrow, and in the brief exchange of glances between the two, a meaning passed that only the two of them could fully interpret.

Song Zhang sent Song Qingxiu a look in return, then let his leisurely gaze settle on Zhang Yuanheng. He watched him keeping his head bowed—even as his father tugged at his arm, Zhang Yuanheng made no move to straighten—and a distinct displeasure rose in Song Zhang's eyes.

He had come with goodwill and been rebuffed.

He gave a thin, cold smile toward Zhang Ping. "In all these years, no one has ever turned the Song family down."

"We came with genuine intention, and if the Earl's Mansion is not willing to receive it, there is nothing to be done. We would not press an unwilling man, naturally."

"I'll give you a few days to think it over. If Zhang Yuanheng refuses to agree in the end, then let this matter drop entirely."

Zhang Ping, seeing Song Zhang's expression, was frightened. He was afraid of some invisible obstacle being quietly placed in their path, and quickly moved forward. "General Song misunderstands. Yuanheng has always been inflexible in his nature—but there is no woman in his life, and he was merely talking nonsense just now. This match..."

Before Zhang Ping could finish, Zhang Yuanheng's voice cut through.

"Father."

"I have never spoken in jest. I told Father clearly several days ago, and however long Father delays, however many days he puts it off—my mind is made up. I will not break my word."

Song Zhang looked up at Zhang Yuanheng, his naturally stern, cold face growing even more impassive.

Song Qingxiu stood. He addressed Zhang Ping: "Since the young master is unwilling, the matter ends here."

His expression too had soured. He turned and looked at Song Zhang. "The Earl's Mansion doesn't know what it's rejecting. We've come all this way for nothing."

Song Zhang gave Zhang Yuanheng one last cold look, pressed his lips together, rose, and stepped out of the room first.

Song Qingxiu saw Song Zhang go, gave another cold snort, flicked his sleeve, and followed.

Zhang Ping broke into a cold sweat, his whole body trembling. Neither of these men was someone he could afford to offend.

Never mind that the Duke of Song's Mansion was at the height of its power and prestige—Song Zhang and Song Qingxiu individually were formidable enough. One commanded the imperial guard, and the other was a fourth-rank Zhongshu Councilor and Yuanheng's direct superior. Offending either of them would have consequences.

He looked at the two men's retreating backs and hurried after them, casting furious glances at Zhang Yuanheng and gesturing urgently for him to come and apologize as well.

Zhang Yuanheng looked at his father's cringing, obsequious posture, and stood coldly in place without moving.

Zhang Ping let out a long, despairing sigh. He gave up on Zhang Yuanheng opening his eyes to sense and rushed out after the departing men.

Yueleng was standing at the gate of the Earl's Mansion, holding her wrapped bundle and talking to the gatekeeper boy, asking him to go in and announce her—when she unexpectedly saw Song Zhang walking out of the Earl's Mansion, his expression still darkened. Those cold eyes of his landed directly on her, and she nearly lost her grip on what she was carrying in shock.

The gatekeeper boy was still talking to her. "Miss, you'll have to wait a moment—our Young Master is in a meeting, and I'll go and announce you once he's done."

Yueleng quickly lowered her head and murmured her assent, trying to make herself as small as possible. But the next moment a pair of black boots had appeared right in front of her. She looked up—and found herself looking straight at Song Zhang's cool, impassive face.

Something blocked her throat completely. She stood there blankly for what felt like a very long time before she could manage a word. "Second Young Master."

Song Zhang's gaze fell with mild interest on the bundle Yueleng was holding.

Song Qingxiu, walking behind Song Zhang and seeing him stop in front of some girl, came over and clapped Song Zhang on the shoulder. "Do you know this serving girl?"

Song Zhang looked away from her. "She's from the Jian'an Marquis Mansion."

Song Qingxiu nodded, then turned to Song Zhang. "Going back to the Duke's Mansion?"

At that point, Zhang Ping had rushed out after them, bowing and apologizing repeatedly in front of Song Zhang and Song Qingxiu. "My boy's always been like this—please don't hold it against him. Give him a few more days and he's sure to come around."

Song Qingxiu looked at Zhang Ping. Zhang Ping himself was an honest, unremarkable man with no particular talents—but his son had a certain uncommon quality to him. He would not have considered this match at all if not for the fact that Zhang Yuanheng had the Emperor's favour and an exceptional future ahead, and if not for Song Zhang raising the subject. He had several daughters of his own, and none of them would ever have trouble finding husbands—even the concubine-born ones had great families competing to marry them.

And yet a matter that should have been entirely settled had been turned down flat by Zhang Yuanheng. It was a clean snub to the Duke's Mansion's face. Since they saw no need to save face for themselves, he would not save it for them either. His daughters were not so difficult to marry off.

Song Qingxiu was about to say something cutting about fending for themselves—when Song Zhang spoke, his eyes moving to Yueleng, who stood nearby. "Master Zhang—it seems that serving girl there is looking for you."

Zhang Ping was startled by Song Zhang's words and followed his gaze to a serving girl he did not recognize.

He blinked, then frowned. "Where do you come from? What do you want with me?"

Yueleng's face had gone white. From what she had been overhearing in this conversation, she had gathered that the man now speaking to her must be Young Master Zhang's father.

With so many people around her, she could not very well say she was here to see Young Master Zhang. She kept hoping Song Zhang would leave first—so she stumbled out, "I have mistaken my road."

chapters.title: I Will Not Marry The Third Princess.
chapters.content:
Song Zhang looked at Yueleng once. Tall in his purple official robe, jade crown holding his hair, one hand resting on the hilt of his sword, brows long and phoenix eyes aloft, looking down at her with a haughtily unhurried air. "Mistaken your road?"

"As I understand it, your Third Miss is acquainted with Second Young Master Zhang. I assumed you had come here looking for him."

Beside him, Zhang Ping, hearing Song Zhang's words, immediately guessed at this serving girl's identity. "Are you from the Second Branch of the Jian'an Marquis Mansion?"

Yueleng was pinned by Song Zhang's gaze and could neither deny it nor refuse to answer. She could only bite her teeth and give a stiff, reluctant nod.

Zhang Ping's expression changed.

He cast a careful glance toward Song Zhang and Song Qingxiu beside him, wondering whether they knew yet that his son was interested in a Third Miss of the Jian'an Marquis Mansion. If they had known, they would never have come to propose in the first place.

Only a few days ago, had it not been for Song Qingxiu's sudden message proposing an alliance between the families, he himself had been about to bring a matchmaker to the Jian'an Marquis Mansion. Afterward, weighing the two sides, he had concluded: his son had a brilliant future, with the Emperor's favour, and even the Duke of Song's Mansion had come to seek a connection—did that not prove his son's talents and his prospects at court? For him to marry a girl from the Marquis Mansion who had neither background nor standing and was not even a favoured daughter—it would do nothing to advance his son's career.

Besides, a girl raised from childhood in the countryside was probably not particularly well brought up. He would not have agreed to it at all if his son had not knelt before him and begged.

The Earl's Mansion had long since been in decline, and among all the clan members at court, there was not a single one who could be counted on. His son was the only hope the family had. An alliance with the Duke's Mansion, with his son rising at court, would be the way to lead the family back to its former standing.

These thoughts passed through Zhang Ping's mind as his expression grew heavy. He looked at Yueleng. "My second son is currently discussing a betrothal—I'm afraid he will not have time to visit the Jian'an Marquis Mansion."

"If you have something to say, you may say it directly to me."

Yueleng heard these words and felt as though a great stone had been dropped onto her chest, barely staying on her feet.

'Currently discussing a betrothal'—and 'no time to visit the Jian'an Marquis Mansion.' Slow as she might be, even Yueleng could read what that meant. He was telling her young lady to stop hoping. Otherwise why say he was discussing a betrothal, why say he had no time?

Yueleng did not believe for a moment that Zhang Ping had no idea about his son and her young lady. They had practically already reached the point of discussing a formal proposal—and now hearing all of this, she understood everything.

She knew that her own face was also her young lady's face. She swallowed her grief at once, made her expression cool and collected, and held the bundle forward before Zhang Ping. "These are things Young Master Zhang left behind at the Marquis Mansion. My young lady found them and asked me to return them. Please take them, Master Zhang, and pass them on to Young Master Zhang."

Zhang Ping was taken aback—he had not expected this serving girl to have come to return things. He had assumed she was here to press his son for something.

He took the items, then heard the serving girl's stiff voice: "I have delivered the things to Master Zhang. I will go back now and report to my young lady."

Yueleng finished speaking, turned around, and walked away.

Without a backward glance.

Zhang Ping stared at Yueleng's rapidly retreating back and found himself slow to react.

Song Zhang watched the serving girl's retreating figure with a remote, indifferent gaze. Her face had been barely holding together—and yet the words she had managed to get out had carried their own kind of backbone.

Then Song Qingxiu's voice came from beside him. "Master Zhang needn't bother seeing us out. My daughter is not so difficult to marry off."

"Your son Zhang Yuanheng may have his talents, but he is clearly unable to read a situation. You've wasted our sincerity."

He looked at Zhang Ping. "Moreover, it was you who first gave your consent—which was why I brought my nephew here to discuss things properly. And then to be refused to my face, at my age—this is an insult I won't simply forget."

Zhang Ping was so frightened he nearly fell to his knees, apologizing profusely. "I beg Lord Song to give my boy one more chance. He'll come and apologize in person within a few days, I can assure you."

Song Qingxiu gave a cold snort and paid Zhang Ping no further attention. He lifted the hem of his robe and walked directly away.

Song Zhang followed unhurriedly behind him, and together they got into an ornate carriage waiting at the Earl's Mansion gate.

Inside the carriage, Song Qingxiu looked at Song Zhang. "You're at the Emperor's side often enough—does the Emperor really praise Zhang Yuanheng as much as they say? What kind of temperament is this? I'm having second thoughts about wanting him for a son-in-law."

Song Zhang leaned back against the carriage, his long legs stretched comfortably before him, and smiled. "If Third Uncle finds him unsuitable, then drop the matter. As for Zhang Yuanheng—since he's shown such ingratitude, let him have a lesson."

Song Qingxiu looked at Song Zhang. "Honestly, I do have a certain respect for his character—he's not like the calculating, status-chasing types, and he strikes me as steadfast and reliable. I'd actually feel at ease marrying a daughter to a man like him. Let's wait and see what he has to say for himself when he comes to apologize later."

He then looked at Song Zhang. "Actually—the story going around about the Jian'an Marquis Mansion lately—I've been wanting to ask if it's true."

"They're saying the Second Branch of the Jian'an Marquis Mansion tore apart their own daughter's betrothal for personal gain and sold her off to Zhang Tingyi as a new wife."

"From what I hear, this girl—though she's a concubine's daughter—is exceptionally beautiful, poised, accomplished. And they drove her to vomit blood and faint. The very next day, the Old Madam and the Second Madam went to her sickbed to press her—people are saying they nearly hounded the girl to death."

"Is it true?"

Song Zhang raised an eyebrow calmly. "It's true."

Song Qingxiu frowned immediately. "So the Old Madam of the Jian'an Marquis Mansion is actually like this—and Shen Rongshen always seemed like an upright man. As it turns out, this is what they get up to behind closed doors."

"Watching Zhang Tingyi gain imperial favour and then going out of their way to cozy up to him—even tearing apart their own daughter's betrothal in the process. No wonder the Censorate had people filing accusations against him today."

"Zhang Tingyi has always been flamboyant and has made plenty of enemies. Shen Rongshen insisted on attaching himself to that man—getting called out was only a matter of time."

"Now the Jian'an Marquis Mansion's reputation has taken a serious fall. They'll have plenty to cry about."

"I saw him outside the palace gates today looking like a stray dog, scrambling into his carriage to flee—quite a pitiful sight."

He then looked at Song Zhang. "My guess is he'll be coming to beg help from your First Branch before long."

Song Zhang's gaze was cold. "I won't lift a finger for this."

Song Qingxiu nodded, then said, "This business does have some connection to you, come to think of it. Your mother isn't at the Marquis Mansion right now, so why not simply stay away for the time being—come back to the Duke's Mansion with me today. The Old Madam has been missing you."

Song Zhang turned a small, gold-trimmed dagger over in his fingers and gave Song Qingxiu a mild smile. "I'll make time to visit the Old Madam another day. I have some duties at the Marquis Mansion to take care of."

Song Qingxiu raised an eyebrow. "What duties could possibly require you to stay at the Marquis Mansion?"

"I hear the Emperor gifted you a Loulan princess—and you put her up at the Marquis Mansion. Don't tell me it's the beauty keeping you there."

Song Zhang only smiled, saying nothing.
