"Don't be envious—who else has a son they can barely get a glimpse of once in ten days? Even when I want some motherly warmth and filial conversation, there's no one to be found."

Lady Xie dabbed the corner of her mouth with a handkerchief. Her words were complaints, but the joy in her eyes was plain to see.

The woman who had spoken knew she had hit the mark, and laughed with all the more warmth.

"Easy to fix—have your Young Master marry soon. Then Lady Xie will have someone to talk to morning to night, and once grandchildren come, the household will be even livelier. You won't be able to keep quiet if you tried!"

Lady Xie didn't take up the thread about "marrying," but her gaze drifted once more to Lu Huaixi—and she smiled with a nod.

The matrons seated nearby were waiting for that line about marriage to be picked up. A few of lower standing even hoped to use the moment to suggest their own daughters.

But the woman at the head of the table said nothing—only lifted her teacup and smoothly changed the subject.

Off to one side, Lu Tangshu had also been waiting.

She had been convinced all along that today's gathering was, essentially, a viewing occasion for Xie Yuanjing—so she had deliberately stayed put the whole time, hoping Lady Xie might take note of her, and hoping she might perhaps manage a glimpse of Xie Yuanjing.

And she had glimpsed him. A man of extraordinary presence—like jade and pine on a high mountain, unmatched in looks, cool and untamed.

Lu Tangshu couldn't help the lurch in her chest.

The way to position oneself well wasn't limited to family backing. Being pursued by a formidable man—even if nothing came of it—could still raise one's own standing.

chapters.title: Quite the Expert at Winning People Over
chapters.content:
Lady Liu caught sight of Xie Yuanjing outside a side room toward the end of the gathering.

The man who was not often warm toward others was waiting under the covered walkway—long robes, jade-pinned topknot, a cool arrogance in the set of his brow. Strikingly refined and handsome.

Lady Liu startled.

She glanced back at her daughter, saw the girl had gone momentarily still, and assumed she was just dazzled by Xie Yuanjing's looks.

Not having the heart to scold her, she simply gestured for Xixi to go back to the carriage first.

The second branch hadn't come out yet. Lu Huaixi glanced their way, then stepped up onto the mounting block.

The carriage inside was spacious, but the moment she lifted the curtain, a large object caught her eye.

A brilliant red coral.

"What is this?"

"In reply to Second Young Miss—this was sent over by the eldest young lord of the marquis' household, via a page boy. He said it was to bring some auspicious cheer to the Lady and Young Miss alike."

Coral had long been considered a symbol of good fortune. The larger pieces were especially rare and costly—which was precisely why when Xie Yuanjing had presented a fine coral to his mother at the flower-viewing gathering, every matron in attendance had praised and envied it.

And the piece before her now was clearly no lesser—a pair measured to the same standard.

Lu Huaixi said nothing more. She only stared at the coral in front of her, and slowly, slowly pressed her lips together.

She was taking back what she'd thought back there in the water pavilion.

An old fox was an old fox. Winning people over—he was quite the expert.

As expected, when Lady Liu returned and saw it, she was momentarily taken aback, barely managing to hold her composure. Once told Xie Yuanjing had selected it personally, she gave a satisfied nod.

"One really can't trust rumors."

Lu Huaixi knew exactly what that meant.

Rumors said Xie Yuanjing was difficult, his temperament unpredictable, his methods numerous and ruthless. That when he smiled at someone, it wasn't necessarily goodwill—there was even a chance he was about to wring their neck.

Lu Huaixi shifted to look at her mother, and moved her lips.

A moment passed, as if a thought had surfaced. She said quietly, "Not entirely to be trusted."

Seeing her mother glance over, Lu Huaixi pointed to herself: "Mother was saying the same thing before—that the rumors were right."

The second branch arrived home half an hour after Lu Huaixi.

Lu Tangshu followed her mother into her courtyard. Once the maidservants had withdrawn, she frowned and spoke.

"We stayed the extra time and still couldn't get a single word out of Lady Xie."

"And what word were you hoping for?"

Lady Lu of the second branch, née Luó, let her expression slip a fraction. With no outsiders present, she no longer watched her tongue.

"The Chengen Marquis' household hasn't been what it was. Right now all they have left is a bit of surface dignity. Once your standing is higher, that eldest son of theirs—he may not deserve you anymore!"

"Then why were you so warm to Lady Xie today, Mother?"

Lu Tangshu said flatly, without patience. Xie Yuanjing's image from the gathering kept reappearing in her mind.

"And besides—never mind how far the marquis' household has fallen. Where could it fall to? Let's not forget the Xie family has produced two empresses. And even now, even with the Marquis out of the Emperor's favor, Xie Yuanjing has never been stripped of any of his authority."

"Two empresses—what use are they now?"

Lady Luo had no interest in quarreling over that.

"If you truly like the Xie eldest son, wait two more years. Once Lu Huaixi's situation is resolved, let her elevate your standing a little. If the marquis' household rises, you'll be marrying into glory. If it doesn't rise—you can still make another choice."

Lu Tangshu didn't argue back.

She did have some feeling for Xie Yuanjing—but she also saw things clearly. Compared to marrying into a household that might never recover, having Xie Yuanjing drawn to her—even if nothing came of it—might serve her better.

But she didn't feel like thinking it through now.

There was something else that bothered her more.

"I still don't understand—why are you so set on getting Lu Huaixi into the palace? If she actually becomes a consort, I'd have to bow my head to her for the rest of my life. Why should she have that?"

"Why should she? Because the Lu family gains influence through it, and your standing gets lifted because of her."

"Grandfather always plays favorites—any influence the Lu family gains goes to First Uncle's branch. How much would actually reach us? And Lu Huaixi—she can't compose poems, can't paint, can't do any of it. Favored by the Emperor? Just because of her face?"

"I keep telling you that head of yours doesn't think—all these years and you've only learned the pretty surface of things."

Lady Luo shot a look at her daughter, pressing down her impatience.

"That face of hers is more than enough! The moment she earns favor, the Emperor's benevolence will extend to the Lu family—even a small gesture from the palace is imperial grace. People everywhere will come seeking to ingratiate themselves. Then you tell me who controls what inside the Lu family—it doesn't matter."

"And if she doesn't earn favor—if she dies in the palace?"

The word "dies" came out of Lu Tangshu's mouth with an odd savoring quality, a crease between her brows that somehow also held a strange anticipation.

"If she doesn't earn favor—"

Lady Luo smiled at her daughter.

"With the Lu family's backing, she'll earn favor. Dying is possible—but if she's killed by someone, then whoever is on the throne owes a debt, and the Lu family will still receive recompense. They still get elevated. Whatever the outcome, you come out ahead. Understand?"

Lu Tangshu understood.

Not only did she understand that Lu Huaixi simply had to enter the palace, she also understood that the moment Lu Huaixi became someone belonging to the Emperor—the Lu family would have only one legitimate daughter left.

And that would be her.

Any other Lu daughter would come below her in standing.

Anyone who wanted to attach themselves to the Lu family—even those seeking to flatter the first branch—would still have to consider her.

"Then... Mother, is it certain that Lu Huaixi will definitely enter the palace?"

"It is. Who else—who would dare make a match with her once the news is out? And another thing—why did you have that He family boy's portrait sent over? He's already engaged. If that caused a scene and your grandfather found out, there'd be trouble!"

"It was He Jianxing who asked me to do it."

Lu Tangshu pursed her lips. "I just wanted to give Lu Huaixi some grief. I won't do it again."

Afterward, she'd only be hoping for Lu Huaixi to enter the palace. And if she was lucky—

The thought surfaced, complicated with it, an unacknowledged darkness growing in her heart.

Though it troubled her, she had truly been thinking it: that Lu Huaixi might be killed by someone inside the palace.

"Killed? She won't be. With the Lu family there, she can't not earn favor."

Lady Luo rose, cutting off that line of thought, with no wish to dwell on it.

"She's still family. Use your head and keep up a close rapport with her. There's plenty of benefit ahead."

"I know, your daughter isn't foolish."

chapters.title: Who Would Marry You at a Time Like This?
chapters.content:
At the Chengen Marquis' household, Xie Yuanjing had been kept behind by his mother.

The hall held that eye-catching coral—brilliant red and festive.

"How did you end up coming back today? Wasn't the assignment complicated?"

His mother sipped her tea, watching her son summon someone to bring ice. She wanted to stop him—but in the end only let out a sigh.

"It really is past time to settle your marriage. At least then there'd be someone to look after you."

Xie Yuanjing gave a languid smile and reached to pour his own tea.

He filled it only halfway—leaving space.

"But you rushed into this engagement so suddenly, and you won't have a proper ceremony—I can't quite shake a feeling of unease. Tell me honestly: was this truly your own idea?"

On the day the arrangement with the Lu family was finalized, Xie Yuanjing hadn't even returned to the estate.

Lady Xie, unable to find him, had only heard the confirmed news from the Old Master himself.

She'd had no chance to say a word about the timing being too rushed before the Old Master instructed that the matter not be made public.

Even the wedding was to be handled discreetly. Lady Xie could not feel this was a happy event.

"The Lu second daughter has a lovely face—gentle and sweet, like a celestial being when she sits there. But—"

Lady Xie paused and chose her words carefully. "But she is truly quite young. A hasty marriage is not good for her."

"She is young—rushing into a wedding doesn't suit her. That's why the date on the betrothal contract was moved forward by a year. And after the wedding, I won't rush her into having children early. So Mother, please don't press on that."

Shortly, a maidservant brought in chipped ice. Xie Yuanjing took it and began nudging pieces slowly into his teacup.

"Mother, going forward, please don't lend your ear to rumors outside. She is marrying in—she will be family. There's no sense in repeating outsiders' gossip about one's own people."

"I'm not talking ill of her—I'm..."

Lady Xie couldn't help knitting her brow. "I'm only saying this to you. To outsiders—do you think I'd say anything so careless?"

"Mother should bear with it—don't say it to me either."

"You really are..."

Lady Xie's words were blocked back in her throat. She collected herself before saying, helplessly:

"Fine, fine. I won't say anything. But if you're truly going to shield that Lu girl so fiercely, then take this marriage seriously. Anyone looking at this household and seeing no hint of celebration, and then suddenly a wife appears—they'll assume your wife has no favor at all."

Something shifted in Xie Yuanjing at last.

He took a sip of his newly cooled tea, and his brow faintly tightened, barely perceptible.

"And—the household knows you've gotten engaged, but not to whom. Your grandmother's intentions are plain enough to you. That one has been hoping for an opening for a long time—I imagine she's looking to use it to have you take that girl in as well—"

"Looking for an opening?"

Xie Yuanjing cut his mother off directly. "She might as well save herself the trouble and die. It would be faster."

"Don't upset your grandmother—if you actually make a move, and your grandmother takes ill over it, the whole wedding with the Lu family might fall through."

Xie Yuanjing said nothing. The hall chilled in an instant, a heaviness pressing through the air.

Lady Xie was about to urge him to endure it through this period when she heard the person before her say with deliberate calm: "Let her try. Let her see how much reach the marquis' household has left—to come between me and my wedding."

Lady Xie's heart lurched. She wasn't quite certain whether her son's "her" meant the Old Madam—or the female cousin residing in the household.

"I only meant for you to keep an eye on things. Was there any need to—"

"My Lady, the Third Madam has come with the young miss."

The maidservant's voice cut in from outside. "They say they've come to drink tea with you, and to take a look at the new coral you've received."

Hearing the words "young miss," Lady Xie instinctively looked at her son.

They must have gotten word that he was here, and couldn't restrain themselves any longer—using any excuse to come and show themselves to the first branch.

She had no desire to upset the Old Madam, but her son's wishes mattered more. And that young miss was no simple creature, either—Lady Xie didn't particularly like her.

"Not today—I'm feeling a little tired. Another time, I'll invite Second Sister-in-law and Third Sister-in-law for a proper visit."

The words made no mention of the young miss. The maidservant nodded and was about to withdraw.

But then, the man who hadn't looked up called the maidservant back.

"The first branch's courtyard is not open to outsiders without cause. If Third Aunt wishes to come for tea, she comes alone."

The words left no face unsaved. But Lady Xie understood he couldn't be blamed—there had been incidents before, caused by someone with unusually thick skin.

After lingering a little longer—drinking some of the freshly cooled tea—Xie Yuanjing rose and left.

Outside the courtyard, a few servants were passing by. Catching sight of him, they immediately lowered their eyes and stepped aside, not daring to move without permission.

Walking behind him was his trusted man, Gong Fei.

Having just overheard Lady Xie's words of reproach, he found it hard to hold back something he wanted to say.

"Master, why not tell Lady Xie plainly that this marriage is nothing more than—"

"No need."

Xie Yuanjing saw nothing problematic in any of it himself.

A cooperative arrangement—each getting what they needed.

After the wedding, he would give Lu Huaixi every dignity befitting the household's head mistress. He would look after her as one of his own. After the dissolution in one year, he would not turn cold or disavow her.

But none of that needed to be known by his mother.

If she were to learn that this marriage was a pretense from start to finish, her instinct would be to treat the girl with a careful, distancing politeness. And then Lu Huaixi's days in the household would not be easy.

"This matter is not to be mentioned again. When she comes, she is likewise the master of this house."

chapters.title: She Is Really Getting Married
chapters.content:
Days moved quickly. Half a month later, the Lu household suddenly became busy.

There was no grand ceremony—but it was clearly visible that the first branch was preparing for something joyful.

Lu Tangshu endured it for a few days before she simply couldn't anymore, and found a pretext to come over.

"Second Sister, let's take the midday meal together today."

She timed her visit carefully—only to find Lu Huaixi about to leave the courtyard. "Second Sister, are you heading out?"

"Mm. I made plans with Sister Xianya—going to pick up a few things."

"Shopping? Then could Second Sister take me along?"

Lu Tangshu was nervous inside, but nothing showed on her face. She only smiled and drew close. "I've barely been outside the estate in ages—Second Sister would be doing me a favor, and besides, it stops all those idle rumors from spreading."

Lu Huaixi also curved her eyes into a smile—but it was a different kind of smile.

"What idle rumors? I haven't heard any."

"Oh—just some nonsense going around. People are even saying Second Sister is about to be married—that the Lu family is celebrating quietly."

Lu Tangshu probed carefully, her eyes fixed on the person before her, unblinking.

She didn't believe Lu Huaixi could possibly be getting married—after all, she had still been looking through portrait scrolls not long ago—but the first branch had clearly been bringing in festive items. Without a straight answer, she couldn't rest easy.

And not only was there movement in the Lu household. A few days earlier, she had heard that the Chengen Marquis' household was also preparing for a wedding.

She had yet to find out whom Xie Yuanjing was marrying. And now that she was seeing the decorations being put up here, she had no choice but to press for information about the first branch first.

"See what Second Sister makes people laugh about—"

"Actually, they weren't wrong."

Lu Huaixi broke in quietly, her tone soft—carrying an air of slight embarrassment, and yet a quiet hopefulness too.

Lu Tangshu went blank. For a moment she couldn't control her expression.

"Impossible. Who would marry you at a time like this?"

"Why wouldn't they?"

Lu Huaixi's eyes went wide—clear and uncomplicated, settling on the other girl's face—as if startled by her raised voice. "We've been engaged for a long time—since a year ago."

"What?"

Lu Tangshu fought to keep her expression in check. "How could you possibly be engaged to someone? You're supposed to be entering the palace—how can you get married now?"

"What do you mean, entering the palace? I don't understand what Third Sister is saying."

Lu Huaixi played confused—blinked at her—as though startled by the sharpness of her voice and pressing down the urge to look hurt.

"I have a betrothal contract to prove it. Why would I lie to you? And as for what you just said—why would I be entering the palace?"

"You—"

Seeing her expression completely serious and nothing like pretense, Lu Tangshu felt her heart plummet.

In her eyes, Lu Huaixi was a pretty but hollow fool. Rather than let her be deceived by someone into a bad marriage, she was better off in the palace—useful to everyone and a vehicle to lift her own standing.

Not to mention that a woman should provide for her family, and she would be well positioned to help the Lu family. Even if her days weren't easy, that was all the more reason to go.

But Lu Huaixi was claiming a betrothal—and about to be married?

Impossible. Lu Tangshu didn't believe it.

If her mother hadn't done her research, she would never have put Lu Huaixi on that list.

Lu Huaixi must have found something out. That was the only explanation.

The thought sent a bolt of urgency through Lu Tangshu. She didn't even try to hide it anymore.

"No one in the capital has announced an engagement—Second Sister, why are you making things up? And not long ago you were still going through portrait scrolls. Who could you possibly be marrying?"

"When have I ever been going through portraits? Or comparing them? Third Sister—where did you hear all this?"

"Stop pretending, Lu Huaixi—you found out about the palace, didn't you? You grabbed the first person you could find to cover it up?"

Lu Tangshu's grip on her sleeve tightened. The words came to her mouth, urgent, and then she reined herself back with effort—swallowing the wild look that had almost broken through.

"Second Sister, don't be angry. I'm saying this for your sake too. I know you may not want to enter the palace—but if you've gone and married someone at random just to dodge the selection, and the palace finds out, there'll be no one left to protect you. And it would bring trouble to the Lu family as well."

Lu Tangshu kept her voice reasonable:

"Even if you don't care about yourself, think about the family. And Second Sister, you're beautiful—you'll surely rise in the palace. Compared to marrying just anyone and being looked down on all your life, isn't it better to enter the palace and have something to show for it?"

Lu Huaixi had been silent throughout—eyes downcast.

Lu Tangshu grew more anxious at the sight of it.

But she also didn't really believe that in so short a time, Lu Huaixi could have found anyone—most likely some low-ranked scholar with no background, deceiving people into thinking she'd climbed high.

"Why would you say I'm supposed to enter the palace?"

Lu Huaixi was quiet for a long time before she finally spoke.

The person before her was caught off guard by the question for a moment. "Naturally, because I heard it."

"What one hears doesn't hold."

"How can it not hold? Rumors don't come from nothing—since—"

"Whether it holds or not, I'm not going."

Lu Huaixi cut her off, and let the look of easy simplicity fall away. She met Lu Tangshu's eyes.

"I'm getting married. Until something is proved, Third Sister had best not bring it up again—lest my husband's family take offense."

"What husband's family—some penniless scholar with no backing, I suppose?"

Lu Tangshu held her gaze just as hard.

Lu Huaixi must have learned about all of it, and was keeping it from everyone until just before the wedding on purpose.

Yet Lu Huaixi—too uninformed about books, too little learned for her own good—was still doing something this selfish at her age, thinking only of herself.

Listed on the Flower and Bird Envoy register, and she dares to get married? She wants to drag the entire Lu family down with her!

"Second Sister, think this through carefully."

Lu Tangshu barely held down the fire, pulling a thin smile back onto her face. "Whoever this person is—once they hear about all of this, they'll likely not dare go through with it. If that ends up being humiliating—"

"He won't."

Lu Huaixi gave her a smile.

Today she had, for once, added a touch of cosmetics—and when she smiled at someone like that, a vivid brightness overtook her usual softness. A hint of feminine charm slipped through—the kind that momentarily stunned the eyes.

Not long after, Zhou Xianya's voice drifted in from outside, calling her name.

Lu Huaixi turned to the person in front of her with an expression of perfect innocence. "Are you still not leaving, Third Sister?"

Lu Tangshu's grip tightened in her sleeve. She watched her walk away so freely, clearly heading toward the man who had spoken up for her, and a knot of something complex and unwilling pressed against her chest.

"Lu Huaixi—are you really so selfish?"

"I don't know what you're talking about."

"Fine. Then I'll be watching. Watching to see whether this husband of yours really has the guts to come and marry you."

She turned sharply and went to find her mother.

"Young Miss..."

"Leave her."

She had been waiting a long time for the second branch to show their hand—and now they had. Lu Huaixi watched her go, without a word.

That same day, Lady Luo of the second branch went to the Old Madam.

Under the banner of concern for the Lu family, she wept and wailed until the Old Madam was convinced that Lu Huaixi would be the ruin of everything.

Lady Liu had long suspected the second branch of being behind it all—having it confirmed now only pressed a weight onto her chest. But she had no intention of tearing things open at this moment. She let Lady Luo carry on at the Old Madam's side, let them hold each other and weep.

Until the two of them began taking turns at Lu Huaixi—calling her useless and cold-blooded, one phrase after another—that Lady Liu finally snapped, and hurled a teacup at Lady Luo.

The Lu Old Master arrived shortly after, and only then did the whole thing begin to quiet.

But the Old Madam still wasn't satisfied with the marriage.

"Everyone else would leap at the chance to enter the palace—but not her. Only ever thinking of herself, not a single thought for the Lu family! And something as large as getting married, done so secretively—what kind of person did Lu Huaixi run off and marry? Does the Lu family still have any dignity?"

Lu Huaixi was out of the house and knew nothing of any of it.

When she returned, she spotted Xie Yuanjing outside the gates.

They hadn't seen each other in quite a few days. After all the time apart, with something new between them, there was an awkwardness in drawing close that she hadn't had to think about before.

The awkwardness, of course, was mostly Lu Huaixi's.

Xie Yuanjing was perfectly at ease—eyes cast downward, looking at the small girl who only came up to his chest.

"I heard about what happened today."

He said it plainly: "I'll have her placed on the list to take your spot."

"No need."

Lu Huaixi sniffed once. Met his gaze for a moment, then turned her head away.

Xie Yuanjing's gaze lingered on the upturned tip of her nose.

He didn't quite agree with Lu Huaixi being too soft on people—but this was still the Lu family's own affair.

"Still holding back?"

"No."

Lu Huaixi shook her head—no hesitation—and after a quiet moment, said softly: "I'll send the name myself. She said I only care about myself. So let her enter the palace and plan for the Lu family's future instead."

Xie Yuanjing raised a brow. This was not the first time this girl had surprised him—and though it was only a flicker, the feeling made him laugh.

Both families, now certain the marriage was secure, had each let it slip that there had been a prior engagement. But the specifics—who to—had not been tracked down by anyone.

Now the wedding was near, and the two of them shouldn't, strictly speaking, be meeting. But Lu Huaixi thought—this man didn't care about the marriage to begin with. He probably didn't care about these formalities either.

After Xie Yuanjing left, Lu Huaixi went back to her own courtyard.

She had spent the whole day running about. Right now she barely had the energy to speak.

She had just been thinking of lying down for a short nap when Yaoshu came in carrying a letter.

"Miss, someone sent gifts to the door."

"Who?"

"It's Miss Wenlian."

Yaoshu had not been with Lu Huaixi when she went out that day, but she had later sensed—vaguely—that her young miss and the Wenlian girl had parted ways.

She hadn't dared ask more, but today the woman had sent someone with gifts and a letter, and there was no way to avoid it.

Lu Huaixi said nothing. After a moment, she took the letter and read it.

The handwriting was neat and fine. The letter was not long—it said she had been having a difficult time in the Wu household lately, and had been ill, which was why she only heard now that Lu Huaixi was about to be wed.

It also said she had been consumed with regret since that day—had not understood why her heart had clouded over and made her act as she had, and that she had felt terrible.

And it said she was wrong—but she didn't want this friendship to end. She asked Lu Huaixi to give her one more chance to meet, just once.

Lu Huaixi read through it quickly. Then she rose and walked to the lamp nearby.

The room had been lit early; the flames burned bright as daylight.

"Have someone return the gifts. Tell her the well-wishes are received—but there's no need to stay in contact."

Lu Huaixi burned the letter. Said nothing more. Did not believe a word of it.

Once the news spread, the days moved even faster. In the blink of an eye, it was time—the day Lu Huaixi was to be married out of the Lu family.

In the lead-up to the wedding, the first branch had revealed no further details, so Lady Luo had not dared make any bold moves.

That morning, before dawn had even broken, the room was already full of movement.

Lu Huaixi sat before the bronze mirror. Her dark eyes held drowsiness and uncertainty—and also, arriving late, a dawning, unguarded bashfulness.

She was really getting married. Looking at the dazzling bridal garments before her, her heart gave one heavy thud after another.

chapters.title: Waiting to Watch Her Make a Fool of Herself at the Wedding
chapters.content:
Ever since Lu Tangshu had spoken so plainly that day, the Second Branch had been waiting for the First Branch to come pressing them with accusations and causing trouble.

But no one came. There had only been that initial scene in front of the Old Madam, and after that, the manor had been quiet as still water for several days.

Luo shi wore a dark expression. It wasn't until today, the day of Lu Huaixi's wedding, that she finally accepted the truth — that man truly intended to go through with the marriage and had no plans to dissolve the engagement.

Compared to Luo shi, who had swallowed her disappointment and was still holding herself together, Lu Tangshu grew harder to conceal her feelings with each passing day.

Especially after she had harbored those thoughts, after those plans had taken shape — Lu Huaixi's sudden marriage felt like it had severed her road to splendor. Her resentment deepened.

But she wasn't foolish enough to cause a scene on a day like this.

"There will be plenty of people outside today. Keep your wits about you. If you hear anyone mocking Lu Huaixi, don't pretend you didn't hear it — step forward and defend her when the moment calls for it."

"I understand, Mother."

She was desperate to see Lu Huaixi make a fool of herself, but right now, what she needed even more was to build herself a good reputation.

"Don't be impatient. Though that business of sending her into the palace fell through, she's been married off because of it. All that talk about an engagement long set in place is nothing but a smokescreen — that man was certainly just grabbed at random to fill a spot. He can't possibly be anyone of standing."

"From here on out, she'll always be beneath you. By then, you'll be the only legitimate daughter of the Lu household. Add to that the name you've built for yourself as a devoted older sister, and there will be no shortage of men seeking your hand."

Lu Tangshu nodded.

Thinking of how young Lu Huaixi was and how she'd been forced into marriage — and married to some scholar who could barely hold his head up in respectable company — the bitterness in her heart eased a little.

There would be plenty of people to mock her later. She would simply sit back and enjoy the spectacle.

Yet even as her thoughts turned, a trace of worry crept back in.

"But Mother — now that Lu Huaixi has suddenly married, could the matter of the list cause trouble for us?"

"Once this critical moment passes, your father will find a way to have Lu Huaixi's name removed from the list. But there will inevitably be some impact."

Luo shi spoke in a low voice, her expression displeased.

"At worst, we'll spend a bit of silver to smooth things over. In a while, I'll also say a word or two to your grandmother, and have the First Branch put forward some money. And now that Lu Huaixi has married out, her monthly allowance naturally ought to be shifted to you."

Hearing this, Lu Tangshu finally felt a sense of ease.

The First Branch had always been generous with their money, particularly toward Lu Huaixi. It was no wonder she'd been raised so pampered and self-indulgent — unwilling to endure even a little hardship.

"Don't worry about any of that for now. Go keep Lu Huaixi company first. Your younger sisters are all there — don't let them get ahead of you."

"Don't worry, Mother. I intend to be the first to catch a glimpse of my second elder sister's future husband, and give her my personal congratulations in her ear."

She was itching to see Lu Huaixi embarrassed at her own wedding — to hear people whisper about this pampered noble daughter and drag her down from her high perch.

"Do as you like, just don't let anyone see anything amiss. We can't afford to give people something to gossip about."

—

The wedding dress was elaborate. By the time Lu Huaixi had finished putting it all on, a fine sheen of perspiration had gathered at her brow.

The nanny beside her couldn't stop smiling. Though she had been brought in simply to attend to the bride, in just a few short days, she had grown genuinely fond of the young woman before her.

"This wedding dress truly suits you, Miss."

The nanny marveled again and again, unable to contain her admiration. If there weren't real regard behind it all — if someone hadn't poured a great deal of silver into this — how could such a beautiful wedding dress have been rushed to completion in so short a time?

Lu Huaixi couldn't help but look down at her own skirts.

Heat bloomed slowly across her cheeks. It wasn't until someone came in from outside that she returned to her senses, reached for the now-cooled tea beside her, and took a sip.

"Second Elder Sister."

"Second Elder Sister, you look so beautiful! What a pity that Elder Sister still has to wait a little longer before she can see you."

Several younger sisters came in with smiles, Lu Tangshu at the front, quiet as always.

Lu Huaixi's gaze swept across her face. She pretended not to notice the undisguised gloating in her eyes.

"Has Elder Sister come?"

"She came early this morning, but Eldest Aunt called her away to help."

The eldest daughter, Lu Ningyou, was Lu Huaixi's own sister — three years her senior, married last year, and now expecting a child near year's end.

Always mindful of her sister's condition, Lu Huaixi had kept many things from her since the engagement was announced.

"How is she being put to work at a time like this?"

"It's not real work. The whole family dotes on Elder Sister — it's just that a few madams have arrived, and Eldest Aunt is occupied, so she asked Elder Sister to go receive them."

Lu Huaixi smiled at that.

She had nearly forgotten — among all the sisters, it was always her eldest sister who was best at saying the right, gentle thing.

A maidservant nearby, seeing Lu Huaixi chatting leisurely, waited a moment before stepping forward to add a touch of lip color.

The other young ladies stepped back a little to make room.

Only Lu Tangshu, thinking of something, smiled and moved closer instead.

"I haven't had the chance to congratulate Second Elder Sister yet."

She stopped at Lu Huaixi's other side. While the maidservant finished with the lip color and turned to fetch something else, Lu Tangshu leaned in slightly toward her ear, her reflection meeting the bright, flower-like face in the bronze mirror.

A flash of envy crossed her eyes — quickly suppressed.

"Second Elder Sister, even after you're married, remember to come back to the manor often. Whatever happens in the future, the Lu family will always stand behind you. As will I — please don't ever feel ashamed, and don't think the family will look down on you."

A beat passed, and then Lu Tangshu continued.

"Truthfully, I do have some grievances against Second Brother-in-law. Even at the wedding itself, I — your younger sister — have yet to lay eyes on him. No matter how lacking a man might be, he shouldn't behave like this. And yet you, Second Elder Sister, are so good-tempered about it — but that said, please don't think too little of yourself. If I ever get the chance, I will certainly give Second Brother-in-law a proper talking-to."

"You are right."

Lu Huaixi nodded along with her words, her red lips curving into a lovely arc, a quiet smile on her face.

"When you see him in a little while, you must speak to him directly — you are my younger sister, after all. If you're dissatisfied, you must tell him yourself, warn him, and stand up for me."

Lu Tangshu was momentarily stunned. She couldn't tell whether the person before her was deliberately deflecting her taunts, or had simply not understood them. The words died in her throat.

But Lu Huaixi did not wait for her. She only met Lu Tangshu's eyes once through the bronze mirror, then rose to her feet with a smile.

The auspicious hour was drawing near. The bridal veil descended, obscuring the scene before her.

All of the Lu sisters were finally gathered in one place. Lu Yuanzhao stood waiting outside the room, ready to carry his younger sister out on his back to be wed.

The sounds outside grew livelier by the moment — gongs and drums drawing nearer.

"They're here, they're here — the young gentleman has come for the bride!"

Someone outside called out, and in that instant, Lu Huaixi felt a nervousness she had never known before.

chapters.title: The One They Were Speaking of Was Xie Yuanjing
chapters.content:
Outside the Lu manor, a noble and handsome young man rode upon a tall horse, reins in hand, leading a brilliant bridal palanquin slowly forward.

His red attire set off the striking pallor of his skin. Sunlight fell across his refined features, softening the usual aloofness about him, drawing out a faint, expectant warmth.

The onlookers on either side had been puzzling over who could possibly command such a grand procession — until they glimpsed the man at the front, and suddenly made the connection.

The eldest young master of Chengen Marquis Manor was taking a wife — and the bride was none other than the low-profile second young miss of the Lu family!

The crowd's noise died down almost instantly. Even those hoping to receive lucky coins hesitated.

Only a few younger children tried to squeeze forward for a closer look, only to be held back by their elders.

"Don't cause trouble — be careful not to offend the nobility!"

"This is the nobility's joyous occasion. Who would be angry today?"

Seeing that the adventurous ones wouldn't listen, someone nearby grew anxious. "What do you know? The young master of the Marquis Manor kept this wedding quiet — no announcements, no festive decorations — if he truly wanted to make it grand, would he have kept it all hidden?"

That wasn't entirely wrong. When ordinary families held weddings, they sent out invitations weeks ahead and plastered the red festive paper everywhere, afraid the whole world wouldn't know.

Yet these two households — among the most illustrious in the city — had not made a sound, and had kept everything concealed right up until the wedding day.

But just as those words faded, cries of astonishment broke out from the front of the crowd once more.

Everyone turned toward the sound — and saw the line of guards and attendants stretching so far back it seemed to have no end, along with chest after chest of gifts, and nannies and maidservants on either side who kept scattering lucky coins and wedding pastries.

They had only seen the head of the procession and already suspected it was a powerful family. Now, following the line to its distant tail, they realized the spectacle was even greater than they had imagined.

"This is not keeping anything hidden."

Someone murmured admiringly. "This is making absolutely sure everyone knows exactly who it is he's marrying."

The one who had urged caution moments before no longer dared to speak carelessly, and simply pushed forward with the rest, hoping to catch a glimpse of the nobility at its finest.

Lu Huaixi knew nothing of what was happening outside. She sat quietly and obediently, unable to see anything in front of her, only able to stare at her own skirts.

During the procession, she wouldn't be able to see Xie Yuanjing — at most she would hear his voice, see him stopped and made to recite poetry, and then exchange pleasantries with the elders.

Thinking of someone like Xie Yuanjing being made to go through the wedding formalities obediently, the nervousness she'd felt moments before dissipated almost entirely.

She couldn't help but laugh — and before long, her thoughts were swallowed up by the exclamations coming from outside.

"Second Elder Sister, why didn't you tell us that Second Brother-in-law would come with such pomp..."

The younger sisters who had gone ahead to see what was happening came scurrying back, too shocked to speak clearly.

"Second Elder Sister, you — you — he —"

Lu Tangshu was somewhat displeased by the younger sisters' loss of composure. She pulled aside the fourth sister, who was about her own age, and scolded her in a low voice.

"What are you making such a fuss about? Look at you — people will think Mother treats you poorly, the way you're carrying on like you've never seen the world!"

"No — it's not like that, Third Elder Sister. I wasn't making a fuss."

The fourth young miss was a concubine-born daughter of the Second Branch who always had to watch Lu Tangshu's expression. Seeing her displeasure now, she didn't dare show too much excitement.

"It's just — it's out front — Second Brother-in-law is here, Third Elder Sister, go take a look and you'll see. There's such a grand procession out front — even Grandfather and Grandmother are smiling from ear to ear —"

"Impossible!"

Lu Tangshu's expression shifted. Realizing her voice had risen, she quickly composed her face.

Their grandfather might smile and be gracious for the sake of the Lu family's image, but their grandmother had always favored her. She would never be so warm toward Lu Huaixi's hastily acquired husband.

"Stay here and keep watch. I'm going to the front to see for myself!"

With Lu Huaixi's humiliation in mind, Lu Tangshu didn't bother asking further. She simply pushed the younger sister out of her way and went forward directly.

Even if she looked down on him, she still needed to meet this man.

The front was even livelier than Lu Tangshu had expected. A large crowd was gathered, blocking the way, demanding that the man seeking the bride compose an adequate poem before they would let him pass.

Lu Tangshu gave a small sniff of contempt. So scholars had only this one talent to show off. But in the very next moment, she heard the admiring voice of one of the Lu family's branch relatives beside her.

"Even setting all else aside, it is still the Marquis Manor — not to mention that eldest young master is powerful and handsome besides. What other girl could so easily marry someone this impressive!"

Lu Tangshu froze, the movement of turning her head going slightly stiff.

"And that's true — if the Marquis Manor weren't capable, would the First Branch have been willing to give away a legitimate Lu daughter?"

"That may not be the whole story. I heard the engagement was set over a year ago, with a marriage contract as proof. With so many eyes watching now, the Lu family can't possibly back out."

The moment she confirmed they were speaking of Xie Yuanjing, Lu Tangshu felt her breathing go uneven.

She suppressed the dizziness that her fury brought on, and slowly tightened the hand hidden in her sleeve.

An engagement made a year ago? With a marriage contract?

Lu Tangshu strained to piece together the events of recent weeks in her mind.

The Marquis Manor arranging a wedding, the First Branch of the Lu family adding festive goods — all of it came together piece by piece in her memory.

From never being able to find out who Xie Yuanjing had sought to marry, to Lu Huaixi standing before her with that innocent smile — things that had made no sense before suddenly seemed to find their explanation.

Red silk festooned every corner of the manor in brilliant, eye-catching splendor. Lu Tangshu stared fixedly ahead, and in the sea of red, she seemed to see Lu Huaixi's deliberate taunting.

As her thoughts churned, the people blocking the path finally stepped aside.

The proud, inscrutable young nobleman that the world had long spoken of was now smiling faintly, stepping through the gates of the Lu manor one step at a time, drawing ever closer.

Xie Yuanjing was always perceptive.

He quickly became aware of the malice and discontentment threaded through the sea of smiling faces — edged with what seemed like resentment, a barely-contained emotion straining to break loose.

His dark eyes narrowed slightly. A moment later, his gaze lifted and swept toward the direction of that gaze.

Those eyes went cold in an instant — sharp and glacial as an arrow, dangerous and cutting, as if they could pierce through a person's chest the very next second.

Lu Tangshu was startled back to awareness. She jerked her gaze away in panic, cold sweat breaking out silently along her spine.

She instinctively stepped back — but in her haste, her foot caught on a raised stone and she fell to the ground.

The people ahead were still absorbed in their shock and delight at learning that the young man was the eldest young master of the Marquis Manor. Only a few nearby turned at the commotion.

Lu Tangshu endured the humiliation and scrambled back to her feet. When she glanced toward him again with trembling eyes, she found that the man had already moved his gaze away and walked past her position.

As if that brief glance had been nothing but coincidence — as if that gaze had held no warning, no pressure.

But Lu Tangshu knew. Xie Yuanjing had been displeased. He did not like her. In fact —

Lu Tangshu tightened her grip, gritting her teeth as she followed behind the crowd.

Driven by her fierce, unresigned indignation, only one thought occupied her mind: she had to let Xie Yuanjing know that Lu Huaixi was someone meant for the imperial palace.

The Marquis Manor must not have known about it — that was why they had been taken in by Lu Huaixi.

But no sooner had Lu Tangshu moved than she was jostled aside by the people around her and nearly lost her footing again. There was no way to push toward the front.

—

In the inner courtyard, Lu Huaixi was being led to her feet by the nanny.

The excitement was for everyone else. At this moment, she felt only hunger and fatigue — and a curious wonder at what Xie Yuanjing might look like, suffering through the wedding formalities in his red ceremonial robes.

Her younger sisters' chatter filled her ears from time to time, and now and then she could hear her eldest sister speaking words meant only for her — telling her how to manage the household after she married in.

But those voices fell suddenly quiet at a certain moment.

"How did he end up in the inner courtyard? Surely he's not here to see you — couldn't wait, could he?"

Lu Huaixi paused at her eldest sister's remark, and after a moment realized that the "he" in question must be Xie Yuanjing.

She didn't know how to explain — she and Xie Yuanjing were not close enough to need to see each other every day. She thought about it, then simply said nothing.

Though the words carried puzzlement, when Xie Yuanjing drew near, Lu Huaixi's eldest sister still stepped aside to make room.

chapters.title: No One Will Say You Are Not Treasured
chapters.content:
As he approached, he brought with him a distinctive scent that was unmistakably his.

Lu Huaixi couldn't see him, but by instinct alone, she looked down just enough to glimpse a corner of the ceremonial wedding robe beneath her veil.

The nanny had said the two of them were not to see each other before entering the bridal chamber — but since this was not truly a real wedding, Xie Yuanjing likely paid no mind to such rules.

Lu Huaixi didn't find anything wrong with it either. The moment she confirmed he was within sight, she felt, for no clear reason, a great deal more at ease.

And Xie Yuanjing, as if he already knew what she was thinking, stopped and explained himself with a word or two that followed her train of thought.

"I haven't lifted the veil. That doesn't count as breaking the rules."

"Can it work that way?"

"It can. Today, you and I make the rules."

A brief pause, then Xie Yuanjing added, "Just now, I saw your third sister. She has schemes, but they're foolish ones."

Lu Huaixi was briefly startled. Recalling the undisguised mockery in Lu Tangshu's eyes, she gave a faintly amused curl of her lips. "You came all the way back here just to tell me that?"

"Not only that — I was afraid you might not be at peace going into the wedding. I came to check on you."

At first, he had had no particular intentions about making the wedding grand. Aside from fearing that someone might target the Marquis Manor and create obstacles for the marriage, there was also his own attitude — he had never given it much thought.

So when he and Lu Huaixi had discussed it, and both had agreed to keep things simple, he had thought that suited them just fine.

But later, something his mother said had reminded him.

A wedding spoke to how much a man valued his future wife. Too casual would never do.

"Outside I have twenty-four guards stationed. Behind them are two squads of my personal attendants. The palanquin is the auspicious cloud and peacock design you prefer, and the betrothal gifts have been added to — thirty-six chests in total, trailing behind us."

"Today's lucky coins and wedding pastries will be scattered across the east and west quarters of the city. In both our names, I have also donated to two academies in the city's west district and one women's school — even a year from now, no one will dare to say that you are not treasured by Chengen Marquis Manor."

The words caught Lu Huaixi entirely off guard.

Whether it was the gravity of Xie Yuanjing's tone — as if he were discussing official matters — or the thoughtfulness described in his words, she found herself unable to respond.

This level of regard was beyond anything she had anticipated.

For a moment, her heart, which had settled into calm, lurched again with a sudden, overwhelming gratitude.

"You didn't have to go this far — after all, we already agreed..."

"I'm only telling you so that you don't feel out of place once you're in the manor. None of this counts toward our arrangement. You don't owe me anything for it, so don't let it weigh on you."

Right. Xie Yuanjing understood her.

Lu Huaixi let out a quiet breath of relief.

But the air between them had grown a little strange, and after thinking for a moment, she steered the conversation back to what he'd raised at the start.

"Just now, you said you saw my third sister — did she speak to you?"

"Why would she speak to me?"

"Because today she said she had grievances against her future second brother-in-law, that she wanted to warn him — and that she would stand up for me. She told me even after I married, I shouldn't think too little of myself."

Lu Huaixi tilted her head slightly, her veil swaying just a little as she smiled.

"Did she warn you?"

It wasn't really about reporting anything — she had no need to report it.

But perhaps it was because Xie Yuanjing's words a moment ago had brought them a little closer, and Lu Huaixi, thinking of it now, simply couldn't resist the urge to share it with him.

Only, having just spoken the words "second brother-in-law," she felt that the phrase carried a certain intimacy — not quite in keeping with the nature of their current relationship.

The air shifted from strange to awkward.

Especially since Xie Yuanjing had gone silent and gave no response.

Unable to read his expression, she couldn't guess his thoughts. Lu Huaixi's heart began to race. She was just about to say it had been a joke — when she heard a soft laugh from the man before her.

Low and unhurried, it carried a trace of languid ease. Without a face to match it, the voice alone seemed somehow more captivating.

"No."

Xie Yuanjing lowered his voice. "What standing does she have to warn me? Piece by piece — almost sending my wife out of the manor, nearly making it impossible for me to see this wedding through — she's asking to suffer the consequences."

"?"

"Wait until I've gotten through this busy stretch."

"What are you going to do?"

"Her new second brother-in-law will show her just how much she's worth. When that day comes, remember to go comfort her — tell her not to 'think too little of herself.'"

Lu Huaixi was rendered completely incapable of thought by his words.

When she finally understood that this man was standing up for her, Lu Huaixi couldn't hold back a laugh.

Xie Yuanjing with a straight face making jokes — how delightful.

The sounds outside began to swell again. Catching sight of the nanny coming in, Xie Yuanjing didn't linger any further.

Before long, drums and firecrackers rang out in another round, and Lu Huaixi was carried on her brother's back, one step at a time, toward the bridal palanquin.

The shoulders carrying her were broad and steady, each step sure. Walking toward the manor gates, the easy mischief of youth faded from her brother's face, leaving only solemnity.

Lu Huaixi hadn't expected to cry — after all, this wasn't a real marriage.

But as they passed the stone-paved path she had walked for more than a decade, and she heard her unknowing brother leaning close to murmur words of comfort, her nose suddenly stung with a sharp, unbearable ache, and tears blurred her eyes.

"If anyone at the Marquis Manor bullies you, or if Xie Yuanjing treats you poorly, your brother will come and bring you home."

Lu Huaixi cried after all.

After that, the palanquin was lifted and carried, all the way to the Marquis Manor to the beat of music and ceremony.

Holding the red silk cord. Bowing before heaven and earth.

Xie Yuanjing even took her hand, leading her to the bridal chamber himself — replacing the nanny, as if he had naturally stepped into her brother's place.

It wasn't until the door of the room closed behind them and the nanny led Yao Xu to stand to one side that the swollen, aching tenderness in her heart finally began to ease.

When she spoke again, her nose was a little stuffy.

—

Xie Yuanjing returned at no very late hour. There was a faint smell of liquor about him, though it was mild enough not to be unpleasant.

When the nanny carried the jade ruyi scepter before him, the hand hidden in Lu Huaixi's wide sleeve tightened with nerves.

She had just stolen a red date to eat, and when she bit her lower lip now, the corners of her mouth still held the lingering sweetness.

Very quickly the jade scepter passed before her eyes, approaching slowly from below, touching the hem of the bridal veil.

Such a light touch — and yet it seemed to graze Lu Huaixi's very heart, leaving her at a loss.

Xie Yuanjing's motion paused there.

As if something had come to mind, he spoke softly: "Don't be afraid. I've had the small kitchen prepare you some noodles."

She wasn't sure why those two sentences were placed together, but Lu Huaixi did relax somewhat.

She gave a small nod, and only then, belatedly, realized she was truly very hungry.

"Is there more?"

"Also crystal dumplings and clear-broth mutton. Don't eat too much in the evening."

"Then I'd also like one serving of something sweet."

"No. Tomorrow I'll have them make it."

"Just tonight — I'll eat a little less. Can I?"

"No. It's too late in the evening. Be good."

On one side of the room stood Yao Xu and the nanny who had come from the Lu family to attend to Lu Huaixi, and on the other, the servants of the Marquis Manor.

Hearing this exchange, the Lu family attendants thought nothing of it — it was no different from the lord and lady coaxing their young miss.

But the Marquis Manor's maidservants and nannies were secretly stunned, exchanging uncertain glances at the man standing before them.

Rather than believe this indulgent, soothing tone had truly come from their eldest young master, they would rather have believed he was a guard in disguise.

Xie Yuanjing paid no attention to the expressions around him.

When the words were done, the jade ruyi scepter lifted once more, and the bridal veil was raised.

The expression on Lu Huaixi's face fell into Xie Yuanjing's view just as she was pressing her lips together in displeasure at being refused — like someone wanting to make a fuss, yet also aware that she was beholden to another and simply having to sulk inwardly.

Xie Yuanjing couldn't help but give a quiet laugh.

The candlelight caught the curve of his mouth — faint, but enough to startle the people already struggling to keep up.

But Lu Huaixi didn't notice.

The sudden openness of her vision made her forget the matter just a moment before. The glow of red candles in the distance entered her eyes. She blinked, still adjusting to the light, and then looked up at the man before her through the shifting warmth of the flame.

The ceremonial robes were dazzling. The young man was breathtaking.

Lu Huaixi thought about it — she didn't believe she had ever seen anyone more beautiful than Xie Yuanjing.

Lost in thought, she heard the nanny at her side bring forward two cups of wine.

The ritual wine of the wedding ceremony — unavoidable.

Lu Huaixi had barely drunk before. She had only ever tasted sweet, fruit-flavored wine, the kind that didn't intoxicate.

She was suddenly a little eager to try it. But no sooner had she reached out than she heard the man before her speak.

"She doesn't drink wine."

"Young Master, this — this is not in keeping with the rules..."

"We don't follow other people's rules here. Go and substitute tea."

chapters.title: A Little at Ease
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi watched longingly, but in the end couldn't bring herself to disobey Xie Yuanjing's words.

It was partly the awareness that she was under someone else's roof and had best not push her luck — or perhaps the thought that she would soon owe him a great deal — that kept her silent as she watched the wine cups be replaced with teacups.

Only as she drank did she find her gaze drifting inevitably toward the wine cup in Xie Yuanjing's hand.

Lu Huaixi tilted her head back.

The man standing across from her was very close. The warmth of his arm against hers seeped through their sleeves, impossible to ignore.

She watched as he raised his hand to lift the cup, bringing it slowly to his lips — and in that moment she forgot that she, too, was supposed to drink. Her gaze traced the sharp line of his jaw, and came to rest at the corner of his thin lips.

She wanted even more to taste it — Lu Huaixi blinked.

Xie Yuanjing had meant to drink it in one swift motion and be done with it. He raised the cup quickly toward his lips.

But the moment a drop of wine touched them, he noticed that the other person hadn't moved.

The slender, slight arm pressed against his gave no real resistance — it could not possibly have stopped his movement — and yet Xie Yuanjing paused.

He looked down, thinking something was wrong.

"What is it?"

Lu Huaixi met Xie Yuanjing's questioning gaze, and her mind went briefly blank. It occurred to her that she had perhaps been a little rude just now.

But stepping back didn't seem right either. She gathered herself, gave her own cup a small shake, and took the lead — tilting her head back and draining it in one go.

Then it was Xie Yuanjing's turn.

The man's naturally straight, expressionless lips were now tinged with a faint sheen of moisture. Because they were standing close, Lu Huaixi thought she caught the newly added scent of wine.

It seemed, somehow, rather pleasant.

"Go wash up first."

Xie Yuanjing set down his cup. "Come back when you're done, and eat something."

Lu Huaixi didn't want to eat again and then have to wash up a second time. Hearing this, she looked at the man before her and was not particularly inclined to move.

Seeing that she seemed a little slow, the man who had been about to step back found the moment oddly entertaining. He reached past her hair arrangement, raised his hand, and gently ruffled her head.

"If you don't change out of the dress, you won't be comfortable sitting later."

The warmth of that touch jolted Lu Huaixi back to her senses at once. She didn't dare look at him. She simply lowered her head in embarrassment.

The wedding dress really was very heavy, and the skirts very wide.

"Understood."

Face red, the girl muttered her reply, thinking only that this person's hands were even larger than her brother's.

But they were quite warm. The slight roughness of calluses had passed over her and left a feeling of ease behind.

As she walked out, Lu Huaixi instinctively took in the room. It was spacious, not overfurnished, but the items that were there looked refined and exquisite.

Nothing like her own room, which she had filled with all manner of things — a single glance there made it obvious that its occupant was still very young.

After Lu Huaixi left, Gong Fei entered.

"Master."

He kept his head bowed and didn't dare look around the room. "This evening, our men cornered He Jianxing in the crowd and forced him to watch the entire wedding procession."

"Mm. Was he pleased about it?"

Xie Yuanjing gave a quiet sound of acknowledgment.

With Lu Huaixi gone, the man had shed whatever patience he'd been showing. His voice now carried a mocking edge, tinged with cold.

Gong Fei recalled the report, suppressed a laugh.

"He Jianxing didn't believe it at first. He was spouting arrogant talk over there. Then he heard it was you coming for the bride, with such a grand procession, and his face went green with fury — but he couldn't get out, so he could only watch — watch the young mistress take her seat in the palanquin."

"Good. When there's a chance next time, let him see something else as well."

Xie Yuanjing had never taken that man seriously.

That Lu Huaixi had admirers was hardly surprising, but this particular person had the fault of being far too arrogant.

And lately, Xie Yuanjing happened to have a bit of leisure. Moreover, this was a newly taken-in protégé — naturally, he had to make the man understand the gap between them.

"Understood, master."

Gong Fei bowed his head. "There is also the matter of the young mistress — the Second Branch of the Lu family hasn't dared to act on the list these past days, most likely afraid of tipping their hand too soon. But the young mistress sent out quite a few messages a few days ago."

"Using the same method they used?"

Xie Yuanjing's brow furrowed slightly. He placed one hand behind his back and lifted his gaze toward the window.

The Second Branch of the Lu family dared to spread the rumor because Lu Huaixi's name was truly on the list — that was why they had blocked her path. But Lu Huaixi spreading rumors herself would pose no threat to the Second Branch.

A different approach was needed.

"Master, the young mistress did not spread the news that the Second Branch's legitimate daughter was going to the palace. She spread the news that someone had bribed their way onto the list."

"Bribery?"

"Yes. Those handling the matter are now being watched. The people behind the list can no longer casually remove names — if the rumor is confirmed, they would be guilty of dereliction. And with a married woman still on the list, they face an even greater liability if it is investigated."

So the replacement was urgent.

But the Lu family was no small household. Lu Huaixi's spot could not simply be filled by some girl of no standing.

Counting the days, the Second Branch's legitimate daughter, who was almost of age, was the most fitting substitute.

Yet the risk was considerable — once the people under scrutiny caught their breath and regained their wits, it would only be a matter of time before they traced things back to Lu Huaixi.

"Have a completely separate group, unconnected to the young mistress, take over — and find other matters to spread alongside it."

"Understood, master."

Better, then, to muddy the waters entirely and leave no one able to trace anything back to anyone.

After Gong Fei withdrew, Xie Yuanjing stood by the window a while longer. He hadn't intended to think about anything in particular — yet his mind, without permission, conjured the image of that girl staring so longingly at his wine cup.

He hadn't missed it.

Xie Yuanjing couldn't help but laugh again — the corner of his mouth lifting, the arc barely there, fading almost before it could be seen.

He found himself thinking that the days ahead, perhaps, would no longer be a stagnant pool — dull and monotonous.

A breeze moved through the courtyard, raising leaves that drifted up and then fell.

Xie Yuanjing returned to himself and decided not to go to the front hall. He would head to the bath early instead.

But just as he reached the doorway, he saw Zhao Nanny approaching from outside, a handkerchief in hand.

"This old servant greets the eldest young master."

She bowed respectfully. "Eldest Young Master, the eldest young mistress brought only one maidservant and a nanny with her. The Madam's thought is to send someone tomorrow from her own side — a girl the young mistress takes a liking to — to serve her."

"I'll arrange the maid situation myself."

Xie Yuanjing's gaze swept lightly over what the nanny was carrying and said evenly, "Take those things away. She is still young — tell Mother not to rush."

Zhao Nanny was briefly at a loss, feeling caught between difficult options. "This servant understands. But if others were to find out that you and the young mistress haven't..."

The words "consummated the marriage" hadn't even left her lips before Xie Yuanjing waved her off.

"Spare the gossip. No one will find out. Everyone step back — no one needs to stay in the room."

Zhao Nanny snapped her mouth shut and didn't dare say another word, retreating immediately.

Lu Huaixi was unaware that Xie Yuanjing had already deflected the nanny's arrangements on her behalf. She had changed into fresh clothes, washed the cosmetics from her face, and sat down at the table — clean and at ease.

Her skin, freshly touched by water, was even smoother than usual, and in the firelight it seemed almost to glow.

Yao Xu was behind her, tying her just-dried hair, when someone knocked at the outer door, saying it was a maidservant sent by the Old Madam with a gift.

A gift delivered to the bridal chamber — Lu Huaixi was uncertain what to make of it.

Not wanting her to feel uncomfortable, the room had been cleared of everyone else for the time being, so she could only look up at Yao Xu.

"Can I accept it?"

Yao Xu hesitated briefly. "Should be all right — after all, it's from the manor's Old Madam."

Lu Huaixi thought for a moment, then stopped deliberating. "True — if it weren't proper, the maid wouldn't be able to get into the courtyard."

The visitors were admitted shortly after, bearing a scroll painting and a large wooden box, and behind them another maidservant carrying a pair of black boots embroidered with gold trim.

"This servant greets the eldest young mistress."

The two bowed respectfully, placing the items on the table before Lu Huaixi.

The boots were set on the floor. Lu Huaixi glanced at them.

Fine craftsmanship — the gold edging elegant and unobtrusive. They were clearly a man's article of clothing.

They must have been meant for Xie Yuanjing — and yet looking at the style alone, they didn't seem valuable enough for someone to go to the trouble of sending them specifically on the wedding day.

Was Xie Yuanjing terribly short of shoes? Lu Huaixi frowned in puzzlement.

chapters.title: How to Sleep Tonight
chapters.content:
The maidservant had kept her head bowed since entering.

Only when the items were set down did the one at the front speak.

"Eldest Young Mistress, this is a painting by Master Yuan that the Old Madam recently acquired — sent to you today to share in the auspicious occasion. And this is a set of jewelry the Old Madam has chosen for you, she says to wear and enjoy."

Lu Huaixi accepted the gifts without hesitation, receiving them openly and graciously.

Only — after a moment passed, the maidservant made no mention of the pair of shoes, simply backing out of the room with a respectful bow.

Once they were alone, Yao Xu unrolled the painting for her mistress and was about to hand it over, but noticed that the person before her was still staring at the shoes on the floor.

"What is it, Miss — I mean, Young Mistress?"

Lu Huaixi didn't react to the stumbled correction. She only shook her head and looked away.

She was just about to take the scroll and look, when she suddenly recalled something the maidservant had said.

Master Yuan?

She didn't care for painting and calligraphy herself, but she had heard the names of many great masters.

This Master Yuan she had also come across before.

Unlike other great masters who specialized in landscapes or figures, this particular one, starting from some year in the past, had taken a sudden turn and became devoted exclusively to painting scenes of a hundred children — and it was said that everyone who obtained one of his paintings had their wishes fulfilled.

When Master Yuan later passed away, his paintings vanished, and they eventually became impossible to find — priceless and ever more precious.

Lu Huaixi looked over.

The moment she caught sight of the grapes and split-open pomegranates painted on the scroll, she hurriedly looked away again, feeling her ears grow inexplicably warm.

Better not to look any further. After all, it had little to do with her.

Xie Yuanjing returned to the room just as the noodles were brought in, still steaming — along with crystal-clear dumplings and mutton cooked in clear broth, the texture perfectly soft.

Lu Huaixi had intended to mention the gifts she'd received, but before she could speak, he called her over to sit, and her attention was drawn immediately to the food on the table.

Lu Huaixi really was hungry. She had eaten nothing all day except for a few bites of fruit. Not to mention she had taken a bath recently, which had drained a little more energy.

Xie Yuanjing didn't eat much — only a few bites to keep her company, then set down his chopsticks.

Beside him, the young girl ate with genuine focus: a bite of noodles paired with a bite of vegetables, then a slice of mutton.

Her manner of eating was graceful. Even with broth and such, the soup never stained her lips overmuch.

Yet she seemed to have something on her mind — every now and then she would accidentally burn herself on a noodle, though she didn't frown. Only the tip of her tongue would flinch slightly, just for a moment, and then it would pass.

By the time she finished, Xie Yuanjing realized he had been watching her eat for quite a long while.

After rinsing her mouth again, Lu Huaixi stood up.

Thinking of the painting from earlier, she felt — even though she knew nothing would happen — a lingering flush of embarrassment that wouldn't quite leave her face.

"Did something happen?"

Xie Yuanjing noticed she was holding something back. He interrupted her thoughts and called her to him. "Tell me."

An unfamiliar manor and an unknown year ahead — it was natural for Lu Huaixi to feel a little unsettled. Though it didn't show on her face, there was inevitably some unease beneath the surface.

But Xie Yuanjing's "tell me" was like a small boat gliding steadily across a rippling surface, taking hold of her, drawing her toward safety.

"Nothing happened."

Lu Huaixi shook her head — but her bright, clear eyes looked straight at him, full of trust.

"It's just that the Old Madam just had someone send gifts. I accepted them — is that all right?"

Xie Yuanjing didn't answer immediately. He met that sincere, slightly dependent gaze, and paused for a moment.

The Lu family's inner household was not truly peaceful. The First and Second Branches had their friction, entangled just as any great family was — the relationship perhaps even more strained than that of the Lu Third Branch, who had been dispatched out of the capital.

And yet, despite all that, Lu Huaixi had been raised with a nature of uncommon purity. It had nothing to do with cleverness or lack thereof.

She would offer goodwill first, without the wariness and calculations that most people brought. And once that goodwill was met — she would give trust in return, and show her reliance and closeness openly, unguarded.

When goodwill found no reception, that was all right too. She seemed to possess an innate gift for healing — both for others and for herself.

And, of course, the decisiveness to cut things cleanly when the time came.

"Is it wrong to accept?"

Seeing Xie Yuanjing hadn't replied, Lu Huaixi pressed her lips together and asked again.

By now, she had already come to think of Xie Yuanjing instinctively as one of her own people.

Even here in the Xie manor, even when speaking of Xie Yuanjing's own grandmother, she still placed Xie Yuanjing firmly on her side.

"You can accept it. It's fine."

After a moment, Xie Yuanjing finally spoke — his voice slightly low — and then picked up his teacup and took a small sip.

"You said nothing, and I thought there was some rule against it."

"Not seeing a rule against it doesn't mean you were unafraid."

"How would you know I wasn't afraid?"

Lu Huaixi murmured in return, turned away, and found another seat. The pair of new shoes delivered by the maidservant happened to be right beside her.

Xie Yuanjing didn't reply this time either — only gave a quiet laugh, his gaze settling on the empty bowl on the table.

Lu Huaixi followed his gaze, and her cheeks turned faintly red.

She could see plainly that Xie Yuanjing was laughing at her — laughing at how she could be afraid and yet have such a hearty appetite.

Face too thin for shamelessness, Lu Huaixi looked away, and after a moment steered the conversation back.

"The Old Madam sent a painting and jewelry. Oh, and there are also these shoes."

She pointed at the items on the floor, hesitating slightly. "Are you terribly short of shoes?"

The faint smile on Xie Yuanjing's face faded as the topic shifted. His eyes lowered, and his expression went cool with it.

"No."

He cast a glance at the pair of boots. When someone came in to tidy, he gave a cold instruction: "Take those and throw them away."

Lu Huaixi was a little surprised.

The shoes were somewhat ordinary, but not so much that they warranted being thrown out directly.

Before she could make sense of it, Xie Yuanjing had already risen to his feet.

"If there's anything you need added to the room, tell Gong Fei to have it arranged. If any of the furnishings feel too gloomy, they can be changed — you don't need to feel out of place here."

Seeing him heading inside, Lu Huaixi lost track of her question about the shoes and simply took in her surroundings once more. "It's not gloomy. It's beautiful."

The maidservants quickly withdrew, and again only the two of them remained in the room.

But rather than admiring Xie Yuanjing's quarters, Lu Huaixi had something else weighing on her mind.

"Tonight... how are we supposed to sleep?"

"Up to you. How would you like to sleep?"

"?"

Xie Yuanjing's steps came to a halt — just beside a newly brought-in wooden sleeping couch.

He didn't say anything, only turned his back to the outer room. "The bed or the floor — either works for me."

A silence settled over the room.

Lu Huaixi lowered her head, not quite knowing how to respond.

That day at Xie Madam's flower-appreciation banquet, she and Xie Yuanjing had talked at length in the water pavilion.

Before she'd left, Xie Yuanjing had called her back — there were conditions he needed her to agree to.

Lu Huaixi had naturally said yes. Among those conditions was this one: that for the first three months after the wedding, they would not sleep in separate rooms.

No giving others cause for suspicion. No letting anyone see anything amiss.

It was reasonable not to refuse, and Lu Huaixi understood that clearly.

But now that the day had truly arrived, she found herself suddenly flustered — and more than that, uncertain how to make the arrangements.

It was his room. She couldn't very well ask a man to sleep on the floor for three months. But if she slept on it herself, she'd ache all over and be unable to stand up.

"Come here."

Just as she was caught in her dilemma, a soft laugh fell — low and deep and pleasant.

chapters.title: The First Time Sharing a Room with Someone
chapters.content:
Xie Yuanjing had watched long enough — her head bowed, obedient and a little forlorn — and called her over with a smile.

Lu Huaixi walked in dutifully and saw the brand-new sleeping couch.

"Do you like folding screens?"

She was still marveling at how timely it all was when she heard the question, and immediately shook her head. "I don't."

"...Then we won't have a screen. This is how we'll sleep going forward — you take the bed, I'll take the couch."

"For — three months?"

"What else?"

Lu Huaixi thought about it. "What if we took turns?"

Xie Yuanjing looked at her again, a quiet laugh escaping him. "No need for you to take turns. There's no reason you should live any worse here than at the Lu family's home."

Those words made Lu Huaixi's heart leap again — and the last trace of awkwardness dissolved in his low, unhurried voice.

"Get settled first. I'll be in the outer room looking over some affairs."

"Won't you go to the study?"

"On a day like today, how would I go to the study?"

Xie Yuanjing lowered his gaze. "No need. The outer room is sufficient."

On one's wedding day, there was hardly any real official business. He simply didn't want her to feel uncomfortable — he was giving her the chance to fall asleep first.

After a few more exchanges, Lu Huaixi also sensed his meaning. She watched Xie Yuanjing turn and walk away, gently pressing her lips together — genuinely relieved by his gesture.

—

The red wedding candles in the outer room were a little too bright for Xie Yuanjing's eyes. He flipped through the ledger in his hand, but found it difficult to concentrate.

Not until the rustling sounds inside fell quiet and the shifting of blankets ceased did he finally set down what he was reading and press his fingers to the bridge of his nose.

The whole room seemed to carry a new, faint sweetness.

On his own, he rarely used incense. With the room being so large and him having filled an entire wall with bookshelves, it had always held the scent of wood, ink, and old paper.

But now the new fragrance had swept through the entire room with remarkable force.

Unlike its owner, who seemed gentle — it occupied every corner with a kind of boldness, lingering at the tip of his nose, refusing to dissipate.

Unable to concentrate, Xie Yuanjing gave up trying.

He put his things away, rose to his feet, and blew out the red candles in the outer room, softening his footsteps.

Before the last light in the inner room was extinguished, he paused and looked at Lu Huaixi from a slight distance.

The thin blanket covered her up to just below her nose. Above the blanket were tightly closed lashes — thick and curling.

She slept very peacefully — more peacefully than he had expected. He wasn't sure whether to call it admirable courage or enviable carelessness.

He put out the last few candles, and Xie Yuanjing finally lay down, pulling a thin blanket over himself.

Darkness fell complete before him. After a moment he adjusted to it.

He wasn't sure if it was because he was sharing a room with someone for the first time, but Xie Yuanjing closed his eyes and opened them again, finding not the slightest trace of drowsiness.

Moonlight filtered in from outside, and at the angle where he was lying, a slight turn of his head would reveal the bed.

He didn't look.

Just as he was attempting to close his eyes again, he heard a faint, soft, murmuring sound, accompanied by the gentle shifting of blankets.

"Sleepy."

Xie Yuanjing froze. He paused for a moment, then replied under his breath: "...You're not asleep yet?"

The person on the bed gave no real reply.

"So sleepy."

Lu Huaixi murmured, turning over with a smacking of her lips. "Want sweet cake tomorrow. Big Brother, buy some."

The sweet cake she hadn't gotten at dinner.
