It dawned on him that she was dreaming, and Xie Yuanjing paused.

After a long moment, he rose with a helpless resignation, pulled on an outer robe at random, and padded in the cold moonlight toward the bed.

The blanket had indeed slipped, exposing the snow-white collar of Lu Huaixi's inner garment at her shoulder and neck. He stood silently for a moment, then reached out and tucked the blanket snugly back around her.

He lay back down on the couch, pressed his fingers to his brow, and forced his eyes shut — drifting gradually to sleep amid the soft, even sound of her breathing.

—

In the rear courtyard of the Marquis Manor, the Old Madam — who was long past the hour for sleep — let out a sigh, exhaustion written on her face.

Seated before her was a young woman with her head slightly bowed, dressed simply in a pale green gown. She didn't speak — only let a tear fall occasionally, looking utterly pitiful.

"Weimi, regardless of whether Yuanjing was forced into this or not, that position is now out of your reach. But if you're clever about it and take things slowly, entering the rear court isn't impossible."

"I know that you care for me, Grand Aunt."

Mu Weimi drew a deep breath and held back her tears.

"Now that my cousin has wed, I no longer dare to hope for anything more. I only ask that the one he has married can take good care of him, tend to the household, and give Grand Aunt a great-grandchild soon."

"It's good that you can think this way. I naturally hold you in higher regard than the others. It's just..."

The Old Madam shook her head.

She had already arranged many opportunities for the girl before her — had nearly come to blows with her own grandson over it.

Today she hadn't initially intended to send gifts to the new bride so suddenly. But seeing how Weimi had put her heart into making a pair of shoes for Yuanjing, she had found a pretext and arranged for that small wish to be fulfilled.

She could see the girl's intentions clearly enough.

Sending shoes made by hand on the wedding night — to plant herself in the man's thoughts, and stir the new bride's suspicions.

Not the most refined of tactics, but not entirely without effect either.

"This sort of thing — once, and only once."

The Old Madam's somewhat clouded eyes narrowed slightly. "You've always been sensible. If you truly intend to compete, you'll have to wait at least until Yuanjing's interest has run its course."

"I understand. My cousin..."

Mu Weimi lowered her gaze, lightly pressing a handkerchief to the corner of her eye.

"Even if this wasn't entirely of his choosing, he has already married her. The fault is only that I have no status to help my cousin. Tonight's shoes were sent partly out of concern for him — but I also wanted to know what kind of person she is. Whether she would show her temper toward my cousin."

"Are you certain Yuanjing doesn't care for the new bride?"

"Grand Aunt, I truly heard it with my own ears — what Grand Uncle said to my cousin. He told him to consider the larger picture."

A pause, then Mu Weimi continued in a low voice: "From the way it sounded, the Lu family's noble daughter seems quite willful and spoiled."

The Old Madam fell silent at this.

She had originally thought that with Weimi married in, she could work on Yuanjing from the inside and make that difficult, unmanageable grandson a little easier to handle. But she hadn't expected him to send Weimi away outright — without a trace of consideration.

Though she had her differences with this eldest grandson, she hadn't wanted a true falling out.

Besides, the younger ones in the family truly needed his support to advance.

"Since she's willful, be even more accommodating."

The Old Madam closed her eyes briefly, then opened them. "Yuanjing's rear court will not forever have only one person. There must always be someone who can soothe him — someone perceptive, someone who understands the situation."

"I understand, Grand Aunt. As long as I can care for you and my cousin, I'm willing to do anything. Even if I can never truly become my cousin's person — I will not say a single word of grievance."

Outside, the Second Madam Qi Miaoji had just arrived with medicine and happened to catch those last two sentences.

She couldn't help but curl her lip, contempt flashing briefly in her eyes for this so-called cousin.

"Still daydreaming when the bride has already married in."

The nanny beside her was startled. She quickly tried to warn her mistress: "We're in the Old Madam's courtyard right now — Second Madam, that sort of talk can't be said here."

"What is there to be afraid of? It's so late — no one heard."

Qi shi simply stopped at the doorway, not bothering to go in.

"I don't know what that Old Madam of ours is thinking — taking in a distant relative is one thing, but now she wants to drag her own grandson into it? Setting that all aside, isn't the Lu girl perfectly fine?"

Today was the First Branch's joyous occasion, and she had been in fine spirits all day — looking forward to meeting the new bride tomorrow.

If they got along, they could spend more time together going forward.

But in the evening, just as she'd been about to retire, she'd been summoned here to attend on the Old Madam.

Ordinarily, this sort of duty fell to the Third Young Madam, and the Old Madam favored her youngest daughter-in-law — always finding opportunities to give the Third Branch advantages.

But tonight the hour was too late, and the Old Madam didn't have the heart to make the Third Young Madam come out. Unable to call on the First Branch either, she had summoned her instead.

Qi shi was quietly fuming, and hearing this kind of talk, she naturally couldn't hold herself back from speaking up for the First Branch.

chapters.title: I am your support
chapters.content:
The next morning, when Lu Huaixi awoke, the sky was already bright outside.

She opened her eyes to an unfamiliar place and was dazed for a long while before slowly sitting up.

As she rose, Yao Xu outside heard the movement and knocked, coming in — followed by a maidservant carrying warm water.

"This servant is Jing Shuang. I greet the eldest young mistress."

Lu Huaixi was still drowsy and didn't look closely — she only gave a vague sound of acknowledgment.

It wasn't until she took the warm towel that she finally woke properly.

"There's still the tea-serving ceremony today, isn't there?" Lu Huaixi was alert at once, and glanced outside. "Have I overslept? Why didn't anyone wake me?"

"Please don't worry, Young Mistress."

Yao Xu stepped in with reassurance. "The Eldest Young Master left for the study and said there was no need to be up so early, and that he would come and escort you later."

"Even so, I shouldn't have slept in on this first day. Being late won't do."

No matter what the marriage was, there was no reason to keep elders waiting.

Yao Xu didn't dare delay further, and together with Jing Shuang helped her change and dressed her hair.

When Lu Huaixi stepped outside shortly after, intending to ask when Xie Yuanjing would arrive, she lifted her head and saw two nannies waiting at the courtyard entrance.

One was Ying Nanny from the Lu family, who had come to tend to her and was close with her. The other she didn't recognize — clearly one of the Marquis Manor's, with a stern bearing.

"Eldest Young Mistress, you've risen rather late today. When you go to meet the elders now, remember to apologize for the discourtesy."

Ying Nanny's brow furrowed at the tone.

But Lu Huaixi felt nothing amiss. Her eyes showed nothing but candid self-reflection.

"I will apologize. I truly did rise late today."

The speaking nanny, seeing her accept the rebuke so readily, was momentarily at a loss and couldn't quite find cause to press further.

She was one of the Old Madam's nannies. Yesterday, the Old Madam had heard that the new bride was spoiled and ill-tempered, and had sent her this morning to have a look and administer a little correction.

She had not yet had the chance to find fault before she arrived and heard voices from inside speaking of being late.

"Eldest Young Mistress, though you are still young, you may not disregard the rules. Going forward, remember to keep to the proper hour for morning greetings — after all, you are married now, and cannot carry on as you did at home."

"Of course. But since your side gave no reminder, allowing me and my people to fall short of courtesy without being aware, it seems you, too, were neglectful in your duties."

Lu Huaixi acknowledged her fault readily enough — yet she was not, as the other woman had hoped, left embarrassed or contrite.

Instead she met the stern gaze directly, furrowed her brow, and asked with perfect seriousness: "Are you from the Eldest Young Master's courtyard?"

The nanny was taken aback again, her expression shifting slightly.

"This old servant belongs to the Old Madam's courtyard. But even if I were not from the Eldest Young Master's household, with the Old Madam's authority, I have standing to teach the Eldest Young Mistress proper conduct."

The furrow in Lu Huaixi's brow had not yet eased.

The usually clear, limpid eyes held something more complex now.

She was just debating whether to spare the Old Madam's face on this first day when she heard footsteps approaching from ahead.

She looked up — and saw Xie Yuanjing returning from the study.

"You slept late last night. Why didn't you rest a while longer?"

The nanny had been about to ask why she hadn't seen the Eldest Young Master's silhouette in the room — but hearing that question, the inquiry died before it could be voiced.

She was worried she'd genuinely angered the man, and felt her heart begin to flutter.

"We have the tea ceremony — I already rose late."

Lu Huaixi replied to him, without noting anything amiss in his question.

Xie Yuanjing gave a quiet sound of acknowledgment, then very naturally reached out and briefly held her hand. Lu Huaixi barely had time to register it before he let go.

"A little cold. You don't need to be up this early going forward."

With that, Xie Yuanjing suddenly lifted his gaze toward the people standing behind her.

His tone was the same as ever — but when the words landed, the air around them inexplicably turned cold, carrying with it a pressure that bore down.

"Have I not said that no outsiders are permitted to come and go as they please in my courtyard?"

"We beg the Eldest Young Master's pardon!"

Several people panicked at once, bowing their heads and confessing their fault. "This servant was careless — did not stop them at the gate!"

"Once last night, once this morning."

Xie Yuanjing swept his gaze over them. "The wedding lasts three days — no bloodshed during those three days. After the three days are up, go receive your punishment on your own."

The nanny standing nearby trembled, her whole body shaking.

She suddenly realized — the new bride might be spoiled, but that only meant she was confined to the inner courtyard. This man, however, if displeased, would not speak of rules or give face.

In her panic, the nanny lowered her head along with the others and began to plead for pardon.

"Twenty strokes," Xie Yuanjing said without reprieve. "So that you don't forget — coming into my courtyard to instruct my wife on proper conduct."

The punishment came down without room for argument.

Lu Huaixi said nothing, only following Xie Yuanjing as they walked out.

Behind them, the sound of the strokes rang out clear and deliberate — proof that no one dared to go easy.

But more than that, her thoughts were still caught on the cold, precise way Xie Yuanjing had said the words "my wife."

"Rather more formidable than I expected. I thought you'd simply swallow the lecture."

"What do you mean?"

Lu Huaixi snapped out of her reverie and turned to look at him, puzzlement rising in her eyes. "What was formidable about it?"

"Just now — saying she was neglectful. Weren't you trying to have her punished?"

"No."

Lu Huaixi shook her head, looking at him with genuine surprise. "If she were a nanny stationed in your courtyard, then she was failing at her duty — I was only telling her so she'd know."

She paused, then curious, asked: "But could she actually be punished?"

Xie Yuanjing was briefly at a loss for words.

He didn't quite know what to say. Watching her blink with those open, guileless eyes, he found himself, for no clear reason, raising his hand again and ruffling her hair.

"Yes. If she shows you disrespect, you may punish her however you like."

"Even someone from the Old Madam's courtyard?"

"Yes."

Xie Yuanjing was rather fond of looking at her eyes — and fond of seeing his own reflection in them.

As if, caught in her gaze, he too could exist for a moment in that clear and unblemished light.

"My courtyard doesn't allow outsiders to come and go freely as a rule. Last night someone slipped through during the wedding — it won't happen again."

"The way you put it, you seem rather formidable in this manor."

"I am."

Xie Yuanjing smiled slightly. "My support is behind you — so you can afford to be bolder."

The small dejection from waking up somewhere unfamiliar, and the little flare of temper from being lectured without cause — half of it faded the moment Xie Yuanjing briefly took her hand. The other half dissolved in the reassurance of his words.

Lu Huaixi tilted her head, a quiet smile on her lips. "Then for this one year, I intend to be a mistress of the rear court — idle and self-indulgent, but with just a hint of temperament."

"That's fine."

The path to the front hall was still some distance away.

Lu Huaixi was in good spirits, following him along a stone-paved walkway, then up a covered corridor, and past a flower garden.

On a trellis standing half a person's height, clusters of vine wound around the frame. Small, nameless blossoms had opened all along it.

Beside the more prized flowers in the garden, Lu Huaixi found these little ones — that could sway in the breeze — altogether more charming.

Xie Yuanjing noticed, and looked over with her.

"The flowers inside were planted by my mother. On the way back I'll come with you to pick some."

"No need."

Lu Huaixi shook her head.

She was just about to explain that the flowers she was looking at weren't the ones inside the garden, when a gust of wind swept through.

It was strong — and in a sudden rush, it sent one of the small purple flowers tumbling from the vine.

The petals fluttered like a butterfly, seemingly without direction — and then, as if guided, drifted down into Lu Huaixi's outstretched palm.

"Why so happy?"

She heard a sound of amusement. Xie Yuanjing turned to look at her.

Lu Huaixi never missed a chance to share her delight. She curved her eyes at him, those moon-bright eyes full of small sparkling lights.

"Look."

She held out her open palm toward him, showing him the flower resting there.

"Happy because I have good luck."

Xie Yuanjing's gaze rested on the flower in her palm for a long moment. After a while, he, too, gave a small smile.

"Yes."

He looked toward Lu Huaixi's eyes again, and added: "My luck is also very good."

chapters.title: What's Mine Is Yours
chapters.content:
In the front hall, the members of the various Xie branches had already taken their seats.

Though Lu Huaixi had been sought out by one of the Old Madam's nannies this morning, now that she stood before the woman herself, she couldn't make out anything particularly displeased in her expression.

The maidservants soon brought in the tea.

Directly before Lu Huaixi stood Xie Madam — who looked at her with warmth on her face and a kind smile.

Beside her was the Marquis of Chengen, whose face showed some fatigue, though even seated, a certain commanding gravity remained about him that spoke of a man long accustomed to high station.

After her engagement, Lu Huaixi had learned a little about the Marquis Manor's affairs. She knew that this Marquis had been entangled in a case a year ago — had nearly been imprisoned, and had almost lost his life proving his innocence.

The case was eventually cleared, but the Emperor's displeasure lingered.

She had also heard, by chance, that the case had initially had nothing to do with the Marquis — he had inserted himself by choice, and that was what had brought disaster upon him.

Lu Huaixi didn't know the full reason, and couldn't even confirm whether all she'd heard was true. But she could sense that when Xie Yuanjing faced his father, the flat line of his mouth carried unmistakable coldness.

"Father, please drink. Mother, please drink."

Lu Huaixi bowed her head, offering the tea cups together with Xie Yuanjing.

Xie Madam was visibly pleased — her expression every bit that of someone who thoroughly approved of this marriage.

Lu Huaixi saw it and returned a gentle smile, giving a gracious reply, meeting the warmth in kind.

But when she reached the Marquis, she slightly drew back her expression — keeping only the composure that courtesy required, bowing her head and listening respectfully as he spoke.

Since his health was still recovering, the Marquis didn't linger long after presenting his gift.

As he rose, he covered his mouth with his fist and coughed for quite a while. At last he looked at the young people before him and added a few more words of instruction before departing.

No one in the hall found anything amiss. Lu Huaixi could also see that the Marquis's health was genuinely not fully restored.

She thought nothing more of it — but Xie Yuanjing, seizing a moment when others were speaking, leaned slightly and lowered his voice.

"He's still recuperating. He hasn't taken a dislike to anyone."

Xie Yuanjing tilted his head ever so slightly, his lips close to Lu Huaixi's ear.

Lu Huaixi blinked, taking a moment to understand — "he" referred to the Marquis.

"I know."

"Mm."

"Were you afraid of him just now?" Xie Yuanjing asked.

Lu Huaixi wasn't sure why he would ask that. She shook her head and looked over at him. "I wasn't afraid. My father sometimes looks more fierce than the Marquis."

Xie Yuanjing didn't reply — but his gaze fell steadily on her, clearly having noticed the difference in how she had treated the two of them.

Sensing him waiting, Lu Huaixi inhaled softly, lowering her eyes.

"I was looking at you. It seemed like you were unhappy."

They were father and son after all — no sooner had the words left her than she rethought them. "No — I mean, I saw that you looked a little serious."

After a moment's thought, she looked back at him and said with sincerity, "We are on the same side. Of course I follow your lead. If I follow wrong, tell me."

Xie Yuanjing had not expected that explanation. He made no reply still — but the gaze he turned on Lu Huaixi held a momentary depth.

Something in the air between them grew slightly strange, and when they looked at each other, it was not quite the usual easy openness.

But before Lu Huaixi had time to think about what felt off, she heard a burst of laughter from nearby.

"All right, I know you two just got married — but the elders ahead are still waiting for their tea. Save the clinging for when you're back in your own room!"

At the sound of it, Lu Huaixi glanced over, and her eartips went warm.

The speaker was Xie Manor's Second Madam — she had met her at the flower-appreciation banquet. She was someone who smiled easily and spoke frankly.

Caught by the teasing, Lu Huaixi had no more time to puzzle over Xie Yuanjing's expression, and quietly pressed her lips together as she moved ahead to wait for the maidservant to hand over the tea.

Xie Yuanjing, just pulling himself free of those thoughts, saw her go neat and obedient, and found it amusing.

"What are you standing so far away for — come here."

He drew her in lightly by the wrist, and let go — the two of them now close enough that the smallest movement would brush her sleeve.

"Second Aunt and my mother are close. No ill intent."

"Oh, understood."

Lu Huaixi lowered her gaze and quietly added the Second Branch to her list of approachable people.

"Any others? What about the rest?"

The maidservant arrived with the tea. Xie Yuanjing took his cup alongside her. "There are. I'll tell you when we're back."

"All right."

Seated here were the Old Master and Old Madam of the Xie family.

Compared with the Marquis earlier, the Old Master before her gave a stronger impression of authority and power.

She took one look, and followed alongside to call out "Grandfather, Grandmother."

She was just about to offer the tea when a small movement nearby caught her attention — and someone came in, stopping beside the Old Madam.

Maidservants came and went through the hall, rarely causing a stir. Lu Huaixi hadn't paid attention at first — but this person was dressed differently from a maidservant, and her clothes, though simple, were of excellent quality.

Yet to say she was one of the manor's young ladies — she had taken her place behind the Old Madam, bent to say a few words in a familiar, close manner, and had no intention of sitting down.

Lu Huaixi quickly looked away.

Xie Yuanjing hadn't glanced at her once.

After completing the ceremony here, he led her through the hall to greet the remaining family members. Not until Lu Huaixi had nearly drunk herself full on tea did all the Xie branches finally get accounted for.

Yet Lu Huaixi didn't show impatience.

She kept her eyes gently curved throughout, and with each gift she received, her smile grew a shade sweeter — until those watching her couldn't help but tease.

"Elder Sister-in-law, why do you look like a little money-lover? Don't tell me my elder brother has been keeping coins from you."

"What are you saying — show some respect for your elder sister-in-law."

The speaker was Xie Qintian, the fourth young miss of the Xie family — a daughter of the Second Branch, the same age as Lu Huaixi.

Her words were barely out before the Second Madam beside her gave her a playful swat.

But she was entirely unabashed, and only laughed more gleefully.

"I meant to say that Elder Brother and Elder Sister-in-law are perfectly matched."

The fourth young miss Xie Qintian then winked at Lu Huaixi. "Elder Sister-in-law couldn't have made a better match with my elder brother."

"How so?"

Seeing her so cheerful — and knowing the Second Branch was a household she could befriend — Lu Huaixi relaxed.

Though hearing that word "elder sister-in-law" made her briefly flustered, she gathered herself quickly enough, and smiled as she tilted her head at her. "Because I'm a money-lover?"

"Exactly — my elder brother has loads of it. Perfect for a money-lover."

Xie Qintian said, "My elder brother doesn't spend much in day-to-day life. He's either attending to official business or dressing people down. Sometimes I used to worry about what he'd do with all that silver."

"Is that so —"

Lu Huaixi made a show of glancing back at Xie Yuanjing. Seeing he didn't seem to mind, she let herself speak a little more freely.

"Then from now on, no need to worry. I'll spend it."

Having said it, she still felt a small pang of uncertainty, and couldn't resist asking Xie Yuanjing once more.

"May I?"

When Lu Huaixi smiled, her eyes curved low at the corners, her dark pupils like rain-touched glass — clear and beautiful.

Now she had her head tilted back slightly, bold yet shot through with a small thread of dismay — as if she already regretted being too quick to speak. It barely showed on her face, but she watched him with that earnest, wide-eyed look — the kind belonging to a child who knew she'd made a mistake and yet still hoped for praise, making it impossible to say anything unkind.

Xie Yuanjing was rarely this patient with anyone.

He watched her — and just as she was about to lose heart, he gave a quiet laugh and nodded.

"Yes."

He said, unhurried, "What's mine is yours."

Beside them, Xie Qintian was astonished. It took her a full moment to believe what she'd heard.

Rarely seeing her elder brother so agreeable, she pushed forward eagerly. "Then I get to spend some too — Elder Sister-in-law, don't forget about me!"

The hall became livelier than ever. The few madams in the front didn't attempt to dampen the mood, chatting pleasantly among themselves, not inclined to interrupt the younger generation. Even the Old Madam said nothing reproving, only drinking her tea with her head lowered.

It was Xie Yuanjing who found it a little too noisy — and stepped forward to remove his wife from the crowd.

"Alright. She can — the rest of you, no."

"..."

Though they knew it was said in jest, the young ladies still didn't quite dare to make a scene with Xie Yuanjing directly.

Xie Qintian could only give Lu Huaixi a muttered pout, swallowing her indignation.

Lu Huaixi found it entertaining and was just about to say something back to Xie Qintian, when, unexpectedly, she felt an unusual gaze settle on her.

She looked up sharply — and caught the young woman standing beside the Old Madam, with a brow that had not yet relaxed.

She seemed displeased. Unhappy.

Rather curious.

Lu Huaixi quickly looked away again — and a thought flickered through her mind with sudden clarity.

Could this be the one her elder brother had mentioned — the one who had been close at hand, and yet had failed to reach the moon?

chapters.title: Be a Little More Bold
chapters.content:
With the tea-serving ceremony done, Xie Yuanjing wasted little time leading her away from the hall.

Lu Huaixi was only belatedly realizing that those things she'd said shouldn't have been said quite so casually — but before she could dwell on it, the person beside her drew her thoughts elsewhere.

"Next time they call you over there, decline outright. Tell them I won't allow it."

It had been a long moment with no response. Xie Yuanjing looked back and found the girl completely lost in thought, wearing a look of flustered vexation at something she couldn't quite work out.

He watched for a moment. Seeing that furrowed brow and half-closed eyes not watching where she was walking, he slowed his pace.

The covered walkway led down a few stone steps at the end. Xie Yuanjing watched her lift her foot and catch nothing but air, then saw those eyes go wide, and felt her lean forward — he hesitated a beat, and at the last moment, reached out and caught her.

Once she was steady and the fear had begun to set in, he let go and stopped beside her.

"Lesson learned?"

They were standing very close. Xie Yuanjing could still feel the warmth radiating from the slender curve of her waist.

Lu Huaixi's attention was not on his hand, which had just released her. She only lightly patted her chest, and turned to look at him — still with the fading unease in her eyes.

Below the stone steps was a gravel path. The stones there had been smoothed and rounded, but they were still hard and unforgiving.

If she had really fallen, her face would have been scraped raw — and her head would have fared no better.

"You were watching me the whole time?"

Lu Huaixi looked at him, tilting her head.

"Yes. Waiting to see you fall."

"And then you still reached out."

She muttered, her voice carrying a small trace of indignation — but she was also aware that he had caught her, and it wasn't a real grievance. "You could at least have warned me sooner."

Xie Yuanjing found her amusing.

"Almost fell down because you weren't watching where you were going, and somehow that becomes someone else's fault?"

Lu Huaixi pressed her lips together faintly. "I didn't say that."

The servants passing through this area occasionally caught sight of the Eldest Young Master and Young Mistress standing together — one looking up as she talked, one looking down with patient attention — and were somewhat surprised.

But surprised as they were, no one dared to stare.

When Lu Huaixi saw yet another person bow and pass by, she grew a little self-conscious and collected herself.

"Let's go."

"Mm."

Xie Yuanjing replied, but didn't move. "What were you thinking about just now?"

"...Nothing."

"Can't say?"

Of course she couldn't say.

Lu Huaixi looked away, speaking evasively. "Come on, let's go — I haven't even eaten noon meal yet, and I'm hungry."

Xie Yuanjing looked at her for a moment, the corner of his mouth curving slightly.

Then he reached out and lightly knocked on her head, and asked nothing more.

"Watch where you walk from now on."

"I know, I know."

—

Back at the Lu manor, it was only the second day after Lu Huaixi had married out, and the First Branch already felt noticeably quieter.

The eldest young miss, Lu Ningyou, was afraid her mother wouldn't adjust well and had come specially from her husband's home to keep her company, speaking in her gentle, careful way.

Whether her younger sister had ever had an engagement, she knew perfectly well. Lady Liu hadn't tried to hide it from her — but to spare her worry, she had left out the other details.

"Mother, Huaixi marrying is a happy occasion. You mustn't fret like this — and besides, you know what that girl is like. She can be cheerful anywhere. Are you really afraid she'll suffer?"

That much was true — yet Lu Huaixi was still so young, and she'd only just recently come to know that Xie from the Xie manor. Lu Ningyou was worried all the same.

"And the scene Xie Yuanjing made yesterday, Mother — you wouldn't believe it. Even my in-laws, who never pay attention to gossip, were talking about Xie Yuanjing. They said he must have truly set his heart on it."

Lady Liu's lips moved faintly, but she said nothing.

How could she tell her eldest daughter that her younger sister had married in name only — and would be separating after a year?

"Mother, stop worrying. Meeting someone, going through the wedding — most girls go through this. And Huaixi's got a young master who's both well-born and handsome — what more could you ask? Besides, I saw for myself yesterday that Huaixi seemed quite at ease with him. They seemed happy together."

"They seemed... happy?"

"Yes, Mother."

Lu Ningyou smiled. "Yesterday, that brother-in-law of mine made a point of going to speak with Huaixi — had her laughing several times. Everyone outside says he's hard to read and hard to get along with, but I didn't find that at all. At least not in front of Huaixi."

"I hadn't seen that."

Lady Liu sighed — but those words did ease something in her.

She knew perfectly well that worrying served no purpose, and the child had already married. What she needed to do was be her daughter's dependable support.

But being a mother — and knowing that her daughter had been rushed into this marriage to escape the palace, only to face a separation afterward — Lady Liu felt a debt of guilt no matter how she thought of it.

"I do hope they get along well. But you know your sister — she only looks well-behaved on the surface, enough to fool people, but she's actually willful. And Xie Yuanjing is so cold with everyone else..."

"Relax, Mother. From what I can see, my brother-in-law treats Huaixi quite well. Cold? Between those two, there will be warmth enough for many years yet."

"..."

Lady Liu felt more heartsick than ever.

The separation was always going to come. She had never believed Xie Yuanjing — a man like him — would change his mind. Nor did she imagine the two families would remain kin-by-marriage forever.

But Huaixi was at that tender, impressionable age. She didn't know — if she spent too long with Xie Yuanjing — whether the girl might begin to feel something more.

"Let it be. Their affairs are beyond what an outsider can touch. I only worry because the Marquis Manor isn't exactly serene."

"No family's inner household ever is — even our own Lu family —"

Something crossed Lu Ningyou's mind, and her expression cooled.

"I never imagined the Second Branch mother and daughter could have such vicious intentions. Has Grandfather said anything yet?"

At that, Lady Liu's expression also grew subdued.

The Old Master did feel grieved that Lu Huaixi might have gone to the palace. He had made up his mind to protect her. But the Second Branch was also Lu family.

Having learned that the First Branch wouldn't yield, the Old Master had come back around to persuade them several times.

In truth, he didn't want to send any of his granddaughters.

Lady Liu understood his difficulty. But she would not concede — nor would she let her daughter have suffered all this for nothing.

Her Huaixi should have been able to stay home a few more peaceful years, choosing slowly and carefully — waiting until her heart was ready, and then letting things unfold naturally.

Instead, all of that had been ruined by the Second Branch.

Not only had she been forced to marry so young, but she would carry the name of a separation afterward. No matter how Lady Liu thought of it, she couldn't swallow this.

"Regardless of whether your grandfather sends word or not — the Second Branch should not expect to quietly turn the page on this. It is not possible."

"I understand. If there's anything I can help with, Mother must tell me."

Lu Ningyou's eyes turned cold, recalling how a nanny had come to her yesterday to say that Lu Tangshu had apparently made an attempt to intercept Xie Yuanjing. She gave a cold smile.

Arrogance and recklessness, through and through.

On that alone — regardless of whether Xie Yuanjing was a good match for Huaixi or not — Lu Tangshu would find no peace.

"All right. I've said all I needed to say. Take care of yourself properly. I worry about Huaixi, but I also think of you."

"Don't worry, Mother. My in-laws and husband treat me well."

"I can see that — they wouldn't keep agreeing to let you slip out of the house if they weren't easygoing. Just stay a little while and head back — don't always be running around outside."

"No hurry. My husband is coming to collect me after he finishes his duties."

At this, Lu Ningyou smiled, her expression softening considerably.

"Only — Huaixi's return visit day, I won't be able to come. Otherwise we could have had a good long talk."

"You just stay home and rest properly."

Lady Liu glanced at Lu Ningyou's abdomen and couldn't help shaking her head. "She listens to you. As her elder sister, you'd better set her a good example."

"Naturally."

Lu Ningyou blinked, thinking of the small box of books she had slipped to her younger sister privately, and couldn't help smiling again.

Their mother had said privately that Huaixi was still young and that Xie from the Xie manor wouldn't do anything to her.

But some things — even if they came early — still needed to be taught.

chapters.title: How Kind of You
chapters.content:
Xie Madam's words were not continued — but the look on her face was enough to make the one who had stirred things up, Xie Third Madam, feel a small prick of indignation.

Mu Weimi had just managed to compose herself when she looked up and saw the Old Madam before her seemingly lost in thought following the First Branch's words.

Her heart sank.

Status was a shortcoming she could not change. But she could not let the Old Madam start reconsidering and shifting in favor of the Lu woman.

Thinking fast, she moved forward to take the Old Madam's arm, and spoke softly.

"Grand Aunt, please don't be angry — it's my fault for coming to deliver your medicine at a time like this. I should have excused myself just now, but when I heard Elder Sister-in-law say she wanted to spend my cousin's money, I was so startled I forgot what I was doing."

Hearing this, the Old Madam's expression dropped immediately.

"It's Weimi's inexperience," Mu Weimi pressed on. "I've never heard a woman speak so openly about taking her husband's money. I forgot myself."

The Old Madam, who hadn't found anything wrong with it a moment before, now thought back on it and felt genuinely displeased.

What kind of girl openly boasted about managing her husband's wealth like that? Truly spoiled — without a sense of propriety.

"You needn't apologize on her behalf."

"I know you care for me, Grand Aunt, but Third Aunt mentioned me, so I felt I had to explain."

Mu Weimi added: "Let me help you back to your room now. Elder Sister-in-law came so late — you've been sitting so long that your back must ache. I'll rub it for you when we return."

The Old Madam's expression darkened, and she left. As she went, she gave the First Madam a pointed look, her displeasure plain.

Walking out of the courtyard, the Old Madam suddenly stopped and spoke to someone nearby.

"Go and call Yuanjing's wife to my rooms."

"Let me go, Grand Aunt."

Mu Weimi stepped in to take the task, masking her feelings. "I should properly greet Elder Sister-in-law myself — can't have us be of the same household and not know each other."

The Old Madam thought for a moment, then nodded.

"I need to rest for a while first. Tell her to come after she's finished her morning meal."

—

Lu Huaixi had been wandering through the First Branch's section of the manor, walking leisurely, and was almost back to Xie Yuanjing's courtyard.

Yao Xu had been chatting with her the whole way, and both of them fell quiet only when they caught sight of a figure waiting at the path ahead.

"Weimi greets Elder Sister-in-law."

The moment Lu Huaixi drew close, the young woman gave her a proper curtsy.

She wore a young woman's hair arrangement, her makeup light, with only one striking jade plum-blossom pin. As she curtsied, her pale-colored gown fell in natural folds, shifting with her movement to cover the tops of her shoes.

It was the girl from the hall — the one who had stood behind the Old Madam.

Lu Huaixi looked at her, then curiously asked: "Elder Sister-in-law?"

Mu Weimi kept her head slightly bowed as she replied. "Yes. The manor's Old Madam is my Grand Aunt — she took me in when I was ten and brought me up at the Marquis Manor, so I grew up alongside my cousin."

Grew up alongside Xie Yuanjing.

Lu Huaixi nodded, and this time matched her up with the person her elder brother had described.

But having made the connection, she found herself in a slightly awkward position.

She might carry the title of mistress of the household — but she could hardly cut off whatever bond Xie Yuanjing might have with this person.

Especially since she had no way of knowing how much this woman meant to him. If this was someone he had kept close in his heart yet could never marry, there would be trouble enough ahead for the whole year.

"You're here to find your cousin?"

Lu Huaixi looked at her. "He's gone out. Why don't you come back later?"

Those words came out so naturally that Mu Weimi wasn't quite sure how to respond.

She had imagined countless versions of this encounter, but not once had she pictured being told, simply and straightforwardly, to come back later — as if none of it was worth worrying about.

"You — Elder Sister-in-law, you're truly willing to let me see my cousin?"

"Why wouldn't I be? Come whenever you like. You're both of this manor — no need to send a card of notice ahead. But today I won't invite you in — he's not here."

Mu Weimi was again left without a word.

She looked at the person before her, searching for the false magnanimity she expected to find.

There was nothing. Only a pretty, youthful face, and a pair of candid, unhurried eyes.

Some things could not be compared. The moment you tried, the one who fell short was already building her own cage.

"Elder Sister-in-law has misunderstood. Weimi didn't come today for my cousin."

Mu Weimi composed herself, bowing her head slightly and offering Lu Huaixi a quiet smile.

"My cousin would not wish to see me. I came because Grand Aunt would like to invite Elder Sister-in-law for a visit."

"Now?"

"Yes."

She made no mention of the Old Madam's need to rest first. Mu Weimi stepped aside slightly. "After you, Elder Sister-in-law. Don't keep Grand Aunt waiting again."

Lu Huaixi frowned. She didn't particularly care for the tone.

Nothing openly rude had been said — yet the air this woman carried made Lu Huaixi vaguely uncomfortable.

Or it might simply have been that she was hungry.

She had a modest appetite, but she needed to eat at every meal. Go without, and she would start to feel irritable.

"A little later."

Lu Huaixi thought it through quickly — recalling the morning incident with the Old Madam's nanny, and recalling Xie Yuanjing's response.

"I can't leave just yet. My husband asked me to return to the courtyard and get acquainted with the household."

"But the Old Madam —"

"I'll go apologize to Grandmother later myself. After all, what happens in the First Branch's courtyard — Grandmother won't be upset over that, I should think."

Lu Huaixi's voice was soft and gentle, and her face was all innocent charm.

But the reply she gave Mu Weimi carried a quiet finality that brooked no negotiation — and left the other woman disarmed.

After a moment, Mu Weimi smiled again.

"Elder Sister-in-law is right. My cousin's instructions take precedence."

Then she added: "Since Weimi is here, there is something else I wish to explain — it concerns the shoes sent last night."

So the shoes had been from her.

Lu Huaixi had felt a flicker of surprise for just a moment — and then it all made sense.

"My cousin is quite particular about shoes. I once promised him a pair but kept missing the chance. Afterward, there was some misunderstanding, and the matter was left unfinished. If Elder Sister-in-law saw that pair last night — please don't take it to heart."

"I won't."

Lu Huaixi gave a small, easy smile.

The shoes had already been thrown away. There was nothing left to take to heart.

Besides, the style of those shoes was not something a man who was particular about his footwear would ever wear.

"I'm glad Elder Sister-in-law isn't troubled. I had been listening to all manner of rumors lately in the company of the Old Madam, and I kept reassuring everyone — I said Elder Sister-in-law surely couldn't be that willful. Once you married in, you would certainly put the Marquis Manor and my cousin first in all things."

"How kind of you."

"..."

No matter what else Mu Weimi said after that, she received only the same unhurried, gentle response.

Like throwing a fist into cotton — the force rebounded right back at her.

Mu Weimi's patience gradually ran out, and she no longer wished to stay and talk.

Lu Huaixi had also gotten a general read on her intentions — but had no plan to expose them.

After Mu Weimi left, the only one who changed expression was Yao Xu.

She watched that retreating figure with undisguised wariness.

"Young Mistress — that Miss Mu came especially to see you, and she said all those things — she must have been up to nothing good. You must be on your guard, and never let it slip."

"She didn't come especially to see me. She came to see Xie Yuanjing, didn't she."

"...That's even more reason to be on guard, Young Mistress."

Yao Xu followed after her. "And I don't know what the Old Madam wants with you now — the nanny this morning already seemed a difficult sort. When you go over later, you must keep your wits about you..."

"Don't worry. I'll wait a while before going."

Lu Huaixi pulled back her attention and walked into the courtyard.

She had no particular desire to be magnanimous — to the point of severing someone else's bond. But she certainly wasn't going to rush to be accommodating, especially not toward someone whose company left her feeling unsettled.

Whether to be civil or not — she'd take her cue from Xie Yuanjing.

After all, of everyone in the Marquis Manor, only he and she were sailing in the same boat.

"I'm hungry."

Lu Huaixi let out a quiet sigh.

Married into this household and already denied a proper morning meal. She really was about to make a scene.

chapters.title: Don't Talk About My Wife
chapters.content:
By the time Xie Yuanjing reached the teahouse, it was still early.

The gathering had originally been planned at Shen Zhoushu's villa on the city's outskirts, but the place was a long ride away and the weather was growing warm, so they'd changed to Juxian Lou in the city.

When Xie Yuanjing was led to the private room, Shen Zhoushu and Qin Yiyun were already there.

One was talking of the hardships and ambitions that might await him over the next three to five years away — the other was half-listening, languid, the rakish corners of his eyes hazy with drowsiness.

Seeing who had arrived, both turned to look.

"Brother Yuanjing is here. You've been invited out the very day after your wedding — I do hope the young madam won't hold a grudge."

The speaker was Qin Yiyun — principled, with a slight tendency toward rigidity.

His transfer orders had come rather late. He'd also been held up by a separate matter and only now had a moment to breathe before he set off.

Xie Yuanjing and he had not had much dealings before, but the man had a stubborn streak. He had decided Xie Yuanjing was learned and perceptive, and had pestered him relentlessly ever since — until, in the end, something like a genuine bond of camaraderie had quietly taken shape.

Beside him sat Shen Zhoushu — the same man who had been in Xie Yuanjing's carriage that day. He was among the few Xie Yuanjing could genuinely call a friend.

He had been too lazy to attend tonight, but had heard Xie Yuanjing was coming — and decided to show up and watch the spectacle.

Seeing the man walk in now, the drowsiness faded from Shen Zhoushu's eyes.

"Our Xie Eldest Young Master is a married man now, and things are already different. The evening banquet had to be moved to midday."

Thinking of yesterday, he couldn't resist a jab. "I thought our Eldest Young Master Xie had no particular interest in the business of taking a wife. Who could have predicted that yesterday's ceremony would be carried off with such spectacle — by now I expect word has even reached the palace..."

Xie Yuanjing didn't find anything to take offense at.

He stepped into the private room — the expression on his face seldom animated — and then, without warning, smiled.

He found a seat and settled in, picked up the freshly poured cup before him, and raised it slightly in Qin Yiyun's direction.

He drank it down in one swallow, then set the cup aside. He picked up the napkin nearby and lightly wiped his fingers, an air of fastidious pride around him.

"When you go looking for someone, of course you put your heart into it."

He lowered his gaze, his tone unhurried and matter-of-fact.

Qin Yiyun was called out on some matter and was ushered away by an attendant. Seeing the private room was down to just the two of them, Shen Zhoushu dropped all pretense.

"Were you not the one who said something to the effect of mutual benefit and going through the motions? When did that change?"

Xie Yuanjing said nothing — like a man too lazy to bother with a reply.

Shen Zhoushu was already in a sour mood from having been dragged out of bed too early. Seeing this reaction, he was even less inclined to let it go.

"And who was it who wasn't going to make a fuss — prepared to be a hands-off sort of husband — said he didn't intend any grand ceremony?"

"Who said that?"

Xie Yuanjing countered calmly, then reached for the teacup beside him and poured himself a cup.

Shen Zhoushu was momentarily caught off-guard — he was just about to press further when Qin Yiyun pushed the door open and came back in, followed by a few others.

With the gathering now properly assembled, Shen Zhoushu collected himself and dropped the subject.

"Having the chance to sit together with good friends before leaving the capital is a great fortune for this Qin."

Qin Yiyun sat down and raised his cup. "I go far, and to distant places — it may be three to five years before we meet again. For all the support and friendship these past years, I raise this cup to each of you."

There was an undeniable sorrow to the toast — those who heard it could not help but feel a pang.

But Xie Yuanjing didn't. Nor did Shen Zhoushu.

One was long accustomed to a certain detachment from human bonds. The other had been drinking half the night and was too drowsy to muster much sentiment.

Not that either of them would have their lapses pointed out. The conversation pressed on, and the private room gradually filled with life.

It is a truth of the world that people will, sooner or later, turn from grand ambitions to idle gossip. Once the wine had gone around a few times, the young masters who had finished discussing life and purpose began to ask after each other's affairs.

The one sitting next to Qin Yiyun burped softly from the wine, then spoke.

"How is it we haven't seen the young lord from the Shao family? I thought he and Brother Qin were quite close — is he meeting up tonight instead?"

"Not possible."

Qin Yiyun smiled slightly and waved a hand — the wine was going to his head fast, and the man was turning a little rosy.

"Young Master Shao has some difficulty getting out of the house lately. It wouldn't have been appropriate for me to invite him."

"Difficulty getting out?"

The other pressed again. "Don't tell me the rumors are true — that he really has come to blows with the family?"

Telling tales about others' private affairs was not something Qin Yiyun would engage in. But someone else at the table picked up the thread.

"You could say he has — who could have imagined that Young Master Shao, of all people, would have the fire in him to sacrifice everything for love? They say he's willing to throw away his future entirely for that woman."

Xie Yuanjing still said nothing, and was not interested.

Shen Zhoushu had more of the ordinary human passions, and would chime in now and then when something caught his attention — but this particular story he couldn't follow, nor did he understand it.

"Didn't he have an engagement already? How does that become nothing?"

"Not nothing — more like: he never agreed to it in the first place. Says he's determined to marry only the one he loves. But the one he loves is a singer from a teahouse — not even fit to be taken home as a concubine."

Shen Zhoushu gave a short, dismissive sound and joined the others in a slow shake of his head.

Though he had an easy, almost careless air, he and Xie Yuanjing were, at their cores, much the same kind of men.

The power and position you held — those were what was real.

Besides, this kind of situation was hardly difficult to manage. Once the engagement was settled and one's footing was secure, taking the woman one favored into the rear court as a concubine was still perfectly possible. They could meet every day.

"Thick-headed. Rash now, plenty of time to regret later."

Shen Zhoushu said it, then glanced toward Xie Yuanjing. "What do you think?"

"Think about what?"

"Giving up a future for a beautiful woman — do you understand it?"

"I don't."

Xie Yuanjing said, then called out toward the door, "Gong Zhuo," and added: "For a beautiful woman to consume your thoughts night and day — can you understand that?"

"No."

Xie Yuanjing answered flatly. "But I don't need to understand it. In my case, there's no such conflict."

"...True enough. You've even taken home the noble daughter."

Shen Zhoushu snorted good-naturedly, then lowered his voice.

"And a wife taken not out of sentiment, at that — mutual respect and measured distance, neither one attached to the other. Heaven falling wouldn't give you, Xie Eldest Young Master, so much as a single day when you'd throw yourself into a blind rage for someone's sake."

"You know the answer — why ask?"

"You honestly don't envy other men their tender moments — moonlight and red sleeves?"

The reply was a quiet, understated laugh — as if the question didn't even warrant serious consideration.

"No need. Not envious."

Then Xie Yuanjing extended his right hand, fingers bent slightly, and knocked lightly on the table in front of Shen Zhoushu.

"When we're outside — don't talk about my wife."

With that, Gong Zhuo came forward and stopped at his side.

"Master."

Xie Yuanjing looked away. "Go to the kitchen and ask for a serving of sweet cake. Also have a few varieties of pastries and small sweets put together and packaged up. If I haven't come downstairs in a quarter of an hour, have them sent ahead to the manor."

Gong Zhuo paused for a moment, then realized this was meant for the young mistress.

He gave a quick nod and slipped out.

Xie Yuanjing didn't care for sweet things, and had never been the kind of man for these small attentions. Shen Zhoushu opened his mouth and then closed it again, remembering the warning just given.

Fine.

He'd ask nothing more. Looking after a ward — bringing the child a little snack — that was hardly something worth mentioning.

chapters.title: A Soft Blade for a Soft Blade
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi finished meeting the household members and listened to Gong Fei's lengthy account of everything in Xie Yuanjing's possession. In the end, she couldn't justify putting it off any longer, and made her way to the Old Madam's courtyard.

She had eaten a little something before leaving — but not much. By the time she'd walked that distance, she felt hungry again.

"Eldest Young Mistress, the courtyard is just ahead."

This time, Lu Huaixi had brought Jing Shuang along.

In the morning, still groggy, she hadn't paid much attention. Afterward, back in the courtyard, Jing Shuang had come to attend to her, and Lu Huaixi noticed that she never elbowed Yao Xu out of the way, never chimed in casually — just stood quietly behind her, and when there was something to be done, moved forward swiftly and capably. It was a presence that put one at ease.

Lu Huaixi had found herself lingering on those impressions.

It was a face with a hint of spirit to it — long hair pinned high, features slightly sharp, faintly stern in repose, the corners of her mouth just a touch too taut when she was silent. But when she spoke to Lu Huaixi, her voice gentled and she would smile a little, and the sternness softened into something reassuring.

"Eldest Young Mistress, don't be anxious. If the Old Madam makes things difficult for you or tries to punish you, just turn around and leave. No need to hesitate."

Lu Huaixi gave a small nod in reply, then turned to look at her.

"If someone comes to stop me, you could handle them, yes?"

"Yes. With me here, Young Mistress need not worry."

Lu Huaixi couldn't help but smile at that.

The only person in this world who would seriously contemplate coming to blows with her in-laws on the very second day of her marriage was probably herself.

Still thinking it over, a nanny appeared from the front, and paused in clear surprise on seeing her.

"This old servant greets the Eldest Young Mistress."

The woman gave her a respectful bow. "The Old Madam is still resting and has not yet woken. Eldest Young Mistress, you've come early — I'm afraid you'll need to wait a little."

"Have I come early?"

A look of puzzlement crossed Lu Huaixi's face.

From the time Mu Weimi had left to now, over an hour had passed. The Old Madam had already been waiting to see her before Mu Weimi even came — so she had waited, and still arrived early?

"Yes, indeed — the Old Madam may not know, but when she says she needs to rest, she truly does sleep for a while."

The nanny spoke, stepping slightly to one side. "It's sunny in the courtyard — please, come inside and have some tea. The Old Madam should be waking soon. I'll go look in on her."

Lu Huaixi couldn't have missed the meaning.

She followed the woman inside, the faint smile on her face thin and careful.

Right, then.

So it begins.

When the nanny withdrew, Lu Huaixi took her seat. The tea beside her was still too hot. She didn't drink it — her thoughts drifted with the steam.

"Sent a cousin over to call you, then left you sitting here — isn't that just deliberate cruelty?"

The room was empty, and Yao Xu could no longer hold it in.

Lu Huaixi showed no great feeling about it, and replied in a mild, easy tone.

"Well, of course it is."

Good thing she'd delayed before coming. If she had arrived immediately, she would have been caught between two equally bad options — stay and let the Old Madam embarrass not only her but the entire First Branch, or leave and give herself the reputation of being disrespectful.

Whether it was the Old Madam's idea or Mu Weimi's — she still couldn't tell.

"Miss — Young Mistress, you've been wronged."

"Wronged how? There's nothing to be wronged about. Now don't call me Miss — you need to say —" Lu Huaixi looked up at Yao Xu. "Eldest Young Mistress."

The way Lu Huaixi met her gaze was bright and cheerful — an obvious reassurance, with just a hint of playfulness in the tone, as if none of this bothered her at all. Like a child who had simply decided to turn a small irritation into a game.

Jing Shuang beside her, unable to help herself, glanced at the young woman in front of her. Seeing no trace of effort or performance — just a clear, lovely face entirely free of ill feeling — she felt her own expression twitch.

She quietly said: "Eldest Young Mistress, you may leave."

"I'm not leaving."

Lu Huaixi waved a hand with perfect indifference.

"If I leave now, what does that make me? That's handing over a weakness. I'm not going to make a loss."

Then she gave a soft huff — the minor exasperation of a child who refuses to back down — and muttered: "Wait till I see Xie Yuanjing and have a good long complaint."

It was said to be funny, and it was — but Lu Huaixi was never going to actually make a scene over it.

If she were truly Xie Yuanjing's wife, she might have felt some temper rising — at the Old Madam, or at Mu Weimi.

But she wasn't. To be blunt, she was an outsider temporarily residing here, and she had no particular interest in coming out on top of these small skirmishes.

What did genuinely bother her — only a little — was that this year had barely begun, and someone had already decided to find her trouble and interfere with her quiet life.

"All right. I've just not been kept waiting, that's all. You two are more put out than I am."

Lu Huaixi raised her teacup, smiling as she murmured the remark.

She was perfectly at ease — the words had been said to soothe Yao Xu, so she wouldn't be fretting and sending word back to her mother about nothing.

The tea was still warm in her hands when she heard movement from the inner room — a few soft coughs.

Lu Huaixi had barely looked over when someone came in from outside, walking quickly toward the inner room, moving with an urgency that suggested she hadn't noticed Lu Huaixi sitting there — or was pretending not to.

Like someone who knew exactly how visible she was in these rooms, and was making a point of it.

"Grand Aunt, you're awake."

The voice that followed was full of concern.

"Does your back still hurt? You waited so long for Elder Sister-in-law, and then didn't put on your medicine — you really can't keep sitting for so long. Later I'll walk with you in the courtyard."

Lu Huaixi, hearing it was Mu Weimi, was in even less of a hurry.

She leisurely touched her teacup — waited until the curtain swayed and parted — and then stood, bowed her head, and greeted the Old Madam: "Your granddaughter-in-law greets Grandmother."

The Old Madam had just woken, her throat dry. She only gave a faint sound of reply, raised a hand for a cup of water, and drank.

After a moment, she sat down, and her expression cleared somewhat.

"You've been here a while?"

"Not long at all, Grandmother."

Lu Huaixi smiled again, looking a shade sheepish.

"I arrived over an hour late — I didn't know how to apologize to Grandmother. I truly couldn't get away from the courtyard — I hope Grandmother won't be upset."

"Not late at all. Just right."

The Old Madam's tone was not particularly warm, but it was acceptable. "If you had come earlier, I'd still have been resting. I tire easily at my age."

"That you're not upset is the best news."

Lu Huaixi nodded. "Weimi told me to come right away — she didn't mention that Grandmother needed to rest first. I did panic for a moment, but it seems Grandmother is forgiving."

Mu Weimi looked over at that.

She had deliberately set a trap — wanting Lu Huaixi to arrive and be left sitting, so that the Old Madam would see it as the new wife being disrespectful and show her power by lecturing her.

She had also planned her excuse: if it came out, she could push the blame onto Lu Huaixi — say she hadn't understood the message, or that Lu Huaixi had done it on purpose.

But Lu Huaixi had refused to come, smiling all the while.

Before Mu Weimi had managed to say anything to the Old Madam, this woman had brought it up herself.

Looked soft and guileless — but she struck with a quiet blade.

The Old Madam heard this, fell silent for a moment, and when she looked up at the figure before her, the eyes that had settled a little deeper with age carried a measuring quality.

Lu Huaixi looked back at her with cheerful openness, her gaze clear.

After a pause, the Old Madam stepped back first.

"It may have been that Weimi didn't explain clearly. No matter — I only called you here to sit and talk. Where is Yuanjing?"

"Grandmother, he's gone out — to visit a colleague."

Both the women before her went still at this, and then one fell into thought, while the other shifted from anger to a private, pleased gloating.

Lu Huaixi appeared not to notice, her smile directed at the Old Madam as before.

"Just now I heard from Weimi that you had been waiting for me and that your back had begun to ache. I'm sorry for that — I should have hurried my husband along this morning."

Before the Old Madam could respond, Lu Huaixi continued:

"Grandmother, have you seen a physician about your back? It could be anything from a minor complaint to something more serious. Applying medicine isn't a real treatment — you really ought to see someone properly. Ideally, there might be acupuncture. As it happens, I know a physician — rather a skilled one."

From start to finish, the delivery had the steadiness and consideration that went beyond her years, leaving the Old Madam with nothing to take issue with.

Meanwhile, Mu Weimi had caught the news that Xie Yuanjing had gone out of the manor the very morning after his wedding — and her spirits lifted.

If not for indifference — how could a man leave his new bride at home on a day like this and go off to meet others?

He put no weight on Lu Huaixi at all.

She had already talked herself back into composure. Now, the thought that Xie Yuanjing didn't care sent a surge of private satisfaction through her.

Whatever her rank, Lu Huaixi was still just someone unloved — still someone who had to cater to the Old Madam, to get through her days in the rear court.

Mu Weimi couldn't help looking over, a flash of contempt in her gaze.

What did a high birth matter? No matter how she had turned the tables just now — she was still without favor, still the one who had to smile and court the Old Madam's goodwill in order to have a foothold in the Xie family's rear court.

chapters.title: Just Won't Take the Bait
chapters.content:
Mu Weimi could not help but look over, contempt flickering in her eyes.

What did rank matter? No matter how she had managed to turn things just now — she was still unloved — still needed to smile and please the Old Madam just to keep her footing in the Xie rear court.

"Elder Sister-in-law may not know — but the physician attending to Grand Aunt is among the very best in the capital, acquainted even with the Palace physicians. This medicine was specially prepared by the physician for Grand Aunt — and winning that physician's time was no small thing. I pestered him for a great many days before he agreed."

Mu Weimi smiled slightly, sitting a little straighter.

"Elder Sister-in-law needn't try to please Grand Aunt by casually recommending someone. This is the back — no room for error. And acupuncture in particular..."

She shook her head, with the air of gently correcting someone who didn't know better. "Elder Sister-in-law is still young, after all. Below the needle is not something just anyone can do — that would be reckless."

"Is that so."

Lu Huaixi listened with genuine attention, and when Mu Weimi remarked on her youth, she even gave an approving nod.

"Elder Sister-in-law, forgive me for being direct. In my years keeping Grand Aunt company, I've come to know her well — what works and what doesn't. Elder Sister-in-law, raised in comfort and pampered at home, sometimes hears something and assumes it's good — like a child playing — when it really isn't. There's still much to learn, and it takes care and attention."

"You're right. I've never attended to anyone before — I don't know these things. I was careless."

When Lu Huaixi smiled, the outer corners of her eyes curved downward just slightly — a playful arc, without a hint of temper, her whole demeanor obedient and lovely.

Mu Weimi suddenly found herself looking at her with envy.

She still couldn't tell if Lu Huaixi was mocking her for being practiced in the ways of a servant — or if she truly was this guileless and couldn't read a compliment from an insult.

But in this moment, Mu Weimi felt a private pleasure too. She couldn't best Lu Huaixi on birth — but she could on other things.

Lu Huaixi might be of high standing, but she still had to listen to the Old Madam inside this manor.

And with Xie Yuanjing indifferent, Lu Huaixi was nothing at all.

"Elder Sister-in-law, don't be upset — when Elder Sister-in-law has time, I'll teach you slowly about things here in the manor."

"Then I'll rely on you, Weimi. I truly am no good at attending to people — I didn't know that the Old Madam's back couldn't just be looked at by any physician."

Lu Huaixi accepted this, then added: "I had been thinking, the next time I visit Old Master Yuan, to ask Little Doctor Ceng to come. But it's a good thing I heard from Weimi today."

"No matter — Elder Sister-in-law, you —"

"Which Old Master Yuan?"

Mu Weimi had not yet recovered, when the Old Madam, who had been silent for some time, suddenly spoke, her gaze turning toward her.

The previous Empress had been of the Xie family. Though she had passed away some years ago and the Xie family had not spoken of her since, they remained well-acquainted with the people of the palace — particularly the few senior physicians of the Imperial Medical Bureau.

Hearing Lu Huaixi mention "Old Master Yuan" and a "Little Doctor Ceng," the Old Madam immediately thought of the retired former head of the Imperial Medical Bureau.

But could someone like that be invited by Lu Huaixi?

"Grandmother, it's Old Master Ceng from the former Imperial Medical Bureau. Little Doctor Ceng is the Old Master's daughter — the one called the Female Healer outside."

"Doctor Ceng?"

The Old Madam was genuinely surprised. "You have a personal acquaintance with Doctor Ceng? That man retired and refused to deal with anyone of power or rank in the capital anymore. How did you come to know him?"

"He is indeed difficult. Quite a temperament."

Lu Huaixi couldn't help but give a small pout — though she quickly composed herself. "A chance meeting when I was young. We've kept in touch since."

There had been few physicians of strange temper in the capital, and after Old Master Ceng retired, he had let go of everything — as if something had unlocked within him, and what he had held himself back from before no longer concerned him.

The chance meeting Lu Huaixi spoke of was exactly that — an accident. And afterward she'd been roped into cultivating certain medicinal herbs for the old man.

Her luck had always run better than most, and whatever she tended with her own hands seemed always to thrive.

"Since Grandmother already has a physician attending to her, I won't presume to overstep. I spoke out of turn just now — I hope Grandmother and Weimi won't laugh at my ignorance."

No physician brought in by Mu Weimi could hold a candle to Old Master Ceng or his daughter Little Doctor Ceng.

Even speaking of Little Doctor Ceng alone — she was the Female Healer that others could barely hope to reach, who had gone from being dismissed as a woman to being sought after desperately, truly beyond price.

With those words spoken, neither of the two women before her looked particularly pleased.

One could not quite keep her dignity, feeling as though the young woman had shown no proper deference.

The other's face had gone iron-still — as if she had been slapped several times and made a fool of in plain sight.

Lu Huaixi paid no attention to either of them. They said nothing — she said nothing — and simply sat there, drinking her tea and eating the pastries, entirely at her leisure.

After a long silence, the Old Madam finally couldn't hold it back any longer. She drew a deep breath, and took the initiative to speak.

"You do have filial heart."

She stretched a thin smile. "It's true that Weimi has been with me these past years and is unfamiliar with many people — not being able to think this far ahead is understandable. A bit of a joke, in the end."

Lu Huaixi only smiled and said nothing.

The Old Madam pressed further: "You shouldn't worry yourself about going to visit Old Master Ceng — the manor will prepare the gifts for you. You've only just arrived — in the manor you're still of an age for play, so don't feel constrained."

"Grandmother mustn't tease me. I'll do my best to learn how to manage the household — learning from Mother and the other madams, and from Weimi as well."

Lu Huaixi half-lowered her head, as if a little abashed.

"I could never tease you. Your mother adores you, and Grandmother certainly won't bother you. You have nothing to worry about here."

"Is that so."

Lu Huaixi finally lifted her head again, giving a small smile. "Then I'm relieved."

No matter what the Old Madam said, Lu Huaixi simply wouldn't take the bait. Even when the words were pushed right up to her face, she responded only with pleasantries and smiles.

Mu Weimi's expression had long since gone visibly sour, the churning behind her eyes impossible to suppress.

She could feel that the Old Madam, in this moment, had been irritated by Lu Huaixi's responses into redirecting her frustration at her — a thing that had not happened in years.

—

Xie Yuanjing still had no idea that the girl he had brought home was quietly making a scene inside because she hadn't eaten a proper morning meal.

Just now he walked in, looked up, and saw the untouched food box on the table, still with its lid on.

"You don't like it?"

"Young Master, the eldest young mistress went to the Old Madam's courtyard a while ago and still doesn't know you had something sent back for her."

Xie Yuanjing's brow furrowed.

"How long has she been gone? Who went with her?"

He spoke while already moving toward the door, without even pausing to change his outer robe.

"Just under an hour. Her own maidservant and Jing Shuang went with her."

chapters.title: I Came to Fetch You
chapters.content:
When Lu Huaixi left the Old Madam's courtyard, her steps were light and her eyes were curved with a smile. She even hummed a soft tune as she walked — entirely unhurried.

She had no intention of actively harming anyone. But she equally had no intention of sitting still while others took advantage of her.

In the end, she had not opened her mouth to offer Little Doctor Ceng again, and had not told the Old Madam when she intended to call on Old Master Ceng.

But she hadn't closed the door on it either. She'd left it exactly where it lay — for whoever wished to reach for it to reach.

Yao Xu followed behind. She knew very well that her mistress was acquainted with Old Master Ceng — but she couldn't quite see why her mistress would go to such lengths for the Marquis Manor's Old Madam.

"Eldest Young Mistress, are you truly going to ask Little Doctor Ceng to come to the manor?"

Personal bonds were personal bonds. Favors were favors.

Yao Xu wasn't small-minded, but she had no love for people who had been unkind to Lu Huaixi. Spending that kind of goodwill on someone like that didn't feel worth it.

"You'd come for free even if she didn't actually accept you — but that woman seems like she won't ever acknowledge your kindness anyway. And that Miss Mu from earlier —"

The words trailed off as Yao Xu stole a glance at Jing Shuang beside her, and let it go.

Lu Huaixi understood perfectly what Yao Xu was thinking — she just couldn't explain it all at the moment.

"I don't know yet whether I'll invite her or not — we'll see. As for the others, don't mind them — they're not really anything to do with us."

Lu Huaixi's tone was easy, a smile still on her lips.

She was asking for Little Doctor Ceng not for the Old Madam's sake but for her own.

The year ahead held unknown variables. How many twists and turns were hidden inside the Marquis Manor, she — an outsider just arrived — had no way to see clearly.

And then there was her relationship with Xie Yuanjing.

The two of them were bound together for a year, and she couldn't very well go on indefinitely without "consummating the marriage."

But she didn't trust the manor's people — and even less the manor's physicians.

She needed someone she knew and trusted to establish themselves in front of the Xie family's people through legitimate means, and then be openly at her disposal.

That way, when Xie Yuanjing was away, she'd have her own physician — no one could take advantage of the gaps.

"I imagine it must be past the noon meal hour by now? I'm hungry."

Lu Huaixi stepped onto the covered walkway, and when she was sure there was no one nearby, raised a hand to pat her stomach.

The Xie Old Madam seemed to have no trouble going without food — and apparently enjoyed drawing things out, waiting for her to be the first to crack and speak.

"I forgot to give the instruction before I left. I don't know if they prepared the noon meal — they might think I'm eating in another courtyard."

The thought of food made her voice, which had been brisk until now, soften into a trace of aggrieved petulance — faint and high, a little childlike.

Behind her, the ever-composed Jing Shuang gave an involuntary laugh, the gaze she directed at Lu Huaixi instantly warming.

"It's been prepared, Eldest Young Mistress. Just a little more patience — once you're back in the courtyard, you can eat."

"Really?"

Lu Huaixi turned to look at her, dark eyes opening just a fraction wider, pupils black and bright.

"Yes. The Eldest Young Master specifically before he left —"

"How long have you been out here?"

The words were cut short by a sudden voice.

All three of them looked over at once.

Lu Huaixi immediately caught sight of Xie Yuanjing's clear, refined features not far away, and froze for a moment — then, understanding breaking through, gave a small, happy leap and jogged toward him.

"You're back so early — how?"

She tilted her face up, chin lifted just slightly, the line of her jaw a lovely curve.

Sunlight fell on Lu Huaixi's face, illuminating the clarity of her fair skin — like flawless white jade, perfect and unblemished — making one momentarily lose oneself in looking.

Xie Yuanjing's gaze met hers instinctively, then dropped slightly.

Whether it was the wine he'd had, or something else, he suddenly felt a little thirsty, his mind not as clear as usual.

"The wine finished early. Didn't stay for the noon meal."

Xie Yuanjing steadied himself, and his gaze went back to her eyes. "You were in there so long — did the Old Madam make things difficult for you?"

"She didn't make things difficult. I just may not have gotten around to everything."

"Not gotten around to it?"

"Mm, mm."

Lu Huaixi nodded several times, and thinking of what had just happened, pressed a hand over her smile. "I'll tell you when we get back."

Then, as if only just remembering something, she looked in the direction Xie Yuanjing had come from. "Were you heading somewhere? Then I won't hold you up — I can tell you later."

Xie Yuanjing didn't know why, but he laughed a little too, and followed her quieter tone.

"Nowhere to be."

He said: "I came to fetch you."

Lu Huaixi looked up and saw Xie Yuanjing's handsome face — the man's eyes narrowed just slightly, those dark pupils deep and still.

Having drunk a little, the usual air that kept everyone at arm's length had thinned. The whole person carried a languid, unhurried ease, and when the corner of his mouth curved, there was an indescribable, effortless charm.

Lu Huaixi's heart gave a sudden, sharp leap.

She wanted to step back a couple of paces and let it settle — but found, to her own lack of dignity, that she failed completely.

She simply did not want to move.

—

Back in the Old Madam's courtyard.

The frustration the Old Madam had held back now came down in full on Mu Weimi.

The words were not particularly harsh — after all, this was someone she had raised, whom she deeply trusted.

But Mu Weimi heard every one of them. She kept her head low, as if she knew her fault — eyes reddening, a tear threatening to fall. And yet beneath her sleeves, her hands were clenched so tight they were almost tearing the handkerchief apart.

After a long while, the Old Madam seemed to tire of speaking.

Seeing the pathetic, grieved look on the face before her, she finally softened her tone a little.

"Next time, don't act on your own impulse in front of her. She's a Lu family born legitimate daughter — that rank speaks for itself. Of course she would know people of consequence. You rushed in without knowing her measure first, and now you've made a fool of yourself."

"Weimi understands. Grand Aunt, please don't be upset."

"If you want me not to be upset, act with more care going forward. Keep certain feelings that should not be visible — keep them hidden."

"Yes, Weimi understands."

Seeing the person before her ease just slightly, Mu Weimi stepped forward and said quietly:

"It was my fault just now. I was too concerned for Grand Aunt's health, and momentarily forgot that Elder Sister-in-law might truly know such a remarkable physician. When it's a little later, Weimi will go and make her apologies to Elder Sister-in-law — ask her not to be at odds with Grand Aunt."

A veiled insinuation hidden in those words of apology.

Mu Weimi was of course unwilling to accept this. She still wasn't fully convinced.

As she saw it, if Lu Huaixi really could summon that kind of physician at will, she wouldn't have gone on speaking in circles and refused to simply agree outright.

Especially when Xie Yuanjing clearly didn't care about her situation.

If Lu Huaixi hadn't been doing it deliberately — then she had simply lied to the Old Madam. In that case, going to apologize was nothing.

Turning it over in her mind, Mu Weimi finally suppressed the churning from before.

"Grand Aunt, please eat first. Don't let Weimi's matters make you upset on your own behalf."

"Good that you can think of it that way."

The Old Madam closed her eyes briefly, then opened them. "Yuanjing's rear court, in the end, will not always have only one person. Eventually, someone who can soothe him — who understands the moment — must be there."

"Weimi understands. As long as I can care for you and my cousin, I'm willing to do anything. Even if I can never truly be my cousin's person — not a word of complaint will cross my lips."

Outside, the Second Madam Qi Miaoji, just arriving with the herbal medicine, happened to catch those last two lines.

She couldn't help curling her lip, a flicker of contempt in her eyes for this so-called cousin.

"Still daydreaming when the bride has already married in."

The nanny beside her was alarmed and quickly tried to hush her: "We're in the Old Madam's courtyard — Second Madam, that sort of talk really can't be said here."
