Xie Yuanjing looked at her. "Did you hear what I just said?"

Without waiting for her reply, he continued, "I was indeed angry. From the moment I heard you'd reported it to the authorities until now — I've been holding it in the whole way here."

Outside, passersby occasionally glanced over, and seeing the two standing so close, they couldn't help but look.

Lu Huaixi had none of the composure she'd had earlier. She felt as though she had been enveloped entirely in Xie Yuanjing's breath, her whole body stiff and buzzing — save for the side of her neck, where a sensation she couldn't ignore continued to make itself known.

Like a caress. Like a reprimand.

"W — why are you angry? Can we go inside and sit down to talk? Please?"

Xie Yuanjing didn't move. His fingertip rested beside that thin mark.

With just a little more pressure, the skin beneath his touch would bloom a faint, pale flush of red.

"Today it was only a handful of easy-to-handle ruffians. But if what came instead had been hired killers, desperate men who would risk their lives for money, outlaws willing to do anything — do you think the few people you had with you could have kept you safe long enough for the constables to arrive?"

"It wasn't that dire...... I do know my limits. If I couldn't handle it, I wouldn't have tried to fight head-on."

She paused, then asked quietly, "Is that why you're angry?"

Xie Yuanjing neither confirmed nor denied it. He only lowered his voice and asked her, "So you'll keep going out on your own from now on."

He said: "Keep cutting me out of things, handling everything yourself — is that it?"

chapters.title: Are You Still Angry?
chapters.content:
Though Xie Yuanjing's voice was not loud, it carried a sternness that was not usually there.

Lu Huaixi parted her lips but could say nothing, and the look she turned on him was, inexplicably, tinged with grievance.

"I didn't."

After a long pause, she finally forced out those two words.

She didn't like his cold severity. It reminded her of a tutor who was about to scold a student — yet with more weight to it than any tutor she'd known.

Xie Yuanjing hadn't meant to frighten her. He had thought it through on the way over — he would speak to her calmly and properly.

But when he had seen the wreckage covering the floor inside, and then the thin red mark on her neck left by a flying shard of porcelain, he had suddenly changed his mind.

Or rather — his temper had suddenly become harder to hold in.

He wanted her to understand: cutting him out had been her greatest mistake today.

"This one thin little mark — left by nothing more than a stray shard of flying porcelain. By tomorrow or the day after it will be gone without a trace. But if what had flown at you today were a blade — have you given any thought to what that would mean?"

"...... No. But I know."

Lu Huaixi lowered her head. Her expression was taut, and after holding it in for another moment, she finally spoke, each word stiff and reluctant. "I did make sure they were just ordinary ruffians first. And I never meant to cut you out — I only—"

"You only thought that the Lu family name was enough, and that you didn't need anyone else."

Xie Yuanjing cut her off. "I'm telling you now: it isn't."

"You——"

"I won't stop you from going out on your own from now on. But you must have my people with you at all times, and I cannot be the last to know about your affairs."

Not wanting to stand there while she searched for some excuse to put him off, not wanting to see her frown and refuse, Xie Yuanjing spoke first.

When the words had landed, he pressed his fingertip again to the spot beside that mark — harder this time than before.

He only let go when he heard Lu Huaixi make a small sound of pain, and then he looked at her again.

"Good. If it hurts, remember it well. Same as what I said before — if you won't listen, I really will punish you."

Xiyuan came out to ask forgiveness while the two of them were still standing outside the entrance.

The two matrons from earlier had not touched her — they had simply looked her over briefly and exchanged a few words, without a trace of impatience or contempt.

And once Xiyuan learned that Lu Huaixi was actually the proprietress of Shun'an Fang, the realization slowly dawned on her: it was the proprietress who had been protecting her all along. Though she had agreed to go along with it, she hadn't truly let anyone touch her, not wanting Xiyuan to suffer.

And precisely because of that, Xiyuan felt all the more guilty.

Wiping her tears, she shuffled her way to the front — but the moment she began to speak, she sensed something was off.

"Pro — Proprietress......"

There was much she had wanted to say — beg the proprietress to punish her, and thank the proprietress for standing up for her — but she had barely managed two words before the man standing before her proprietress gave her such a fright that her voice died in her throat.

A nobleman in fine brocade robes, with an upright bearing and a severe, striking face.

His appearance was breathtaking, but the air about him made one's heart seize.

Xiyuan's feet locked in place — unable to go forward, wrong to retreat.

In the end it was Lu Huaixi who noticed her discomfort, and gave a light cough.

"Why have you come out?"

Lu Huaixi's voice was steady, even with a note of reassurance in it, and Xiyuan drew a steadying breath at the sound.

Only Lu Huaixi herself knew that the composure she wore right now was holding on by a thread.

She didn't want to show any weakness in front of the girls. She didn't want them to think their proprietress was being lectured.

"Nothing is the matter out here. Those troublemakers won't be making another appearance so easily. Rest and recover — we can talk once you're well."

"Thank you, Proprietress. I — I......"

Xiyuan stumbled to a stop several times, her furtive glances at Xie Yuanjing catching in Lu Huaixi's eye — and somehow making Lu Huaixi feel a kinship with her.

They were both afraid of him. That was not a problem unique to her.

"Don't think on those things anymore. From now on, stay close to Sister Qingling. Shun'an Fang is still the same Shun'an Fang — nothing will change."

Perhaps because Xie Yuanjing's presence was simply too daunting, not a single one of the things Xiyuan had prepared to say made it out. She only lingered for a moment longer, before retreating to the back under Lu Huaixi's gentle reassurances.

After she left, the interrupted Lu Huaixi let out a quiet sigh — though the brief interlude had, in its way, steadied her considerably.

"Would you like to come in for some tea?"

She asked it casually.

Lu Huaixi didn't actually expect the man, who had just finished reprimanding her, to have any inclination to step inside. But after the words left her mouth, Xie Yuanjing actually nodded.

She blinked again. "Don't you have duties to attend to today?"

"So that question just now was your way of showing me the door?"

Xie Yuanjing shot back, drawing out a flicker of guilty color in her expression.

"Of course not."

Lu Huaixi touched her nose, and seeing that he had no intention of changing his mind, she turned sideways and, bracing herself, said, "I was just worried you'd be bored — that there wouldn't be much to your liking here."

"Not much inclination for it, no."

Xie Yuanjing picked up the thread. "But Lu Huaixi — I am your husband in name. I came out of my way to back you up. Even if you didn't need it, this scene still needs to be played out in full."

"In name......"

Something hesitant crossed Lu Huaixi's eyes, and then came understanding.

He meant he wanted people to see that they were on good terms.

"Oh. I understand."

"Understand what?"

Xie Yuanjing let out a quiet breath and fell into step behind her.

"Don't go listening to things by halves."

Lu Huaixi led him up to a private room upstairs. Only after she had climbed the wooden staircase did it occur to her — those words had another half to them.

He had come out of his way. To back her up.

—

After the group had been taken away, someone followed behind the constables.

The bound man worked the gag out of his mouth and spat hard in the direction of the woman beside him.

He was just about to launch into a torrent of abuse when the nearest constable drove a kick squarely into him.

"Keep still! Still looking to cause trouble!"

"Officer — Officer, I've been wronged!"

The man, seizing the chance, bellowed toward the one in the lead.

"It's all this woman's fault! She heard a few rumors from someone and there was no stopping her — I got nagged to death until I had no choice but to follow her there. I never wanted any trouble, Officer — I swear!"

The constable nearby was about to order him to shut his mouth when the one in the lead suddenly seemed to think of something and gestured for him to hold off.

"You smashed up a shop and hurt people. You think a few rumors will get you out of this?"

"I wouldn't dare try to fool you, Officer! It really was this woman who heard people say that kicking up a fuss was the way to get things done, and she rushed out there to make a spectacle of herself! If you don't believe me, Officer, question her yourself!"

Seeing that the constable showed no sign of letting him off, the man turned his head and cursed at the woman a few times, then went back to pleading.

"I'm innocent, Officer, I really am! That woman's no pushover either, I'll tell you that much. My wife used to work for her — did quite a lot of jobs for her! This has nothing to do with me! It's all because this jealous woman decided to take things into her own hands and hire those ruffians to cause trouble! That's the truth!"

"Which woman?"

"The embroidery shop on the west end of the city, on the front street. But she's already closed up and gone back to her hometown — left just a few days ago! That gossipy woman — if I ever run into her again, I swear I'll——"

"Enough!"

The man had been about to shout something else when something seemed to click in his mind. "Officer — I didn't hurt anyone, Officer! Just now I only lost my temper a bit because that girl provoked me, and I smashed a few things — I didn't hurt a soul!"

The constable beside him shot him a look, then stuffed the gag back in his mouth.

Not far behind, someone had been listening to all of this. They noted down: embroidery shop, west end of the city.

But the listener did not leave. Nor were they convinced.

"Keep watching. Dig further."

The person gave a low instruction.

The man's words had clearly been trying to steer the blame toward the woman's jealousy. If it stuck, the whole matter would be judged lightly.

But the silver found in both of their homes, and the way they had handled themselves throughout — it all pointed to something planned well in advance.

If that was the case, their target had not been only Shun'an Fang.

chapters.title: I'll Coax You a Little
chapters.content:
In the private room upstairs at Shun'an Fang, Lu Huaixi had just settled Xie Yuanjing into a seat when Qingling came in carrying a card.

"Proprietress."

She didn't dare look at the Young Master of the Xie family sitting beside them, keeping her head down with careful composure.

"This is a card from the owner of the tavern at the corner of the street. He says it's the first time he's seeing who the proprietress of Shun'an Fang actually is, and since they're all on the same street, he hopes you'll do him the honor of sharing a cup of tea and getting acquainted. Their owner also sent a gift along with it, and said he'd like to discuss some business together — but I didn't let them leave it."

Lu Huaixi took the card and glanced at it, but made no move to open it.

"That tavern at the corner? Weren't they always trying to squeeze out our business at Shun'an Fang? Didn't they even scheme to poach our people?"

"Yes. They probably never imagined, that our proprietress would be you."

Qingling agreed. "Just now, the one who brought the card looked utterly terrified — didn't dare meet anyone's eyes in here, afraid of what he might see. If this were before, would they have ever come to us with an attitude like this?"

Lu Huaixi gave a light snort and tossed the card aside.

"What a quick change of face. Before, their people were saying Shun'an Fang is all women, that we couldn't manage things — and now they want to invite this very woman over for tea. Hmph. Who wants to drink tea with them? Do they even have anything worth drinking, that they have the nerve to invite me?"

Qingling was tickled by Lu Huaixi's sulky tone.

But because of who was sitting nearby, she held it in.

"Then I'll go and decline them. Left and right, Shun'an Fang and their tavern have never gotten along anyway — and word is their tavern recently brought in a batch of girls from the south and is keeping them in the back courtyard. Sounds like they're planning to turn the tavern into something else."

Lu Huaixi's brow creased.

It was plain to see what kind of business they intended to run — the very kind Shun'an Fang refused to.

But she didn't particularly want to dwell on that. She was weighing her options: was it more worthwhile to have a falling out with them entirely, or to preserve some thin veneer of civility?

"Wait."

Before long, Lu Huaixi called Qingling back. "The corner spot is the prime location on this street. We never burned the bridge with them completely before — there's even less reason to now. Besides, they wouldn't dare try anything anymore. You go and tell them——"

"No need to go."

The quiet Xie Yuanjing, who had said nothing until now, suddenly spoke. His cool, measured voice made Qingling, who had only just relaxed, tense up all over again.

"Go and turn them down. Tell them I said so — and that they should think carefully about just who they're sending invitations to."

He paused, then glanced at Qingling, and called for Gong Zhuo with a slight furrow of his brow.

"Go with her. Tell them: the Young Madam is just amusing herself. If they want to talk business, they come to me."

No one would actually dare seek out the Young Master of a marquis estate. The words were plainly a warning — delivered in person, from his own mouth.

Qingling looked over at Lu Huaixi. She saw that though Lu Huaixi's eyes had gone wide at his words, looking rather startled, she clearly had no intention of objecting.

Qingling thought it over, pressed her lips into a quiet smile, bowed her head, and withdrew.

"Something small like this — I didn't think you'd bother."

Once there was no one else in the room, Lu Huaixi spoke softly, and with genuine gratitude.

A matter of business on the same street — if she were the one to refuse, it would always invite comment. But accepting wasn't exactly a good idea either. And yet with Xie Yuanjing's word, she had been cleanly excused, and he had backed her up all at once.

"Something small like this — I thought Proprietress Lu wouldn't want me involved."

Xie Yuanjing echoed her phrasing, and there was something in it — the faintest trace of reproach — that inexplicably made Lu Huaixi laugh.

"What are you doing — why are you copying what I say?"

The words had barely left her mouth when a knock came at the door of the private room.

It opened, and Qirui came in carrying tea and refreshments, along with a plate of beautifully made rabbit-shaped soft cakes.

Something Lu Huaixi was fond of.

"These are from Xiyuan."

Qirui noticed Lu Huaixi staring at them and couldn't help smiling. "She said she was sorry for the trouble she caused you. She didn't dare come and bother you again, so she made some of the things you usually like."

Lu Huaixi didn't make any fuss over it, just smiled the way she always did and took a bite.

"Delicious — the sweetness is just right!"

She scooped up another bite, then said, "When Xiyuan has a free moment, have her think up more things like this. I'll want them again the next time I come."

"Of course. I'll go pass that along."

Qirui said nothing else. She gave a small bow to both Lu Huaixi and Xie Yuanjing, and withdrew with the empty tray.

But everyone who had heard understood: this was Lu Huaixi putting Xiyuan's heart at ease.

Xie Yuanjing's gaze had come to rest on Lu Huaixi's face and stayed there. Only after she had finished the last small bite did he finally speak.

"If you didn't want people knowing about your connection to Shun'an Fang, why not keep concealing it?"

He said quietly, "If you wanted to hide it, you easily could have."

Lu Huaixi dabbed at the corner of her mouth with a handkerchief, then took a sip of tea.

Xie Yuanjing without his anger was a different person — his voice gentle, and after having just stood up for her too. Sitting quietly like this, the sound of him talking felt oddly comfortable, and she found herself suddenly trusting him a little more.

"It wasn't that I had to hide it."

She curved her eyes into a smile and looked at him. "That girl earlier, Xiyuan — she's a little younger than me. And besides her, there are plenty of other young girls in Shun'an Fang. The youngest is only seven."

"Because she wants to be a dancer?"

"Not entirely, I think — but a lot of them are girls who couldn't get enough to eat. I didn't think much of it before, but today made it clear to me: a proprietress who stays in the shadows can't hold a place like this together. Without any real backing, the girls here will always end up being pushed around."

Lu Huaixi said it calmly, in a quiet voice:

"I'm not anyone particularly powerful, but at least I have a name that counts for something. If I truly want to protect them, I can protect them — at least a little."

Xie Yuanjing didn't respond right away.

The private room filled only with the flowing sound of the qin, like wisps of smoke curling upward — gentle and meandering, drifting toward the ceiling.

"What do you mean, not powerful?"

At last he spoke again. He reached out and lightly touched Lu Huaixi's cheek. "You are very capable already. I was angry today, yes — but I have to admit, you had real presence out there."

"Really?"

Lu Huaixi blinked. And from that light touch, she felt, inexplicably, something like reassurance.

She filed it under warmth — something like what she felt with her mother — and, much as she would have done with her mother, tilted her cheek and leaned into his hand, just barely, as if in answer.

"Was I quite intimidating?"

"Very. When I arrived just now, even I was afraid of getting on Second Miss Lu's bad side."

Xie Yuanjing spoke, and then, without quite meaning to, smiled again.

Lu Huaixi had already drawn her face back. But somehow his hand was reluctant to follow.

"I don't believe you."

Lu Huaixi gave a soft little scoff, then asked, "Are you still angry?"

One song ended, and the sound of the qin faded into silence. The private room grew quiet again.

Xie Yuanjing met her clear, bright eyes — and when he caught the flicker of trust in them, something shifted in him for just a moment.

His fingertips felt warm. Some nameless feeling rose in him, thread by thread — making him hesitate, making him want to pull back.

But words moved faster than thought.

"And if I am still angry?"

"Then I'll coax you a little."

Lu Huaixi said it easily.

Then, thinking of all the times she had made her mother cross and then gone to her with a pitiful look and soft words, she couldn't help curving her eyes into a smile.

"I won't dance for you — but I'll play you a song. As thanks for helping me frighten the owner of that corner tavern. Would you like to hear it?"

Xie Yuanjing had forgotten to respond. He only remembered that one phrase — she would coax him.

He stood there for a moment, something hollow inside him feeling as though it were slowly being filled, a faint warmth passing through it — and he found himself unwilling to let his mind wander anywhere else.

chapters.title: Going Back Home to Make Trouble
chapters.content:
After returning to the marquis estate from Shun'an Fang that day, Lu Huaixi had braced herself for a reprimand from the estate's Old Madam or the First Madam.

But nearly three days had passed, and not a single person in the estate had come to ask about it.

The Lu family hadn't either. Only her eldest brother, Lu Yuanzhao, had sent her a letter saying she had gotten impressive — though whether he was genuinely praising her or thinking about giving her a good smack was hard to tell.

A few more days passed.

When Lu Huaixi finally had a quiet moment to think about new dance routines, Jingshuang came in from outside.

"First Young Madam, there's news from Qingling."

"What is it?"

"The messenger says that although those people have been detained, only one charge of theft and one of assault and public disturbance could be established. Nothing else was found."

Jingshuang continued, "Though those two charges are no small thing either — enough to keep them from ever getting back on their feet."

Lu Huaixi had been reclining against the soft chaise with one cheek propped in her hand, turning things over in her mind. She sat up at this, her expression turning serious.

"Nothing else? What about the silver?"

"They're saying the silver came from the woman helping a manager at her former workplace sell off some things. When that place started failing and was about to close, she skimmed some off the top and stole a few things besides."

Jingshuang didn't look convinced by this either, and spoke with a furrowed brow.

"The couple did, in fact, act on someone's advice — that manager's, apparently. He told the woman to go in and make a scene, not let anyone take advantage of them. After that, the manager closed up shop and went back to his hometown, and no one can find him now."

"What did this manager do? Has anyone looked into this business of him going back to his hometown?"

"They have. He ran an embroidery shop for several years, on the front street in the west end of the city."

Jingshuang paused when she finished, then lifted her head slightly and added:

"The manager had no contact with anyone suspicious. The only thing of note is that Third Miss Lu visited that embroidery shop once, some time ago. Though she apparently found it beneath her standards and didn't go back."

Lu Huaixi's brow creased at this. "When? Is it certain it was her?"

"Just two days after your return visit to the Lu family. The west end of the city doesn't see many wealthy visitors, and that embroidery street in particular does sluggish business — the people on that street remember clearly who has come by and who looked well-off.

"When your maidservant heard it mentioned, she thought it sounded like Third Miss Lu, so she had someone make further inquiries at the Lu estate — and it was confirmed that on that day, Third Miss Lu did leave the estate and go to the west end of the city."

Jingshuang said earnestly, "Though all the neighbors say Third Miss Lu only went the once, and didn't stay in the shop long — just took one look and left with a rather disdainful expression."

"Why do they remember it so clearly?"

"They were all standing out front, hoping to draw wealthy customers into their own shops."

Lu Huaixi said nothing more after hearing this.

It was Jingshuang who, after waiting a long while and still feeling uneasy, spoke again. "The embroidery shop closing up so suddenly is admittedly strange. Your maidservant has already arranged to pass word of the couple's situation to Third Miss Lu's side — if it really is——"

"It's probably her."

Lu Huaixi said it lightly, and didn't seem particularly angry.

"Everything she uses has to be refined and costly. There's no way she'd have any interest in wandering around a place she looks down on — the west end of the city especially, she never goes there. Though it is rather foolish of her to be traced back to that embroidery shop so easily."

"Third Miss Lu must have been trying to keep it secret. She simply stands out too much."

Jingshuang watched Lu Huaixi as she spoke. "The people investigating had to spend two days on it. They said that on the day Third Miss Lu left the estate, she changed locations several times and even changed her clothes — as though she was going to meet someone."

"By all appearances, this matter can't be separated from her. But there's something I genuinely can't work out: what does Third Miss Lu gain from going to all this trouble to scheme against you?"

"She gains from me not doing well."

Lu Huaixi's tone was indifferent. As she rose, she picked up a piece of pastry from the side table and put it in her mouth.

When she had finished, she continued, "She probably thought Shun'an Fang truly was running dirty business, and wanted to humiliate me in public — have people point their fingers, and then have my husband's family turn against me."

There were still a few things she hadn't quite sorted out.

Such as how Lu Tangshu had even learned about Shun'an Fang. And if she had been clever enough to hatch such a roundabout scheme, why hadn't she been clever enough to not go to the west end of the city herself?

"Have someone prepare the carriage."

"First Young Madam is going out?"

"Yes. Back to the Lu estate."

Lu Huaixi walked toward the bronze mirror. "Life has been too dull lately. I'm going back to make a little trouble. Oh, and — find a way to make sure those two in prison don't have too comfortable a time of it."

Xie Yuanjing had said she was too well-mannered — that even with her standing behind her, she still insisted on following proper procedure. Fine then. She would stop concerning herself with procedure entirely.

Even if nothing else could be pinned on them, they were going to suffer in there.

In the carriage, Yaoshu, who had by now heard the news, was feeling indignant on her behalf.

"I never thought she could be this vicious. You're already married and out of the house, and she's still scheming against you — she must just not be able to stand......"

The words trailed off there. Perhaps thinking better of it, Yaoshu swallowed the rest of the phrase — can't stand to see you do well.

But she didn't stay quiet for long. After a moment, she leaned over again and said quietly:

"First Young Madam, don't let this weigh on you. No matter what happens with Shun'an Fang, the Young Master keeps you in mind and looks out for you. Let that one stew in her own bitterness."

"How do you know about that?"

"I caught a little bit."

Yaoshu smiled. "The day the Young Master was outside Shun'an Fang, he said out loud in front of everyone that he had come to back you up. It's been the talk of the street for days now."

This was news to Lu Huaixi.

That day outside Shun'an Fang, she and Xie Yuanjing had been too far apart — she hadn't caught what he said to the crowd. She had thought that coming in person was already enough to show where he stood, but she hadn't imagined he would say it plainly to strangers.

Lu Huaixi was about to ask Yaoshu more when the carriage suddenly slowed.

"Are we there already?"

Yaoshu leaned forward and lifted a corner of the curtain. "Couldn't be this quick yet."

"We're getting close, but the road ahead is blocked. We'll have to cut through this side alley — there's a carriage stopped right up ahead, sitting there taking up space, right in the middle of everything."

The driver said a few words, and Yaoshu followed his line of sight to look.

Lu Huaixi did the same.

"That carriage...... looks a little familiar."

After a moment, Lu Huaixi thought back to that time before the wedding, when she had been lured out under false pretenses and found He Jianxing in a drunken state — and it seemed like it had been this same sort of carriage.

"Isn't that the young master of the He family?"

Yaoshu had seen him once before. She narrowed her eyes to look more carefully. "What is the He family's carriage doing stopped here? They don't live around here anymore."

Just before she dropped the curtain, Yaoshu looked one more time — and then, as if something had occurred to her, lowered her voice to murmur:

"Word is this He young master's engagement has fallen apart. The girl's family has kicked up a fuss and called off the match. And here he is, not trying to save his own engagement, just sitting around with nothing better to do."

Lu Huaixi raised an eyebrow. She didn't pick up a lot of gossip, but that didn't mean she didn't listen.

Especially now, when she had a rather strong distaste for He Jianxing.

"You know about that too?"

"Your maidservant has to keep watch. Last time this He young master already had a betrothal, and yet his portrait somehow ended up in your hands — of course your maidservant had to keep her ears open after that. Can't have someone taking advantage of the situation with bad intentions."

Yaoshu said it earnestly, with a furrowed brow.

"Word is this Young Master He isn't someone who keeps himself in line. He was already about to take a wife, and was still keeping another woman's things on him — and not the drinking and carousing kind, either. Your maidservant suspects they were things like handkerchiefs and jade pendants.

"When this came to light, he apparently felt humiliated, shoved the girl, and then turned around and accused her of being jealous and having too much of a temper."

Lu Huaixi had gotten the general picture.

Along with disgust, there was a flicker of genuine disbelief.

A man who needed his wife's family to prop him up, and he still had the audacity to carry on like this — truly believing he was something remarkable. What a laughingstock.

"Your maidservant even made special inquiries about the young lady's family. Truly a respectable scholarly household — good that she's calling off the engagement. If she hadn't, your maidservant would have been tempted to go and talk some sense into her."

Lu Huaixi burst out laughing.

"You looked into that too? Were you actually thinking of going and getting involved in someone else's engagement?"

"You really do mind everyone's business."

At the same hour, Xie Yuanjing was in the deep red of his official robes, cold and impassive.

Shen Zhouxu stood beside him, and after listening to him call Gong Zhuo over to give instructions, couldn't help muttering:

"You're keeping track of how many young girls are in Lu Huaixi's shop? Why don't you just open a proper school for girls and make her the teacher?"

"Be quiet."

Xie Yuanjing didn't even look up.

chapters.title: You Mind Too Much of Other People's Business
chapters.content:
Shen Zhouxu was about to say something back when a young man came walking over from the side.

Seeing the two of them, he stopped, gave Shen Zhouxu a nod, and then looked toward Xie Yuanjing.

"I was still on my way back to the capital when you got married — didn't make it in time. But from what I hear, your wife is quite young. Getting along with someone like that must be a bit of a trial, I'd imagine."

The man was dressed in fine brocade, every inch of him radiating wealth.

He spoke with a smile, outwardly pleasant, yet with an undercurrent of arrogance that made him difficult to warm to.

"Get together tonight? I've just taken in a new batch — right around the right age. Come pick a couple to bring back and keep yourself entertained."

Xie Yuanjing's brow drew together, almost imperceptibly, and then the man continued: "Oh, and someone asked me to bring you something — said it's to congratulate the great Young Master Xie on his wedding. The poor thing — I couldn't bring myself to refuse on your behalf."

"Don't know who it's from. Not accepting it."

Xie Yuanjing glanced at the man, his tone perfectly flat.

The man didn't seem particularly bothered, only smiled again. "Really not taking it? I thought the person was, at the very least, something of a...... confidante of yours?"

Xie Yuanjing's lips curved, just slightly, and a short quiet laugh escaped him.

"Officer Zheng has been away from the capital for some years — misunderstandings are inevitable. But that phrase — best not to say it loosely going forward. My wife has a candid nature; if she heard it, she'd believe it."

The words away from the capital for some years made the man's expression shift briefly — though he recovered quickly.

"So you've taken this marriage seriously after all. I'd assumed it was a matter of going through the motions, giving the Lu family some face...... it seems certain things are better left unsaid from now on."

After the man left, Shen Zhouxu's eyes lingered on his retreating figure.

He was just about to say something when the man beside him turned and made to leave.

"Where are you going? Want to have a drink tonight?"

"To the Lu estate."

Xie Yuanjing recalled the news he had just received, and said without particular urgency, "She's going back there today to make trouble. I'll go and pick her up."

"...... What kind of trouble needs you to make the trip yourself? And she's not exactly going to come off the worse end of things in the Lu estate, is she? Did Zheng Xiaoqi just get under your skin?"

"You mind too much of other people's business."

The phrase thrown right back at him made Shen Zhouxu sputter.

—

Inside the Lu estate, Lu Huaixi went directly to Lu Tangshu's Lanqing Courtyard. She didn't even wait to be announced — she simply pushed the door open and walked in.

The person inside hadn't had time to school her expression. Lu Huaixi caught a flash of irritation on her face at a glance.

And then, upon seeing who it was — surprise.

"You——"

She seemed to be about to demand why Lu Huaixi had barged in unannounced, but Lu Huaixi didn't give her the chance.

"Wanted to see me make a fool of myself, did you?"

She walked over and sat down naturally beside Lu Tangshu, unhurried, even helping herself to a cup of tea. "Next time you want to pull something like this, be cleaner about it. Either leave no trace at all, or come at me directly."

"What — what are you talking about? You're making no sense."

Lu Tangshu was rattled. She bit her lip and glared at the person in front of her.

She was still seething inside, half-tempted to fly at her right then and there. But she didn't dare.

She still needed the first branch to show her some leniency. And besides, she had the nagging sense that this supposedly worthless second sister of hers was somehow harder to get past than she used to be.

Seeing her hesitate, Lu Huaixi let her gaze rest on her face for a moment, then smiled at her — the picture of easy-going affability.

"Those people who caused trouble at Shun'an Fang are already in prison. I won't let them out anytime soon. The way I see it, they'll need to come out of there missing an arm or a leg before my anger cools. As for you — don't sleep too soundly."

"What — what Shun'an Fang, what prison — I don't know what you're talking about."

Lu Tangshu went a shade paler, but held herself together well enough, only tightening her grip around her teacup.

"Second Sister barging into my courtyard like this and throwing all this mud at me — isn't that a bit much? Even if something has truly happened, Second Sister should at least come with evidence."

"I don't have evidence."

Lu Huaixi said it plainly. "And I'm too lazy to go looking for any. This is just the two of us dropping all pretense — no need for that sort of thing."

"You——"

"Instead of spending your time thinking about how to make the marquis estate turn against me, you'd do better thinking about your own marriage prospects. The marquis estate isn't going to do anything to me. My father and mother won't blame me either. It's you who should be worried — if you can't find a husband, and then end up in the palace without knowing how to conduct yourself, you'll end up with nothing in the end."

At the mention of marriage, a flash of vexation crossed Lu Tangshu's face.

Lu Huaixi caught it clearly, then looked away as if she hadn't noticed, and picked up the teacup beside her.

Having been struck where it hurt, and with the other person now making it clear she was done being civil, Lu Tangshu had no more patience for keeping her temper in check. She fixed Lu Huaixi with a hard stare, her eyes full of fury and resentment.

"Going into the palace was your doing all along! Isn't it enough that you've ruined me — now you want to blame it on me too? Do you really think that just because you've married into the marquis estate, you have someone to fall back on? Xie Yuanjing just finds you a novelty. Once he comes back to his senses and remembers you have nothing to offer, neither he nor the estate will give you a second glance!"

"And yet here you are, spending your energy worrying about whether he'll give me a second glance."

Lu Huaixi let out a short laugh. "Whoever has reaped what they sowed knows it themselves. I didn't come here today to discuss anything else with you. I came to tell you——"

She glanced at Jingshuang, who stepped forward immediately, seized Lu Tangshu's arms with one hand, and with the other gripped her by the jaw, pinning her so she couldn't move.

The maidservant who tried to run out and alert someone was shoved firmly back in by Yaoshu.

In short order, the pain of having her arm twisted behind her back brought tears spilling from Lu Tangshu's eyes.

Lu Huaixi paid no attention. She raised her hand and tipped the contents of the teacup directly into Lu Tangshu's face.

"Because of your own selfish designs, you nearly destroyed the lives of the girls in my Shun'an Fang. I will not let that go. And another thing — I don't care where you got your information, but if you want to use something like this to ruin my reputation, you had best think harder first. Never mind one Shun'an Fang — even if I had truly opened a brothel, a trick as feeble as this could never bring me down."

The tea slid down Lu Tangshu's face.

Her eyes, which had been open at first, closed instinctively. Her eyes reddened — whether from the water stinging them, or because she had actually begun to cry.

"You don't need to feel aggrieved about any of this. The gates of the Chengen Marquis Estate are right there. If you think Xie Yuanjing would have been better off marrying you instead of me — go tell him so yourself. If you can get him to annul the marriage and take you instead, I won't say a single word against it. I'll even help dress you for the wedding and see you off in style."

Lu Huaixi had genuinely lost her temper. Looking at her, she couldn't help lifting the now-empty teacup and smashing it on the floor.

"All these schemes you run day after day — and in the end you can't even keep them from getting traced back to you. Lu Tangshu. You are truly, deeply stupid."

chapters.title: The Punishment You Have Coming Is Different From Everyone Else's
chapters.content:
By the time Xie Yuanjing arrived at the Lu estate, Lu Huaixi had already gotten her grievances out and made her way to her mother's courtyard.

For a married daughter to suddenly come running home — Madam Liu was so doting that she could only feel delighted.

Even when she heard about the commotion that had just come from the second branch, she didn't find anything amiss.

"Mother, find a few people to keep an eye on Lu Tangshu. I have a feeling she's been corresponding privately with someone."

"Someone you know?"

"Yes."

"I've been keeping an eye on the second branch overall — I forgot to watch her separately."

Madam Liu thought of it and felt only irritated. "All that pleasantness to your face while stabbing you in the back — with a mind like that, imagine what she'd get up to inside the palace, where you'd never be rid of her."

Vicious people should be left to be ground down by other vicious people. A moment's softness would only harm yourself.

"Don't trouble yourself with it. I have my hands in her affairs already. At most it's another two months, and there's still the fourth one waiting to make her life miserable — that one won't let Lu Tangshu get off easy."

"I know. I just find her irritating to look at. She can't even scheme properly — she's both foolish and infuriating."

"Complaining that her methods are too crude, are you?"

At this, Madam Liu couldn't help laughing. Then, as if something had occurred to her, she took her daughter's hand and said, "Since Shun'an Fang is yours, the next time we host a banquet, we'll invite performers from there. What do you think?"

"Fine by me."

Lu Huaixi nodded and curved her lips into a smile. "Though you'll have to pay the proper rate, Mother. It goes in the ledger."

"Keeping such strict accounts — you're not planning to come out of pocket even once?"

"Of course not. I'm already married out of the family. That can wait until I'm back visiting. And when I am back, I'll cover one or two evenings for you — but we'd have to be discreet about it. Our head manager is very strict."

"Strict is good. Otherwise with someone like you in charge, you'd be giving money away."

"How could that be? Mother, you really have no faith in me at all."

Lu Huaixi gave a soft indignant sound, but her face never lost its smile — clearly unaffected by any of the events of the day.

Madam Liu looked at her and finally let out a breath of relief.

She had said that for two reasons: first, to show her attitude toward Shun'an Fang and put her daughter's mind at ease; and second, because for estate banquets, this arrangement was genuinely the most convenient.

But as they exchanged a few laughing words, her gaze drifted to Lu Huaixi's face and stayed there.

Her daughter was at exactly the age when the heart first begins to stir. Spending so much time with someone like Xie Yuanjing — it would be hard not to develop some soft, hazy feelings.

Madam Liu sometimes worried. She was afraid her daughter might fall for someone unsuitable, and then find it hard to let go when the year was up and they parted ways.

But looking at her now, she seemed — all right. For the time being.

"You — honestly, all you ever think about is how to get money out of your mother."

Madam Liu said it teasingly, and tapped her daughter's forehead with one finger.

Lu Huaixi didn't look the least bit embarrassed. She hooked her arm through Madam Liu's and gave it a little swing.

She was just about to say that she wanted to stay and eat dinner at the estate tonight, when the voice of a maidservant drifted in from outside.

"Your maidservant pays her respects to the Young Master."

The words Lu Huaixi hadn't yet spoken died on her lips. She turned her head toward the wooden door, eyes rounding with curiosity.

She hadn't been paying attention when it was said on the day of her return visit after the wedding — but hearing the words Young Master spoken aloud today felt, for some strange reason, quite novel.

Madam Liu was also a little surprised. She glanced at her daughter. "You asked him to come?"

"No." Lu Huaixi shook her head immediately. "I came to deal with Lu Tangshu. Why would I ask him along?"

"Could he have come to keep you in line? Your father isn't here, so it can't be on your father's account."

"Him coming to keep me in line wouldn't be unusual."

Lu Huaixi muttered under her breath, "He looks like he doesn't say much and keeps to himself, but actually he manages me quite a lot."

Madam Liu paused. The look she turned on her daughter suddenly held a hint of something more careful.

But she didn't dwell on it for long. Seeing the maidservant enter, she gathered herself and rose.

"Madam, the Young Master has come to take Second Miss home. Not wanting to disturb Madam and Miss from their private conversation, he is currently waiting in the courtyard."

"Waiting outside? In this heat? Go and invite him in at once. Bring tea."

"Wait."

Lu Huaixi called the retreating maidservant back. "Bring some ice as well."

"Ice for what?" Madam Liu asked.

"To put in the tea."

—

"Please have some tea, Officer Zheng."

Zheng Xiaoqi, who had received nothing but a cold reception from Xie Yuanjing, was now seated in a teahouse where he had arranged to meet a colleague.

He had only recently been transferred back to the capital. Compared to his more brash days, he had smoothed out considerably — otherwise, a modest teahouse like this and a colleague of no particular standing would never have merited his time.

"You've had a long day, Officer Zheng."

"Not at all, Officer Zhou."

Zheng Xiaoqi answered offhandedly.

"I saw Officer Zheng speaking with Lord Xie today, and knowing the two of you are acquainted, I had actually thought to invite Lord Xie to join us."

The man beside him was somewhere around thirty, his manner of speaking carrying a mild flattery that was nonetheless easy to sit with.

"Is that so — and why didn't you? Because Yuanjing wouldn't come?"

"Not exactly. I just remembered that Lord Xie has rarely gone out to socialize since his wedding — I didn't think it was my place to ask."

The man smiled. "After all, Lord Xie was just married. Naturally he'd want to keep his household happy."

"That does sound rather unlike him."

Zheng Xiaoqi seemed to find his interest suddenly piqued, and sat up slightly. "I heard Lord Xie's new wife is quite young, and that the wedding wasn't originally planned to be a large affair — no one knew anything about it?"

"She's not especially young — the second daughter of the Lu family. By all accounts a very fine young lady in both appearance and temperament. There's the occasional bit of talk here and there, but nothing serious. As for the wedding not being planned as a large affair — that's not quite right either."

The man said, "The day he came to ask for her hand, quite a stir was made of it. Word even reached the palace. His Majesty, who normally keeps a cool expression around Lord Xie, actually smiled a few times when it came up."

Zheng Xiaoqi nodded with a smile, looking perfectly pleasant on the surface — though a flash of quiet disdain moved quickly through his eyes.

Whether that imperial smile was because of the Lu family, or because of Xie Yuanjing himself, remained to be seen.

"A young lady from the Lu family — of course she'd be exceptional."

Zheng Xiaoqi poured himself another cup of tea. "I also heard the young lady runs a little entertainment venue of some kind — quite an interesting character, by the sound of it."

"It's not much more than a young girl's little amusement. Though a few of the dancers there are quite remarkable — I wouldn't have expected them to be under this Second Miss Lu's care."

"Is that so. Then I'll have to go and take a look sometime — show my support."

Zheng Xiaoqi smiled. "Yuanjing used to enjoy listening to a particular girl sing, even stood up for her once. I wonder if there's anyone at Shun'an Fang who suits him even better."

The man across from him did not pick up that thread. He didn't so much as show the slightest curiosity about the girl who had been mentioned.

He wasn't foolish enough to. Flattering one person by slighting another was a trade not worth making.

Zheng Xiaoqi didn't seem to care whether or not he was being listened to, and went on drinking his tea.

—

In the carriage, Lu Huaixi sat beside Xie Yuanjing, gazing at the curtain ahead, her mind drifting slightly.

Before long she grew drowsy, and stifled a yawn.

"You came all that way to make trouble — so why the long face?"

Xie Yuanjing looked at Lu Huaixi, who hadn't said a word, and watched the full range of her emotions display themselves plainly across her face. He let out a quiet laugh.

"If the trouble wasn't satisfying enough, we can turn around right now."

That finally made Lu Huaixi look at him.

"And what would we do if we went back?"

"Have her tied up and beaten."

Xie Yuanjing said it casually. "There are instruments in the dungeon. A few days in there, and she'd be much more well-behaved."

The man before her spoke as though it were nothing, yet Lu Huaixi had the inexplicable sense that he would actually do it.

She looked at him — studying the handsome face, beautiful and cold all at once.

"You're genuinely frightening."

"Have I frightened you?"

Lu Huaixi thought about it, then shook her head. "No."

"Good. Because I won't frighten you."

At those words, Lu Huaixi fixed her eyes on his carefully. "Then if I get into trouble, or cause some disaster — you won't frighten me either?"

"No."

Xie Yuanjing glanced at her, then curved his lips toward her slightly. "You have your own punishment coming. It's different from everyone else's."

chapters.title: Do You Trust Me?
chapters.content:
The carriage moved along the main street. Perhaps because the road ahead had more people than usual, it slowed, and every now and then the faint sounds from outside drifted in.

When Lu Huaixi grew bored in a carriage, she would usually lift the curtain to look outside.

But right now, she couldn't spare a single thought for it.

"What punishment?"

She couldn't help leaning toward Xie Yuanjing, her dark eyes full of undisguised curiosity. "Like how my father punishes my elder brother?"

"If you want to know, cause some trouble next time and find out."

"......"

Lu Huaixi sat back before long. "I don't want to know."

The person in front of him was genuinely entertaining. Xie Yuanjing reached out instinctively, wanting to pinch her cheek again.

But the moment the pad of his finger touched her face, something in him flickered.

The warmth of it made his heartbeat slow for just an instant. Delayed, he realized he shouldn't be giving in to these unguarded gestures of closeness.

He stopped where he was, his movement growing slightly stiff, as if his mind had wandered.

Lu Huaixi, watching him, assumed he was going to soothe her the same way as before. With easy familiarity, she leaned her cheek into his hand on her own, just barely, and then sat back upright.

"My mother says I don't need to bother with Lu Tangshu's affairs."

"Mm."

"She says it's only another two months or so. She says Lu Tangshu wants everything and will end up with nothing."

"Mm."

"But I'm still going to get involved. I'm not going to just——"

Xie Yuanjing made another sound of acknowledgment. Lu Huaixi frowned and looked at him.

"Never mind, I'm not talking to you. You're just going through the motions."

When Xie Yuanjing withdrew his hand, the carriage had turned off that street, and the pace picked up again.

Lu Huaixi used the gentle sway of the turn as cover to shift herself outward, putting some distance between them.

The blatant sulking of it pulled him back from wherever his thoughts had gone.

Xie Yuanjing rubbed his fingertips together quietly, then looked at the side of her face where she had turned away.

Without much delay — almost at once — he pulled her back toward him.

"Sit properly."

He said it quietly. "I wasn't going through the motions. I was thinking."

Seeing that Lu Huaixi's curiosity had turned her face back toward him, Xie Yuanjing gave a small inward smile, though his expression was now considerably more serious.

"Have you already guessed that what happened with Shun'an Fang involves someone else besides your third sister?"

"Yes."

"Then why are you unhappy, even though you have a lead?"

Xie Yuanjing asked, "When you got into the carriage just now — you were already thinking about this, weren't you?"

"Yes. How do you always know everything."

Lu Huaixi settled back beside him. "If there really is someone else behind this — it has to be someone I know...... no, someone I'm close to."

An ordinary person would have no way of knowing about Shun'an Fang. Whoever knew, or could even have guessed, must have had some degree of closeness with her at some point.

Back to the matter at hand, Lu Huaixi's eyelids drooped, the energy going out of her. "Whoever it is — it's someone familiar who has turned against me. What is there to be happy about?"

Xie Yuanjing looked at her and said nothing.

He rarely saw dejection or low spirits on Lu Huaixi's face.

She always seemed to have energy to spare — even when she was unhappy, it was written all over her face, a clear invitation for someone to come and coax her. Very easy to comfort.

But now — she was genuinely disappointed.

Xie Yuanjing decided this time was not the moment for comfort. He felt that Lu Huaixi needed to learn to keep faith in people — in anyone.

"You——"

His lips parted, the words ready — but when he caught the look of dimmed brightness in her eyes, something shifted without his meaning it to, and a different sentence came out instead.

"I'll have people look into this. You don't need to worry about it anymore."

Seeing her look up at him, he continued, "I hear business at Shun'an Fang has been good lately. Instead of sitting here brooding and making yourself miserable, put your mind to making money — and making other people miserable."

He paused, and looked at her. "Do you trust me?"

After a moment, Lu Huaixi nodded.

"I do."

—

Once they returned to the estate, the carriage didn't linger — it turned and headed back out again.

Xie Yuanjing said nothing about where he was going. Lu Huaixi only watched the carriage roll away into the distance, and didn't ask.

Some things were better not thought about too long. The longer you dwelt on them, the more likely they were to drift in the wrong direction.

Two more days passed before Zhou Xianya came to find her.

Lu Huaixi had just finished making plans for the lake excursion when she heard Zhou Xianya's invitation to go out. She turned at once and called Yaoshu to come help her change.

"Xianya jiejie isn't coming in?"

"She isn't, First Young Madam."

Yaoshu held up a light-colored dress. "Miss Zhou says she came without notice, and that this isn't the Lu estate — she said it would be presumptuous to come in unannounced."

Lu Huaixi said nothing for a moment at that.

Come to think of it, she supposed that was true. At the Lu estate, Zhou Xianya could drop by to see her at any time. But here at the marquis estate, even she herself was only a temporary guest.

"First Young Madam, don't be downcast. Miss Zhou says Miao Zhen Pavilion has just received a lot of new things from outside, and she slipped out herself without even taking the family carriage."

While they were talking, Gong Zhuo stopped Jingshuang outside and said a few words. Jingshuang then came in carrying a small booklet.

"First Young Madam, this is a record the Young Master had drawn up of the younger girls at Shun'an Fang. The Young Master says to have a look — if any of them would like to attend a girls' school, arrangements have already been made on that end. They can be sent over starting tomorrow."

Lu Huaixi was taken aback.

She took the booklet and looked through it. The girls listed were all around ten years of age or younger. A few had marks beside their names — presumably indicating they wished to go to school.

"The Young Master says Shun'an Fang doesn't only need singers and dancers. Girls who have no interest in performing can learn other things and still be Shun'an Fang's people — and even if they don't stay on there in the long run, it would still be to the First Young Madam's benefit."

Lu Huaixi fell quiet. She thought back suddenly to what she had said to Xie Yuanjing that day.

"The youngest is only seven. Some of them don't really have their hearts in it — they're just looking for a way to make a living. Trying to carve out some path for themselves."

He had taken those words to heart.

And what he was doing was genuinely an act of kindness — more thoughtful than what she herself had managed. Yet she knew this person didn't do things out of sudden goodwill. He was doing this because of what Jingshuang had said at the end: to her benefit.

To her benefit.

Lu Huaixi turned it over in her mind again.

Her reputation, Shun'an Fang's reputation — both would shift, in some way, because of this.

"I understand."

After a long moment, Lu Huaixi finally nodded.

There was no reason to refuse. She would accept his kindness, and she would remember it.

"I'll take them myself tomorrow."

—

It was only when Lu Huaixi stepped out of the estate and saw Zhou Xianya that the tangle of thoughts finally scattered, and a smile found its way back to her face.

The two of them hadn't managed a private outing since the wedding, and finally getting together today made Lu Huaixi so happy she almost felt like crying.

"Don't stand there tearing up at the estate gate. They'll have you hauled off."

"Hauled off for what?"

"For upsetting the First Young Madam of the marquis estate."

Zhou Xianya laughed — the composed, gentle manner she wore for outsiders gone, replaced by the easy closeness of an old friend.

"So then," she said, giving Lu Huaixi's cheek a gentle pinch. "Is your husband treating you well?"

chapters.title: A Familiar Face You Don't Like
chapters.content:
There were many forms of address after the wedding that still caught Lu Huaixi off guard.

Like the words Young Master spoken by the maidservants on her last visit to the Lu estate. And now, the word husband in Zhou Xianya's mouth.

When she herself said it in jest, it never felt like much. But hearing it from someone close to her — that was a different matter. Lu Huaixi had, as ever, a rather telling reaction: her face went warm.

She was not a coy person by nature, and she hadn't taken any real liberties with Xie Yuanjing, so she simply composed herself and nodded.

"He's a good person. Treats me quite well."

Zhou Xianya seemed relieved, though she was clearly still a little astonished — their whole circuit of Miao Zhen Pavilion wasn't enough to put an end to her exclamations about Xie Yuanjing.

Only when they settled into a newly opened restaurant did Lu Huaixi's ears get any peace.

"Isn't the lake excursion coming up in a few days?"

Lu Huaixi took her arm as they walked. "You'll get to see him then. Though he can look rather severe sometimes — but it's just how he looks. Don't take it too much to heart, Xianya jiejie."

"Just how he looks?"

Zhou Xianya's eyes went wide. "Do you know what people say about your husband out there? Though of course rumors aren't always reliable, and I trust you over anything else."

"Being severe doesn't mean he bites people." Lu Huaixi laughed.

"You'd think, but you can't always be sure...... this place looks busy, I wonder if there are still rooms upstairs — let me find someone to ask——"

"There are, there are — right this way, two young misses."

The words had barely left her mouth when the proprietor came forward with a smile.

"Perfect timing, young misses — there's one last room upstairs. Brand new, clean and bright."

He led the way. "You two look like fine and distinguished ladies — as it happens, the kitchen is testing new dishes today. I'll have the server bring you a special portion of our house specialty, plus some tea and pastries on the side. Come back again if it suits your taste."

Lu Huaixi blinked. It was her first time encountering a proprietor this enthusiastic.

But when they reached the upper floor and saw the room nearest the staircase, it became clear why.

Private enough, in its way — but it was the room closest to the outside. You could hear anyone coming or going on the stairs, and if the door was left open, you might even catch someone's eye as they passed.

Zhou Xianya hesitated. She looked at Lu Huaixi. "Should we...... go somewhere else?"

This was a new place, and Zhou Xianya hadn't been able to go out much lately. She had been looking forward to it when they arrived.

Lu Huaixi could see she was only thinking of her — worried she wouldn't be able to eat in peace. She shook her head and curved her eyes into a smile.

"The proprietor's going to bring us extra food. That's practically free money — we're not going anywhere else."

That one smile, and the whole room smiled along with her.

The door was soon shut, cutting off the noise from outside.

"This place really is doing well — the food must be decent."

Zhou Xianya settled into her seat. "I've been hungry for a while now."

The restaurant was busy, but the dishes came out at a reasonable pace. In addition to the local flavors of the capital, there was a decent selection from other regions as well.

Lu Huaixi had a sweet tooth, and later ordered a braised pork dish from the south, which leaned on the sweeter side.

When the red-glazed stewed meat arrived, the server also brought out an extra serving of post-meal tea and pastries.

With people coming in and out to deliver dishes, the door was left open a crack.

Lu Huaixi was busy staring at the braised pork, which looked as good as it smelled, when an elbow nudged her gently.

"What is it, Xianya jiejie?"

She looked up and found the person beside her had her gaze fixed on something outside. She followed it.

"That's...... Lu Tangshu?"

Not far off, at the top of the staircase, Lu Tangshu emerged with an irritated expression — she seemed to have been called over by someone, for she paused there briefly.

But she turned away quickly and left without lingering.

"Your sister is out meeting someone, looking that put-out about it."

"I don't know."

Lu Huaixi looked away and carefully lifted a piece of meat into her own dish.

She set her chopsticks down before eating, though, since they were still talking.

"She can't have been having a good time of it lately."

"Is that so? I heard the second branch has been arranging matches for her — I'd have thought she was doing well enough. Though I'm only telling you this."

Zhou Xianya lowered her voice. "It was the same with your wedding — one day there was nothing, and the next it was settled and done with. Now this third sister of yours seems to be in the same situation, sneaking around to meet potential matches in secret. What's with your family and all this secrecy?"

Lu Huaixi was momentarily at a loss, and then she smiled at the person in front of her.

"Since it's all being done in secret, Xianya jiejie, how do you know she's looking for a match?"

"Because they came sniffing around my brother."

Zhou Xianya didn't bother softening it. "Between you and me, if it were you — I wouldn't say a single word against it, I'd help things along myself. But your third sister——"

She said it directly. "I don't like her. And neither does my brother."

"Well, your brother didn't exactly like me either."

Lu Huaixi laughed. "When I was going through the matchmaking process, I never saw your brother's portrait. Clearly he didn't want to be considered."

"Impossible. My brother would never not want to be considered."

Zhou Xianya was unconvinced. "Don't try to pull something over on me — did you forget I know you two were already matched before, so there was no need for portraits?"

Lu Huaixi choked on her words, only then realizing she had let something slip.

She didn't want to keep things from Zhou Xianya, but this sort of thing — best not to drag anyone else into the water.

Though it was true she had never seen Zhou Xianya's brother's portrait. Maybe it hadn't been put in, or maybe someone had taken it out.

"I was just talking. So your family isn't willing to consider it?"

"Not willing. My mother said if it were you...... anyway, never mind you, let's talk about your third sister."

Lu Huaixi listened a while longer.

She wasn't particularly surprised. She knew her mother had been working on the question of Lu Tangshu's marriage — and she had no intention of letting her have an easy time of it. A few well-placed pieces of information were enough to make the second branch panic, and their desperation made them more careless than she had ever been when she was being matched. And the more desperate they were, the more likely they were to make mistakes.

While Zhou Xianya was still talking, someone passed outside the door again.

Both of them instinctively glanced at the movement beyond.

"That's......"

Lu Huaixi recognized the figure and her brow drew together, a flash of distaste moving through her eyes.

He Jianxing again. All dressed up, fancying himself charming and debonair — one look was already one look too many.

"Why is it always someone unpleasant everywhere I turn — first your third sister, now this He family......"

Zhou Xianya's words were still coming.

Lu Huaixi reached for her teacup — and froze the moment her fingers found the warmth of the cup.

A thought surfaced in her mind, unbidden and unwelcome.

These two. Could they actually be here together?

If so — the carriage stopped in the side alley near the Lu estate a few days ago — could that have had something to do with Lu Tangshu too?

"Jingshuang."

Lu Huaixi looked up at once. "Go and see."

Lu Tangshu looked down on He Jianxing — that was certain. And He Jianxing would never be able to tolerate Lu Tangshu's temper. If these two were somehow entangled, the days ahead would be nothing but chaos for them.

But their chaos, for her, would be a rather satisfying kind of relief.

Thinking of it that way, it actually didn't seem so bad.

Lu Huaixi tucked her expression away and turned back to chatting with Zhou Xianya.

The two of them finished their meal, lingered over tea for a while, and when they finally came downstairs, the noise of the restaurant had quieted considerably — barely half the crowd of when they had arrived.

As they prepared to head back, Zhou Xianya took her arm with a reluctant expression.

"I can't exactly come to the marquis estate, so next time you come to mine. You haven't been in ages — we can't only see each other a handful of times in a whole year."

She sighed.

"Not long ago you used to bring Wu Wenlan along to keep me company every now and then. Now...... speaking of which, I ran into Wu Wenlan a couple of days ago. She was asking after you — whether you were doing well, whether you'd been treated poorly."

Zhou Xianya frowned. "I told her of course you were doing well, and of course you weren't being mistreated. Though I'd guess she's trying to make amends and just using me as an excuse to bring it up. She has no idea how to go about it."

chapters.title: Are You Dealing With Her, or Dealing With Me?
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi stilled for just a moment at the name, but quickly let the feeling pass.

"I'm not reconciling with anyone. If two people can't walk the same path, they part ways."

"I know your nature. You never owed her anything — she was the one who wronged your trust."

Zhou Xianya gave her a gentle hug, confirmed the time of the lake outing once more, and returned to her own carriage.

Beyond that first brief moment, Wu Wenlan's name left no lasting impression. By the time Lu Huaixi stepped through the gates of the marquis estate, she had already forgotten the conversation.

Yaoshu came to find her just as Lu Huaixi had finished a visit to the First Madam's courtyard.

She wanted to bathe early tonight so she'd have the energy tomorrow to bring the girls from Shun'an Fang to the school.

Come to think of it, she hadn't seen a teacher in a long time. Tomorrow's teacher wouldn't be there for her, and yet she still had an inexplicable, jittery feeling — as though her palms might get smacked.

She was still thinking about this when Yaoshu came in, carrying two small boxes.

"Young Madam."

She said, "Little Doctor Zeng had these two boxes of her newly made beauty pills sent over for you. The messenger also said that Old Master Zeng wants to know why you've stopped coming to see him — and whether you've been off somewhere enjoying yourself and forgotten all about him."

"I'm not going anywhere near there. The heat is unbearable — that old man just wants me to come harvest herbs for him."

Lu Huaixi gave a soft snort, then took the boxes from Yaoshu's hands. "Newly made again, and I'm supposed to be the first to try them? Being useless would be one thing, but let's hope they don't upset my stomach."

Yaoshu couldn't help laughing at that.

"You're not the first to try them, Young Madam. These have already been on sale at Little Doctor Zeng's medicine shop for several days now — people can hardly get their hands on them. A box or two comes out every few days at most. It seems Little Doctor Zeng makes them more for her own amusement."

"Then I'll hold onto them for now. At my age, I don't really need to be taking things like these......"

She stopped mid-sentence and suddenly looked up. "Wait — these aren't meant for me to give to my mother and the First Madam, are they?"

Yaoshu pressed her lips together to keep from laughing and said nothing.

She didn't dare say that the two madams were getting on in years — but she rather suspected that was the idea.

"Fine, fine. I'll play the gracious gift-giver and go deliver them."

Just as she said it, two figures approached in the distance. Lu Huaixi looked up and immediately recognized the maidservant from the Old Madam's courtyard — and beside her, Mu Nianwei, smiling at her with careful, proper composure.

Several days had passed since they last met, and the young cousin-in-law had settled considerably.

Lu Huaixi took a quiet, measured look, then shifted her gaze to the maidservant.

Little Doctor Zeng's people had only just left, and here was the Old Madam already sending someone. No need to think too hard about why.

But she'd been stalling long enough. It was time to throw them something.

"Cousin-in-law."

Mu Nianwei dipped into a curtsy. The maidservant beside her also lowered her head in greeting. "Your maidservant pays respects to the First Young Madam."

"Cousin, you've come — would you like to come in and sit?"

Lu Huaixi said it easily, but a flash of embarrassment and displeasure crossed Mu Nianwei's face.

She quickly lowered her head again and said softly:

"I wouldn't dare impose on cousin-in-law. Great-Aunt said she hadn't seen cousin-in-law today and had been thinking of her, so she sent someone to check in. Nianwei has been thinking of cousin-in-law as well — and knowing that cousin-in-law's husband is so often away and no one is there to keep her company, Nianwei thought to come and have a chat."

"Grandmother is so good to me. And so is cousin."

Lu Huaixi smiled warmly, her eyes curving with the expression, her face the picture of genuine fondness — as if she truly were close to the Old Madam.

"I'd actually been worried at first that Grandmother and cousin didn't care for me. And yet it turns out it's Grandmother and cousin who think of me most in this household — especially cousin, who wants to see me every single day. Even more than your cousin-brother does."

Mu Nianwei's smile twitched. She couldn't tell whether she was being complimented or mocked.

She was about to say something more when a manservant passed nearby, carrying a load of ice.

The weather was warm, but not so oppressive that this amount of ice needed to be moved around every day.

Mu Nianwei looked at it, and her brow drew together. "Cousin-in-law, this is...... a little indulgent, isn't it?"

She said it with a trace of dissatisfaction. "Cousin-in-law may not have managed the household yet and might not know how these things are budgeted. The ice here was set aside from the beginning, but it's not something to be used so freely. It's nearly sundown now — for cousin-in-law to be using this much—"

"You make a fair point, cousin."

Lu Huaixi blinked, and called out to the manservant who had already entered the courtyard.

"Go ahead and take it back. Cousin says it's not right to be wasteful, and we shouldn't break the rules of the household."

The group of them froze. But since the First Young Madam was also their mistress, no one spoke up to question it. After a brief exchange of glances, they followed the order and withdrew.

A glimmer of satisfaction crossed Mu Nianwei's face, the irritation at being kept out of the courtyard dissolving in an instant.

She was about to add a few more words — but the Lu Huaixi before her had already dropped her smile, her expression cool and unhurried.

"I just remembered I have account books I need to start looking over. Since cousin doesn't wish to come inside, I won't keep you."

With that, Lu Huaixi glanced at the maidservant beside Mu Nianwei. "As it happens, I've set aside a box of Doctor Zeng's pills for Grandmother — just the thing to help her health. Please let Grandmother know, and I'll have someone send it over shortly."

"Yes, your maidservant will go and inform the Old Madam at once."

The First Young Madam's displeasure was plain enough — but since she had genuinely received something from the little miracle doctor, the maidservant didn't dare linger. She noted that she would also need to report the earlier exchange to the Old Madam.

Mu Nianwei too assumed she had finally managed to get under Lu Huaixi's skin.

Her chin lifted slightly, and she didn't stop to consider the value of the pills Lu Huaixi had mentioned.

"Cousin-in-law isn't upset about just now, is she?"

Lu Huaixi said nothing.

"Cousin-in-law looks a little displeased. And sending the pills by messenger instead of letting my maidservant take them now — could it be that cousin-in-law has misunderstood Nianwei——"

"Why would I be upset? That ice wasn't mine to begin with."

Lu Huaixi gave a light smile and glanced at her, her tone easy and offhand.

"That ice was your cousin-brother's. Not mine. But I'm glad you reminded me the household has its rules — now I have every reason to have it taken away without question. Otherwise, sleeping tonight with all that ice nearby — it would have been far too cold."

Hearing that it was Xie Yuanjing's doing, Mu Nianwei's expression froze. Her face twisted, her mouth opening and closing without producing a sound.

Lu Huaixi acted as though she hadn't noticed, and turned to leave.

"All right — I'm going in now. Next time you come, cousin, just walk right into the courtyard. No need to stand on ceremony the way you do with your cousin-brother."

—

By the time Xie Yuanjing returned to the estate, Yaoshu had just come back from delivering the gift and was still feeling a pang of regret on her young madam's behalf.

"Young Madam, did you really set that box of pills aside specially for the Old Madam? When Old Master Zeng finds out, he'll use it as an excuse to make you come plant herbs for him again as payment."

"As if I have the energy for that."

Lu Huaixi said it idly. "I just grabbed a random box of the old tonic pills — as long as they don't upset her stomach, that's enough. If I don't throw them something soon, that courtyard's maidservants are going to wear a path through my floor."

"That's true...... and that young cousin-in-law — she's really quite unpleasant to deal with."

"Don't worry. The maidservant will tell the Old Madam that I'm displeased. The Old Madam just received something from me — even if it's only for appearances, she'll step in and say something on my behalf this time."

While she was still speaking, someone came in from outside.

Xie Yuanjing had not yet changed out of his official robes, still dressed in deep crimson, looking cold and composed.

"Go ahead and play her — but taking my ice in the process?"

He walked straight toward her, an exasperated curve at the corner of his mouth. "Are you dealing with her, or dealing with me?"

chapters.title: Do You Want Me to Let Go?
chapters.content:
Lu Huaixi was seated in the chair. When Xie Yuanjing stopped before her, his presence seemed to fold around her entirely.

She tilted her head back to look up at him, and blinked at that rather close distance between them.

"I didn't do anything. She was the one who said the household has its rules, and that I didn't know how to manage the budget."

Lu Huaixi made no effort to hide it, neatly passing off the whole thing. "I'm just a new bride who came in from outside. Of course I have to follow the household's rules — otherwise Grandmother and Mother-in-law would be displeased with me."

"Is that so?"

Xie Yuanjing looked down at her. "From where I stand, you seem to have them both quite happy."

He gave a quiet laugh. "I thought I had a well-behaved little rabbit on my hands. Turns out she's been calculating things quite thoroughly all along."

"I have not. I'm nothing like you."

Lu Huaixi turned her head away after saying it. Xie Yuanjing gave her a look, then went inside to change his clothes.

"You've been waiting a long time for an opportunity like that, haven't you? If you're cold at night, just tell me directly next time."

"It wasn't like that. It was just convenient."

She watched his retreating figure and said:

"I'm fine under the blankets — I don't get that cold. But your mother said it's too early to be using ice, and my mother always said not to let yourself get chilled in the night. No one was looking out for you before, but I'm here now. I can't exactly watch you be so careless about it."

Xie Yuanjing's hands stilled. He turned his head and looked at her again. "Oh? You're going to manage me now?"

"Yes, a little."

Lu Huaixi nodded. "Is that not allowed?"

Silence from inside for quite some time. Then, after a long pause, came a quiet laugh. "It is."

Xie Yuanjing changed quickly. When he came back out, Lu Huaixi was still sitting where she had been, turning over the little trinkets she and Zhou Xianya had bought that day.

Watching her absorbed, head bent, Xie Yuanjing didn't say anything at first.

The quiet of the room gave him a feeling of steadiness he had never quite had before. He looked at the figure in the lamplight, his gaze resting on the soft downward sweep of her lashes — then drifting, without meaning to, a few inches further.

He had been watching for quite a while. Only when Lu Huaixi was on the verge of looking up did he finally speak.

"You had that much fun today — why didn't you have your friend stay for dinner?"

"We already ate out."

Lu Huaixi knew he meant Zhou Xianya, and answered simply. "And this isn't the Lu estate. It wouldn't have been right."

"What wouldn't be right about it?"

"It's just not quite appropriate." Lu Huaixi set down what she was holding. "It's not her own home — inviting someone here would make her uncomfortable."

The moment those words landed, Jingshuang, who had just come in to refill the tea, felt her heart give a small lurch.

She didn't dare raise her head, but borrowed the edge of her vision to steal a glance at the two of them.

Her young madam looked perfectly composed, her tone relaxed and easy. But the Young Master standing beside her — his expression was something else entirely.

She didn't look again. She lowered her head and retreated quickly.

The silence stretched for a long while before Xie Yuanjing spoke again.

"Come here."

He stood at the beaded curtain without moving. Lu Huaixi had no idea what he was about, but she set her things down and rose, puzzled.

"What is it?"

Xie Yuanjing didn't answer. Instead, when she drew near, he reached out and took her hand, leading her to the inner room and settling her onto the edge of the bed.

Then he leaned in slightly, one hand resting against her shoulder, bowing his head so that his face came to rest just beside her ear.

A very intimate gesture — one that made Lu Huaixi forget, quite suddenly, how to speak.

"The main bedroom is the bed you sleep in. Half the things in this room are things you've put there. Every manservant and maidservant in this courtyard follows your instructions before they follow mine. When you gave the word about that ice just now, not one of them came to ask me a single thing."

Xie Yuanjing spoke slowly, his low voice carrying the weight of some held-back feeling.

Lu Huaixi felt the warmth of his breath settle against her earlobe, then drift down the length of her neck — until her palms began to heat.

She instinctively tried to lean back, to put a little space between them. But the moment she moved, he noticed, and the hand on her shoulder pressed down with more intention.
